Job ID371908

Position Summary

SAP Operate Manager  

 

Are you an experienced, passionate pioneer in technology who wants to work in a collaborative environment? As an experienced SAP Operate Manager, you will have the ability to share new ideas and collaborate on projects as a consultant without the extensive demands of travel. Our Deloitte Enterprise Performance team is at the forefront of enterprise technology, working across finance, supply chain, and IT operations to deliver holistic performance improvement and digital transformation. Join our team of strategic advisers and architects, differentiated by our industry depth to collaborate with leading solution providers and leverage your experience in strategy, process design, technology enablement, and operational services to enable heart-of-the-business solutions. 

 

Recruiting for this role ends on 11/1/2026 

 

Work you'll do/Responsibilities    

We are looking for an experienced SAP Operate Manager to lead steady-state Application Managed Services (AMS) for our clients' SAP ECC, S/4HANA, and BTP environments. The role is based in the US Delivery Center (USDC). You will own service delivery against contracted SLAs and KPIs and lead a team of SAP functional and technical resources. You'll manage the full incident, problem, change, and enhancement lifecycle, and drive continuous improvement, automation, and clean-core adoption. The role combines operational leadership, technical oversight, client relationship management, and accountability for service quality, team capacity, and engagement economics. A strong candidate will have the following skills:

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
  • Ability to lead projects or workstreams
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Ability to mentor and provide clear guidance to others

The Team 

The Enterprise Operations as a Service Offering addresses our clients' needs for on-going operations of their technology and business process investments through multi-year contracts. We deliver continuous modernization, upgrades, and address incremental business changes as part of our engagements through our 5 key offerings: SAP Operations, Oracle Operations, IT Operations, Supply Chain Operations, Finance Operations.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own day-to-day delivery of SAP AMS across ECC, S/4HANA, and BTP, including incident, service request, problem, change, and minor enhancement management.
  • Make sure the team meets contracted SLAs and KPIs (response and resolution times, backlog aging, first-time-right, reopen rates, customer satisfaction), and take corrective action when performance trends off target.
  • Manage ticket inflow, prioritization, and backlog in ServiceNow (or a similar ITSM tool), balancing work across teams by priority and complexity.
  • Lead major incident management for P1/P2 issues: coordinate triage, client communication, and recovery, and complete post-incident reviews.
  • Run problem management with structured root-cause analysis, permanent fixes, and trend analysis to cut repeat incidents.
  • Oversee release and change management, including transport governance, CAB participation, regression testing, and coordinated production deployments.
  • Support periodic SAP maintenance activities such as Support Packs, Feature Pack Stacks (FPS), upgrades, and OSS Note implementations.
  • Provide technical direction to developers maintaining and enhancing custom objects (RICEFW) using ABAP Workbench, Eclipse ADT, SAP Business Application Studio (BAS), and BTP.
  • Make sure fixes and enhancements follow SAP extensibility guidelines (in-app vs. side-by-side, key-user vs. developer extensibility, released APIs, clean core), and lead efforts to reduce technical debt in the custom code landscape.
  • Review RAP artifacts (behavior definitions/implementations, validations, determinations, actions, draft handling, locking, authorizations), CDS views, and Fiori elements for quality, performance, and standards compliance.
  • Act as the primary operational contact for client IT and business stakeholders, managing expectations, escalations, and scope (in-scope support vs. project/enhancement work).
  • Lead service governance: weekly and monthly service reviews, SLA/KPI dashboards, monthly service reports, and quarterly business reviews.
  • Spot opportunities for enhancements, automation, and small projects, and help shape estimates, change requests, and contract renewals or extensions.
  • Capacity, Resource & Financial Management
  • Plan and manage team capacity and FTE allocation based on ticket volumes, complexity mix, and utilization; forecast resource needs and justify staffing to leadership and clients.
  • Run a continuous improvement program: ticket deflection, root-cause elimination, knowledge base growth, and process standardization.
  • Find and deliver automation opportunities (job monitoring, alerting, self-healing scripts, bots, GenAI-assisted triage) to lower effort and improve service quality.
  • Use SAP Cloud ALM (CALM), Solution Manager, and monitoring tools for proactive system health, job, and interface monitoring.
  • Lead knowledge transition from implementation teams or incumbent vendors into steady state, including hyper care exit criteria, run books, and SOPs.
  • Lead, mentor, and develop SAP developers and consultants with technical guidance, performance feedback, and career coaching.

Required Qualifications:

  • 10+ years in SAP Application Managed Services / production support, including at least one leadership role managing an AMS team against contracted SLAs.
  • Strong hands-on and supervisory background in SAP ABAP (Workbench, Eclipse ADT), BAS, and BTP across ECC and S/4HANA.
  • Working knowledge of ITIL processes (incident, problem, change, release, service request) and ITSM tools such as ServiceNow.
  • Experience with SLA/KPI reporting, service reviews, and client-facing governance.
  • Working knowledge of RAP, CDS, Fiori elements, and SAP extensibility/clean-core principles, enough to review and guide technical teams.
  • Experience with capacity planning, resource forecasting, and managing team utilization.
  • Strong root-cause analysis skills and experience leading major incident and hypercare support.
  • Familiarity with SAP Cloud ALM, Solution Manager, JIRA, HP ALM, and SharePoint for defect, test, and documentation management.
  • Ability to work flexible hours and support critical production issues when needed.
  • Bachelor's degree, preferably in Computer Science, Information Technology, Computer Engineering, or related IT discipline; or equivalent experience
  • Limited immigration sponsorship may be available
  • Ability to travel 10%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve

Preferred 

  • ITIL v4 Foundation certification.
  • SAP certifications (ABAP for S/4HANA, RAP, or BTP).
  • Experience moving AMS clients from ECC to S/4HANA or supporting post-go-live stabilization.
  • Experience building automation or GenAI/AI agent solutions for IT operations within SAP or related ecosystems.
  • Exposure to SAP BTP services such as Integration Suite, API Management, Event Mesh, or the ABAP Environment (Steampunk).
  • Experience working in a blended onshore/offshore delivery model.

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $130,000 to $175,000.

Requisition code: 371830

Job ID371830

Description & Requirements

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

Pogo has been the leader in online casual games since 1998. Featuring a growing library of 60+ titles spanning popular genres like Solitaire, Mahjong, Match 3, and more, Pogo exists to be the best destination for online casual games. We strive to produce high-quality HTML5-powered games with sophisticated metagames and social mechanics, all while working seamlessly across desktop, tablet and mobile web. Our fans and subscribers come to Pogo for fresh content, daily challenges, great events, new games, and a live service that delivers!

We are seeking an experienced Product Director to lead product strategy and live services for Pogo. In this key leadership role, you will report directly to the Studio General Manager and serve as the studio's strategic product anchor. You will partner with cross-functional leadership spanning Art, Design, Engineering, Production, Analytics, and Community to deliver a high-retention live service roadmap that delights players every day and meets core business outcomes. You will be responsible for gaining a deep understanding of Pogo players' needs and Pogo's key business objectives to plan, prioritize, and deliver the right content and feature improvements for our players.

Key responsibilities
Product Management

  • Drive Portfolio Roadmap: Own the holistic product vision and roadmap, orchestrating live operations, catalog health, platform enhancements, and game updates to maximize lifetime engagement.
  • Optimize an Established Ecosystem: Identify high-impact opportunities to evolve and grow an existing web platform, prioritizing scalable improvements over disruptive "0-to-1" rebuilds.
  • Drive Player & Market Intelligence: Develop a deep understanding of player motivations, competitive titles, and market trends to identify opportunities for improvement and growth.
  • Data-Informed Decision Making: Synthesize complex behavioral, telemetry, and transactional datasets into actionable product roadmaps, clear executive narratives, and measurable KPI benchmarks.

Financial Management

  • Deliver Business Commitments: Partner with Studio Leadership and Finance to forecast, establish, and meet quarterly and annual revenue, retention, and engagement goals.
  • Balance Multi-Stream Monetization: Optimize and grow our multi-tier business model across subscriptions, programmatic advertising, and live-event monetization without compromising player trust.

Leadership

  • Lead the Product Discipline: Mentor and empower the Product Management team, fostering a culture of curiosity, data rigor, player empathy, and operational excellence.
  • Foster Cross-Functional Alignment: Collaborate with other key studio leaders to support our vision, mission, and strategy; develop plans to achieve those goals
  • Cultivate Healthy Accountability: Promote a development culture of healthy accountability, maximizing potential and pride in accomplishments

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of product management experience in digital games or web/mobile consumer platforms
  • Demonstrated success optimizing, maintaining, and scaling an existing, live consumer business with an established, highly engaged audience (as opposed to strictly early-stage startup/pre-launch environments).
  • High emotional intelligence (EQ) with a track record of driving change collaboratively across tenured teams and deeply invested player communities.
  • A deep understanding of the casual games space, including player motivations, market trends, and key business drivers.
  • A genuine passion for creating fun, compelling, and engaging user experiences that resonate with everyday players.
  • Natural curiosity with a strong emphasis on continuous learning, adaptation, and iterative business growth.
  • Comfort and readiness to work effectively in a fully remote environment across multiple time zones.

Position Summary


Our Deloitte Cyber team understands the unique challenges and opportunities businesses face in cybersecurity. Join our team to deliver powerful solutions to help our clients navigate the ever-changing threat landscape. Through powerful solutions and managed services that simplify complexity, we enable our clients to operate with resilience, grow with confidence, and proactively manage to secure success.

Recruiting for this role ends on 05/31/2027.

Work you'll do

• Lead implementation planning, including cutover from legacy case management or SOAR tools, training direction and User Acceptance Testing preparation

• Oversee pre-sales through delivery handoff, including scoping, estimates, staffing plans, delivery approach, and transition-to-operations readiness

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

The team

Our Cyber Strategy & Transformation offering develops and transforms cyber programs in line with our client's strategic objectives, regulatory requirements, and risk appetite. We support capabilities across a broad suite of ServiceNow products across SecOps, Integrated Risk Management, and IT Asset Management. We are a growing team and are looking for our next generation of leaders to steer the direction of practice.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Front Desk Agent / Concierge, Hospitality / Tourism / Events
Job.JobDescription:
Shape the Next Generation of Vacations!
Welcome to Evermore Orlando Resort—the resort that's redefining the Orlando vacation experience. Just steps away from Walt Disney World®, Evermore stretches across 1,100 acres and offers a one-of-a-kind blend of spacious, upscale vacation homes, flats, and villas alongside the luxurious Conrad hotel. Our Team Members are true trailblazers, reimagining the vacation experience for each guest. Here, guests create their own adventure, enjoying the best of both worlds: the space and comforts of vacation home rentals combined with the amenities and services of a world-class resort.

Evermore is Orlando's ultimate game changer. In a city known for its theme parks and endless lines, Evermore is the paradise guests crave on their days between park visits. Imagine endless relaxation around Orlando's first and only beach paradise, Evermore Bay. Our stunning 8-acre crystal-clear lagoon is framed by zero-entry swim zones, beach bars, private cabanas, cozy firepits, and 20-acres of white sand. From beachside bars to a vibrant food hall and rooftop dining with views of the fireworks, we've crafted unforgettable experiences. Guests can challenge themselves on 2 Jack Nicklaus championship golf courses, enjoy water sports including kayaks and paddleboards, a family water slide, rope swing, and activities that fill their days including pickleball, bocce ball, and volleyball.

If you're excited to help guests reimagine the Orlando vacation, join us! Become part of an energetic team bringing Evermore Orlando Resort to life!

Key Responsibilities:

  • Welcome guests upon arrival, efficiently manage the arrival process, and provide them with relevant information about the resort's amenities and services. During departure, handle billing procedures accurately and bid farewell to departing guests
  • Respond promptly and courteously to guest inquiries, requests, and concerns. As a subject matter expert, offer helpful information about resort facilities, local attractions, and transportation options to enhance the guest's overall experience
  • Assist guests with making or modifying reservations, ensuring accurate room availability, rates, and preferences. Collaborate with the reservations and sales teams to maximize occupancy and revenue
  • Address guest complaints and concerns in a professional and empathetic manner. Strive to resolve issues promptly and escalate matters to supervisors or management when necessary
  • Provide anticipatory concierge services, including making dining reservations, arranging transportation, and organizing local activities based on guest preferences
  • Professionally manage incoming phone calls, chats, and emails, directing inquiries to the appropriate departments or providing accurate information as required
  • Engage in ongoing training and professional development to enhance knowledge of resort services, local attractions, and customer service skills
  • Handle cash, credit card transactions, and other forms of payment accurately and securely, following established resort procedures
  • Adhere to resort security and emergency procedures, ensuring a safe environment for guests and colleagues
  • Work alongside security at the resort entry gates to greet guests and process their arrival.
  • Assist guests to their units with luggage as needed upon request.

Education, Skills, and Experience:

  • High school diploma or equivalent is required.
  • Additional education in hospitality management or a related field is an advantage.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong customer service orientation with a friendly and helpful demeanor.
  • Attention to detail and accuracy in handling reservations and guest information.
  • Ability to handle multiple tasks and work efficiently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency in using resort management software and basic computer applications.
  • Prior experience in a customer service role, preferably in the hospitality industry, is an advantage.
  • Familiarity with resort reservation systems and front desk operations is beneficial.
  • Ability to work weekends, holidays, overtime, and rotating schedules.

    Physical Requirements:

    • Able to safely lift, pull and push up to 50 pounds
    • Able to stand, walk, stoop, kneel, bend, and reach periodically
    • Visually look at a computer for extended periods
    • Able to sit and use the computer for hours at a time
    • Subject to environmental conditions, work activities can occur inside and outside
    • Visually look at a computer for extended periods
    • Repetitive hand motions, such as typing

    Evermore Culture

    At Evermore, our purpose is Togetherness, and our vision is to make a more together world possible.

    Through relational wellness, we cultivate an inclusive, people-first culture where collaboration, trust, and respect empower every Team Member to thrive. Our Values guide how we think, make decisions, and show up for our guests, one another, and the moments that matter most. We are committed to acting with integrity, striving for the extraordinary, and recognizing that our greatest success comes when we succeed together.

    We offer our Team Members competitive pay, along with a range of benefits including FREE Life Insurance, FREE Short-Term Disability, FREE Long-Term Disability. Additionally, we provide affordable health benefits, including Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage for your dependents. Furthermore, we offer a 401K with employer match, a robust paid time off policy, parental and grandparent leave, as well as family and pet bereavement leave. We also have unique policies in support of our team and significant relationships in their lives.

Job.JobTitle: Seasonal Tax Delivery Manager, Individual Tax Services - Global Employer
Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

This is a seasonal opportunity expected for the Spring 2027 (January - April) or other mutually agreeable period. Extensions may be available upon mutual agreement. Remote opportunities available.

The role is designed for an experienced tax professional who can quickly assume responsibility for complex client deliverables, manage competing deadlines, and support high-quality outcomes during peak season.

Recruiting for this role will end on January 31, 2027.

Work you'll do

As a Deloitte Seasonal Tax Delivery Manager supporting Individual Tax Services – High Net Worth, you will:

  • Own delivery for assigned client engagements from planning through completion of seasonal deliverables.
  • Review complex individual and gift tax returns, workpapers, and related deliverables for accuracy and completeness.
  • Track filing, review, and client milestones; identify risks early and escalate blockers.
  • Resolve review notes and coordinate with specialists to meet agreed deadlines.
  • Maintain clear communication with clients, advisors, engagement leaders, and team members.
  • Manage team assignments, workload, and priorities during peak periods.
  • Provide focused coaching and real-time feedback to tax professionals supporting assigned work.
  • Monitor engagement scope, budgets, and open items, escalating issues that may affect delivery.
  • Prepare clear handoff documentation and status updates for any work continuing beyond the seasonal assignment.

A successful candidate will possess the following skills:

  • Completion of assigned tax returns and deliverables by agreed deadlines.
  • Timely resolution of review notes, client requests, and technical issues.
  • High-quality, well-documented work requiring minimal rework.
  • Early identification and escalation of delivery, staffing, or scope risks.
  • Consistent visibility into engagement status, workload, and open items.
  • Effective coordination across clients, advisors, specialists, and tax teams.

The Team

At Deloitte Tax LLP, our Individual Tax Services professionals advise high-net-worth individuals and families on complex tax compliance and planning matters. The practice supports clients with individual income tax considerations while building long-term relationships with clients and their trusted advisors. Learn more about Deloitte Tax Global Employer Services.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration or other relevant degree
  • 5+ years of experience in individual tax compliance and planning, with exposure to high-net-worth individuals and gifts
  • Strong technical knowledge of high-net-worth taxation, including experience reviewing complex individual and gift tax returns
  • Demonstrated ability to serve as a trusted client advisor, communicate complex tax matters clearly, and build relationships with high-net-worth clients and their advisors
  • Ability to ramp up quickly and contribute effectively in a seasonal, deadline-driven environment
  • Demonstrated ability to manage high-volume work while maintaining quality and attention to detail
  • Availability to support peak-season deadlines and changing priorities
  • Ability to travel up to 5%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future
  • One of the following active accreditations obtained:
    • Licensed CPA in state of practice/primary office if eligible to sit for the CPA
    • If not CPA eligible:
      • Licensed Attorney
      • Enrolled Agent

Preferred

  • Master's degree or equivalent in a related field.
  • Experience serving high-net-worth individuals or private clients.
  • Strong client communication and relationship-management skills.
  • Experience leading, coaching, and developing tax professionals.
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines while maintaining quality and attention to detail.
  • Proficiency with Excel and PowerPoint; experience with CCH tax technology or workflow tools is a plus.

Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

Join Deloitte Tax LLP's Global Employer Services practice as a Tax Manager, Equity Operations, where you will advise clients on how to optimize, redesign, build, and stand up effective stock administration functions, including operating models, governance, processes, controls, technology, data, integrations, service delivery, and readiness for major corporate events.

Recruiting for this role will end on May 31, 2027.

Work you'll do

As a Deloitte Tax Manager on the Equity & Incentives team, you will be responsible for:

  • Assessing current-state stock administration functions across people, process, technology, data, governance, controls, vendor models, and participant service.
  • Defining target-state operating models, including scope of services, organization design, governance, escalation paths, service levels, and stakeholder interactions.
  • Designing and improving end-to-end administration processes for grants, vesting, releases, exercises, purchases, cancellations, settlements, mobility, tax withholding, payroll reporting, reconciliations, and participant support.
  • Leading or supporting function stand-up, transition, and stabilization activities, including implementation planning, data conversion, knowledge transfer, cutover, post-go-live support, and readiness for major corporate events.
  • Advising on equity administration platforms, vendor strategy, integrations, data flows, operational risk, controls, and scalable delivery approaches for client environments.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
  • Ability to lead projects or workstreams
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Ability to mentor and provide clear guidance to others

The team

At Deloitte Tax LLP, our Global Employer Services Rewards professionals help clients design and manage compensation and rewards programs for their global workforce. The practice advises on rewards strategy, compensation structures, benchmarking, and related tax and regulatory considerations to support effective business and talent outcomes. Learn more about Deloitte Tax Global Employer Services.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Ability to perform job responsibilities within a hybrid work model that requires US Tax professionals to co-locate in person 2 – 3 days per week
  • Bachelor's degree in business, finance, accounting, human resources, information systems, or a related field
  • 5+ years of experience in stock plan administration, equity compensation operations, or stock administration advisory services
  • Experience in a corporate stock administration function, broker, recordkeeper, administrator, consulting organization, or professional services firm
  • Experience administering equity award lifecycles, including grants, vesting, releases, exercises, purchases, cancellations, settlements, withholding, and participant transactions
  • Experience designing or improving stock administration processes, controls, reconciliations, reporting, procedures, service delivery, or cross-functional issue resolution
  • Ability to travel up to 20%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
  • Limited immigration sponsorship may be available.
  • One of the following active accreditations:
    • Licensed Certified Public Accountant (CPA) in state of practice/primary office
    • If not CPA eligible:
      • Licensed Attorney
      • Enrolled Agent (EA)
      • Certified Executive Compensation Professional (CECP)
      • Certified Equity Professional (CEP)
      • Global Professional in Human Resources (GPHR)
      • Certified Employee Benefits Specialist (CEBS)
      • Certified Pension Consultant (CPC)
      • Certified Payroll Professional (CPP)
      • Project Management Professional (PMP)

Preferred:

  • Experience designing, building, transforming, or standing up a stock administration function or major component of one
  • Experience with Equity Edge Online, Morgan Stanley at Work Shareworks, Fidelity Stock Plan Services, or a comparable equity administration platform
  • Certified Equity Professional (CEP) credential or comparable equity compensation expertise
  • Experience supporting global equity plans, globally mobile employees, and coordination across multiple payrolls and jurisdictions
  • Experience in public company environments, initial public offering readiness, executive or insider processes, financial reporting support, or corporate transactions
  • Experience with operating model design, vendor selection, platform implementation, data conversion, testing, cutover, transition, or post-go-live stabilization

Job.JobTitle: Senior Manager, Operational Risk Management Liaison Team
Job.JobDescription:
Your opportunity


At Schwab, you're empowered to make an impact on your career. Here, innovative thought meets creative problem solving, helping us challenge the status quo and transform the finance industry together. We believe in the importance of in-office collaboration and fully intend for the selected candidate for this role to work on site in the specified location(s).

Enterprise and Operational Risk Management is part of Corporate Risk Management and helps strengthen enterprise and operational risk practices through independent oversight, consultation, and effective challenge. The Operational Risk Liaison Team provides risk intelligence that supports informed decisions and a strong risk environment.

As the primary Operational Risk Liaison for the Finance and Legal enterprises and Capital Stress Testing activities, you will provide enterprise-wide risk oversight, consultation, and effective challenge across first- and second-line teams that contribute to CST, working closely with Financial Risk Management, Model Risk Oversight, and the Treasury Capital Stress Testing team.. You will apply Risk Management, Risk Assessment, Analytical Thinking, and Decision Making to identify exposures, assess the CST control environment, and drive meaningful outcomes.

Success requires strong attention to detail, Stakeholder Management and Communication skills to influence without direct ownership, present well-supported assessments to leadership, and build alignment across Finance, Treasury, Financial Risk Management, Model Risk Oversight, and other partners. Your Collaboration and Adaptability will help the organization navigate evolving risks, competing priorities, and seasonal demands while strengthening risk-based decision-making.

  • Provide independent oversight, consultation, and effective challenge of business-led initiatives, including the evaluation of new instruments used in Finance ensuring operational risk considerations are appropriately identified, assessed, and addressed throughout implementation.
  • Provide effective challenge to CST process execution, governance documentation, controls, and cross-functional handoffs to identify and address operational risk exposures.
  • Assess CST-related issues, remediation activities, and emerging risk themes across Finance, Treasury, Financial Risk Management, Model Risk Oversight, and other contributing business teams.
  • Provide support and mentorship to business partners to ensure adherence to the Operational Risk framework elements and policy requirements.
  • Oversee and challenge the design, implementation, and maintenance of business processes and controls to manage relevant risks.
  • Oversee the identification and remediation of operational risk issues in accordance with framework requirements.
  • Analyze operational risk data to support risk identification, assessment, monitoring, and reporting activities.
  • Monitor and assess emerging risks, industry trends, and operational risk exposures related to Capital Stress Testing.

What you have


Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree
  • 7+ years of experience in risk management, governance, or a similar role
  • Experience in Risk Management and conducting Risk Assessments within banking, brokerage, or financial services
  • Analytical Thinking and Decision Making skills demonstrated through the evaluation of complex processes, controls, issues, and risk information
  • Communication skills, including the ability to present assessments and recommendations to leadership
  • Stakeholder Management and Collaboration skills, with the ability to build effective partnerships and influence outcomes without direct ownership
  • Ability to exercise independent judgment, solve complex problems, and bring projects and reporting to conclusion
  • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build effective relationships with business unit partners and risk management teams.
  • Experience with Capital Stress Testing, CCAR/DFAST-like processes, Treasury, or Finance is preferred
  • Familiarity with Risk and Control Self-Assessments, issues management, control testing, or model and process governance
  • Adaptability and Attention to Detail when navigating emerging risks, ambiguity, competing priorities, and seasonal workload demands
  • Executive Presence and Strategic Thinking when providing effective challenge and communicating risk-related recommendations

What's in it for you

At Schwab, you're empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

Police Department:

At the UCF Police Department, safety is our top priority. Our mission is to help ensure that students, faculty, staff, and visitors can both be safe and feel safe every day.


As a Police Dispatcher, you will serve as the vital first point of contact during emergencies, providing calm, professional support when it matters most. You will be the critical link between those in need and the police officers responding to help.


Through comprehensive training, you'll learn how to remain focused under pressure, gather essential information, and coordinate rapid emergency response efforts. Your ability to think quickly, communicate effectively, and stay composed can make a meaningful difference in reducing response times and helping save lives.


Whether you are starting your career in public safety or bringing valuable experience from another field, you'll join a dedicated team that values professionalism, teamwork, and service to others. If you're looking for a rewarding career where every shift presents an opportunity to make a positive impact, we invite you to become part of the UCF Police Department family.


The Opportunity:

Help Protect the UCF Community. Become a Police Dispatcher.


A Dispatcher II (911 Operator/Police Dispatcher) is a Public Safety Telecommunicator that is responsible for answering, processing, prioritizing, and dispatching incoming emergency and non-emergency calls for service using a computer-aided dispatching system. A Dispatcher is an essential part of the First Responders team that receives calls from the public concerning law enforcement, fire, or medical emergencies. They evaluate the situation and decide which service to utilize by relaying instructions, asking questions, and obtaining pertinent information.


Dispatcher will then notify officers of where to respond via radio while providing pertinent information about the call for service while entering data into the computer-aided dispatch system. This Dispatcher will handle and manage emergency situations, work within a fast-paced environment, and multitask. This position is highly rewarding by providing help to our citizens and visitors when they need help the most.


Responsibilities:

  • Receives and evaluates calls from the public requesting police assistance of both emergency and non-emergency natures. Operates Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) and Records Management systems to record and retrieve data relevant to requests for police and non-police service calls.
  • Operates digitally enhanced, encrypted, radio console to dispatch calls to public safety units, parking patrollers, and other auxiliary units.
  • Provides police and non-police units with necessary information to accomplish their tasks. Coordinates police information with other local law enforcement agencies.
  • Answers all in-coming calls on multiple lines, take messages and/or transfers calls appropriately; monitor and review email correspondence and reply as necessary.
  • Utilizes various criminal justice and public safety computer systems to validate driver's license records, vehicle registrations, stolen files, warrants, criminal histories and other files. Enters stolen property into the FCIC/NCIC computer system.
  • Access university computer system to verify student and staff information, parking services information and other related files.
  • Maintains various departmental databases utilized to provide information to department members.
  • Monitors campus wide critical alarm system equipment (security and fire).
  • Dispatches police and/or make appropriate notifications for proper disposition of all alarms received and/or reported in the emergency call center.
  • Monitors and operates the Emergency Alert and Mass Notification system.

Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma and 2+ years of relevant dispatch experience or completion of training and probation as a UCF Law Enforcement Dispatcher.

Must receive National Crime Information Center (NCIC)/Florida Crime Information Center (FCIC) certifications provided by UCF Police within six months of employment.

Successful completion of an appropriate 9-1-1 emergency dispatcher training that meets the requirements of current Department of Health Public Safety Telecommunicator course provided by UCF Police must be obtained within the first 6-months of employment. Certification must be maintained once complete.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Current Florida Department of Health 911 Public Safety Telecommunicator Certification.
  • Knowledge of jurisdiction geography, University geography, and associated landmarks.
  • Experience with multi-line telephone system, radio, and other computer equipment, and its operation.
  • Experience making decisions and functioning effectively in high stress, emergency situations.
  • Ability to organize, prioritize and reach closure on multi-functional tasks.
  • Able to maintain a positive, professional, and customer-focused approach to work.
  • Ability to respond to the public in a calm, effective manner.
  • Ability to type 30 wpm with minimal errors.

Health Assessment Required:

The UCF policy requires completion and passing of a physical exam for this position.


Additional Application Materials Required:

Candidates who complete the application, provide a cover letter and a resume will be afforded priority consideration.


Special Instructions to the Applicants:

Position requires a valid Class E driver's license. This position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.


Shifts include 7a-3p; 3p-11p & 11p-7a; employees shall be required to work different shift hours due to operational necessities, when deemed appropriate by UCF management. Must be able to work weekends and holidays.


This position may be eligible for a sign-on bonus in accordance with university guidelines.


All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.


This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.


UCF is seeking to fill multiple roles. Candidates for this job posting will be considered for additional Dispatcher II vacancies.

The Department of Chemistry (science.ucf.edu/chemistry) and the National Center for Forensic Science (NCFS, www.ncfs.ucf.edu) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invite applications for one full-time, 9-month, tenure-earning Assistant Professor in Forensic Toxicology. This is a joint position between the Chemistry Department and NCFS. This position is anticipated to begin in August 2027. Candidates hired at the assistant professor level are expected to develop externally funded, nationally competitive research programs. State-of-the art laboratory space and a competitive startup package can be expected. Successful candidates will contribute to teaching in both the undergraduate and graduate programs. The instructional duties and service assignments are in accordance with the department's current equitable workload policy.

The Department of Chemistry at UCF is fueling the STEM workforce of the future, preparing students through five broad areas of study, including: materials, biochemistry, environmental chemistry, forensic chemistry, and chemistry education research. Our faculty are actively engaged in cutting-edge, interdisciplinary research in collaboration with the National Center of Forensic Science, the Nanoscience and Technology Center, the College of Optics and Photonics, the College of Engineering and Computer Science, and the College of Community Innovation and Education. The department offers a range of academic programs, which include both B.A. and B.S. degrees in Chemistry and a B.S. in Forensic Science, as well as M.S. programs in Chemistry and Forensic Science, and a Ph.D. in Chemistry. Our B.S. Forensic Science degree is accredited by the Forensic Science Education Programs Accreditation Commission (FEPAC) and UCF is a member of The Consortium for Nuclear Forensics, one of only 16 universities in the nation. The National Center for Forensic Science at UCF, a State of Florida Type II Research Center, leverages the expertise of Chemistry faculty to provide relevant and responsive forensic science research and training and operational support to communities that rely on science to achieve justice.

The UCF College of Sciences (COS) is the largest college at the university and a powerhouse for the regional and national STEM workforce, spanning the natural, computational, and social sciences with centers, institutes, and initiatives that serve as hubs for research and innovation. Through sharing and applying knowledge, COS is cultivating pathways for students to solve our world's most pressing and complex problems. The mission of COS is to provide a world-class education in an environment where faculty, staff, and students thrive, research flourishes, and our community prospers. Several COS academic programs are nationally ranked by U.S. News and World Report, Princeton Review, and others.

Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The School of Global Health Management and Informatics (SGHMI) in the College of Health Profession and Sciences (CHPS) at the Univiersity of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for a 9-month, tenure-earning assistant professor or tenured associate professor for the Health Care Informatics programs. This positions is located at the UCF Downtown campus with an anticipated start date in August 2027. The successful candidate will perform research and teach face to face and full online undergraduate and graduate courses in the area of healthcare informatics, specifically related to artificial intelligence. UCF has world renowned infrastructure and support for online teaching.


The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in cutting edge AI technologies and their applications in healthcare. Candidates with a strong record of interdisciplinary scholarship and external grant funding for research are highly desirable.

They will join UCF's School of Global Health Management and Informatics (SGHMI), home to some of the nation's largest undergraduate and graduate programs in health services administration. The School offers a comprehensive portfolio of academic programs, including the Bachelor of Science in Health Services Administration (B.S. HSA), Master of Health Administration (MHA), Executive Master of Health Administration (eMHA), Master of Science in Healthcare Informatics (M.S. HCI), Bachelor of Science in Health Informatics and Information Management (B.S. HIIM), and the recently launched Bachelor of Science in Health Informatics (B.S. HI). Further expanding its academic offerings, SGHMI anticipates welcoming its first cohort of Master of Public Health (MPH) students in Fall 2027, creating additional opportunities for interdisciplinary education, research, and collaboration.

SGHMI is committed to academic excellence, with programs accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Management Education (CAHME) and the Commission on Accreditation for Health Informatics and Information Management Education (CAHIIM). The undergraduate Health Services Administration program is also certified by the Association of University Programs in Health Administration (AUPHA).

For more information about the school, visit https://healthprofessions.ucf.edu/hmi/.


Minimum Qualifications for Assistant Professor:

  • Doctoral degree in a health discipline e.g., health care informatics, biostatistics, public health, or health services research) or an information technology discipline (e.g., management information systems, applied science, computer science, computer engineering, or biomedical engineering) from an accredited institution.
  • Industry or academic experience in research related to artificial intelligence applications in health care by the start of the appointment.
  • ABD's will be considered if the degree is conferred before the date of hire.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop a research agenda that supports tenure and promotion, along with the potential to secure external funding.

Minimum Qualifications for Associate Professor:

  • Doctoral degree in a health discipline e.g., health care informatics, biostatistics, public health, or health services research) or an information technology discipline (e.g., management information systems, applied science, computer science, computer engineering, or biomedical engineering) from an accredited institution at the time of application.
  • Industry or academic experience in research related to artificial intelligence applications in health care by the start of the appointment.
  • To be eligible for appointment as a tenured associate professor upon hire, the selected candidate must have a demonstrated record of teaching, externally funded projects/research, and service commensurate with a tenured faculty appointment rank of associate professor.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Early, mid-stage, or established investigators with expertise in artificial intelligence application in health care provision, including large language models, biomedical data processing, and data analysis.
  • Strong background in health informatics, digital health, and emerging healthcare technologies, including clinical decision support, health data interoperability, Internet of Things (IoT), wearable technologies, and other innovative technologies applicable to healthcare delivery and population health.
  • Expertise in responsible and trustworthy AI, including explainable AI, algorithmic fairness and bias, privacy, security, model validation, AI governance in healthcare, and AI interoperability, is desirable.
  • Demonstrated success in publishing high-quality research articles in top-tier international and national refereed journals or those who have completed a post-doc with an associated record of publication in the preferred research areas.
  • Actively engaged with various health informatics societies such as AMIA and HIMSS.
  • Demonstrated experience collaborating with healthcare providers, health systems, government agencies, industry partners, or other healthcare organizations on interdisciplinary research, implementary, or externally funded projects is preferred.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • Curriculum vitae
  • A cover letter

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

JOB SUMMARY:

Provides complex planning and scheduling support to executive management in lead capacity of planning/scheduling responsibilities at the Portfolio, PMO, or land level development project assignments. Supports the project team with planning and schedule development on large multi-disciplined program(s)/project(s) throughout the entire project life cycle spectrum from concept development through turnkey completions, consistent with project needs and appropriate policies and procedures. Scope of planning and scheduling responsibilities include development/establishment of program/project schedules, show/ride concept development, show, ride, facility, area development designs, building construction, show/ride production, installation, and commissioning stages.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Prepares program project life cycle and project master schedules and statuses the project schedules utilizing Primavera software. Develops comprehensive plans and schedules from multiple discipline drawings and specifications. Prepares project plans and works with scoping/strategy documents to develop integrated project master schedules. Prepares schedule contract milestones for bid packages.
  • Provides project team with Schedule guidance during all phases of the project. Coordinates with estimating/finance teams to develop appropriate level of detail scope definition and durations for schedule activities to support project monitoring and project controls reporting needs. Coordinates with contractors, vendors, and responsible project team members to develop and integrate activity durations and logic sequences required to perform project work. Integrates project schedule input from all internal and external project organizations.
  • Leads planning and coordination meetings as required to support planning and monitoring functions. Collects/reports progress, evaluates progress variances, develops work-around plans, and coordinates resolution of variances. Conducts resource loading/resource analysis and develops and statuses earned value tracking tools and progress curves as required. Produces reports as required to support project team needs and executive management reporting. Frequently communicates, reports, and interacts with project and core team members including vendors and outside consultants on complex topics.
  • Implements highly effective project control tools and reports and provides insightful analysis that contributes to schedule certainty.
  • Understand and actively participate in Environmental, Health & Safety responsibilities by following established UDX policy, procedures, training and team member involvement activities. 
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS: 

  • Proven prior project controls leadership, supervisory experience preferred
  • Solid working knowledge of theme parks, show/ride product lines and design and construction.
  • 8+ years of primavera scheduling experience required
  • Possess strong understanding of design and construction progress measurement.
  • Working knowledge of architectural/engineering and show and ride design and production.
  • Must be a well-organized self-starter with strong communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Solid understanding of practical project controls applications and earned value measurement.
  • Ability to supervise staff, consultants, and suppliers including setting goals, prioritization of tasks, coordinating work, and managing time.
  • Strong meeting leadership, facilitation, and alignment skills
  • Strong communication, collaboration, technical writing, and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to successfully influence and lead a team.
  • Ability to appropriate delegate and coach/mentor talent.
  • Ability to successfully negotiate schedule changes with vendors and contractors.
  • Basic conflict resolution skills
  • Thorough knowledge of planning techniques

EDUCATION:

Bachelors degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management or an applicable field required. Advanced degrees preferred.

EXPERIENCE: 

9+ years engineering/construction planning and scheduling experience required. 8+ years theme park planning/coordination experience preferred; or equivalent combination of education and experience. 

Your talent, skills and experience will be rewarded with a competitive compensation package.

JOB SUMMARY:

The Director of Audience Science is a key leader within UDX Commercial Advanced Data Analytics, responsible for Audience Science across UDX destinations. The role leads a multidisciplinary team that develops audience strategies, segmentation, predictive models, experimentation, journey measurement, and decision-support capabilities.

The Director partners with Marketing, Digital, Product, Operations, Technology, Finance, and destination teams to translate guest and commercial data into measurable improvements in marketing performance, guest experience, and revenue. The role sets the team roadmap, develops talent, guides data and platform priorities, and ensures analytics capabilities are scalable, actionable, and embedded in business decisions.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Team Leadership and Operating Model
    • Set the team strategy, roadmap, priorities, and operating model in alignment with UDX commercial objectives.
    • Lead, coach, and develop a multidisciplinary analytics team while building succession and critical capabilities.
    • Manage the portfolio of recurring delivery, strategic initiatives, and emerging business needs.
    • Establish consistent standards for analytical quality, stakeholder engagement, and delivery.
    • Partner with senior leaders to prioritize investments in data, technology, and talent.
  • Audience Science and Personalization
    • Lead segmentation, predictive modeling, experimentation, audience strategy, and personalization across marketing and digital channels.
    • Guide the development and adoption of scalable customer and audience data, identity, activation, decisioning, and measurement capabilities.
  • Guest and Journey Analytics
    • Own journey analytics priorities and standards across UDX destinations.
    • Lead analyses that identify guest behavior, needs, friction, and opportunities across the end-to-end journey.
    • Integrate audience, behavioral, transactional, operational, and experience data to produce actionable insights.
    • Partner with Marketing, Digital, Product, Operations, and destination teams to translate findings into prioritized and testable improvements.
    • Establish impact tracking that connects journey improvements to guest, commercial, and operational outcomes.
  • Commercial Strategy and Measurement
    • Translate analytics into commercial decisions, measurable financial outcomes, and prioritized actions across UDX destinations.
    • Establish measurement frameworks and controlled testing that quantify marketing, guest, and commercial impact.
    • Provide executives and channel leaders with clear recommendations that improve performance and support a guest-centric approach.
  • Understand and actively participate in Environmental, Health & Safety responsibilities by following established UDX policy, procedures, training, and team member involvement activities.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or abilities (KSAs) required.

  • Demonstrated leadership of advanced analytics or data science teams, including talent development and operating-model design.
  • Expertise in segmentation, predictive modeling, experimentation, causal measurement, personalization, and journey analytics.
  • Experience developing audience and guest analytics strategies across marketing, digital, and destination touchpoints.
  • Ability to translate complex analyses into measurable guest, commercial, and operational outcomes.
  • Experience with customer and audience data platforms, identity and activation platforms, cloud data and analytics environments, visualization, experimentation, measurement, and decisioning technologies.
  • Experience partnering with Marketing, Digital, Product, Operations, Technology, Finance, and other cross-functional teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior executives and communicate complex findings through concise recommendations.
  • Strong program and product management skills with the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Strong guest and stakeholder focus with the ability to build effective working relationships.
  • Intellectual curiosity and a commitment to continuous learning.
  • Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
  • Consistent attendance is a job requirement.

EDUCATION:

  • Bachelors degree in data science, statistics, economics, computer science, marketing analytics, business, or a related quantitative field required; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • Masters or Ph.D. in a quantitative field preferred.

EXPERIENCE:

  • 10+ years of experience in advanced analytics, data science, marketing analytics, commercial analytics, or a related field, including experience with guest or customer data, measurement, and experimentation.
  • 5+ years of experience leading analytics or data science teams and developing technical talent.
  • Demonstrated record of building scalable analytics capabilities and translating insights into measurable business outcomes.
  • Experience partnering with senior leaders and cross-functional teams to deliver enterprise initiatives; experience applying AI and intelligent automation to analytics workflows is preferred.

Your talent, skills and experience will be rewarded with a competitive compensation package.

Job.JobTitle: Tax Manager, Global Employer Services - Individual Tax Services, High Net Worth
Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

Are you a tax professional who enjoys building trusted relationships with high-net-worth individuals, families, and their advisors? Do you bring strong experience in individual tax compliance and planning, including complex matters involving gifts, trusts, or wealth transfer? If so, this Tax Manager opportunity within Deloitte Tax may be a strong fit.

Recruiting for this role will end on May 31, 2027.

Work you'll do

As a Deloitte Tax Manager supporting our Individual Tax Services - High Net Worth group, you will:

  • Serve as a trusted advisor and primary point of contact for high-net-worth individuals and their advisors.
  • Lead tax compliance and advisory engagements involving complex individual income tax matters.
  • Review individual tax returns and related deliverables, identify issues, and coordinate with specialists when needed.
  • Build strong client relationships through clear, thoughtful communication and responsive service.
  • Translate complex tax matters into practical recommendations for clients and their advisors.
  • Lead and develop tax professionals by providing coaching, reviewing work, and coordinating assignments across multiple deadlines.
  • Manage engagement timelines, priorities, resources, and budgets to support high-quality client outcomes.
  • Collaborate with engagement leaders and other tax professionals to resolve issues, manage risks, and deliver a consistent client experience.

A successful candidate will possess the following skills:

  • Client service: Builds trusted relationships with high-net-worth clients and their advisors through responsive service, clear communication, and a strong understanding of client needs.
  • Communication: Explains complex tax matters in a clear, practical, and professional manner to clients, leadership, and team members.
  • Team management: Leads, coaches, and develops team members while creating a collaborative environment focused on accountability, quality, and growth.
  • Delivery leadership: Organizes priorities, manages competing deadlines, anticipates risks, and coordinates resources to deliver consistent, high-quality client outcomes.

The Team

At Deloitte Tax LLP, our Individual Tax Services professionals advise high-net-worth individuals and families on complex tax compliance and planning matters. The practice supports clients with individual income tax considerations while building long-term relationships with clients and their trusted advisors. Learn more about Deloitte Tax Global Employer Services.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration or other relevant degree
  • 5+ years of experience in individual tax compliance and planning, with exposure to high-net-worth individuals and gifts
  • Strong technical knowledge of high-net-worth taxation, including experience reviewing complex individual and gift tax returns
  • Demonstrated ability to serve as a trusted client advisor, communicate complex tax matters clearly, and build relationships with high-net-worth clients and their advisors
  • Experience leading the delivery of complex tax engagements, including coordinating teams, managing competing deadlines, reviewing work, and maintaining high-quality client outcomes
  • Ability to travel up to 5%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve
  • Limited immigration sponsorship may be available
  • One of the following active accreditations obtained:
    • Licensed CPA in state of practice/primary office if eligible to sit for the CPA
    • If not CPA eligible:
      • Licensed Attorney
      • Enrolled Agent

Preferred

  • Master's degree or equivalent in a related field.
  • Experience serving high-net-worth individuals or private clients.
  • Strong client communication and relationship-management skills.
  • Experience leading, coaching, and developing tax professionals.
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines while maintaining quality and attention to detail.
  • Proficiency with Excel and PowerPoint; experience with CCH tax technology or workflow tools is a plus.

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $105,375 to $215,375.


Deloitte is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities. If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the recruiting process, please direct your inquiries to the Global Call Center (GCC) at USTalentCICInbox@deloitte.com.

Recruiting tips

From developing a stand out resume to putting your best foot forward in the interview, we want you to feel prepared and confident as you explore opportunities at Deloitte. Check out recruiting tips from Deloitte recruiters.

Benefits

At Deloitte, we know that great people make a great organization. We value our people and offer employees a broad range of benefits. Learn more about what working at Deloitte can mean for you.

Our people and culture

Our inclusive culture empowers our people to be who they are, contribute their unique perspectives, and make a difference individually and collectively. It enables us to leverage different ways of thinking, ideas, and perspectives, and bring more creativity and innovation to help solve our clients' most complex challenges. This makes Deloitte one of the most rewarding places to work.

Our purpose

Deloitte's purpose is to make an impact that matters for our people, clients, and communities. At Deloitte, purpose is synonymous with how we work every day. It defines who we are. Our purpose comes through in our work with clients that enables impact and value in their organizations, as well as through our own investments, commitments, and actions across areas that help drive positive outcomes for our communities. Learn more.

Professional development

From entry-level employees to senior leaders, we believe there's always room to learn. We offer opportunities to build new skills, take on leadership opportunities and connect and grow through mentorship. From on-the-job learning experiences to formal development programs, our professionals have a variety of opportunities to continue to grow throughout their career.

As used in this posting, "Deloitte" means Deloitte Tax LLP, a subsidiary of Deloitte LLP. Please see https://www.deloitte.com/us/about for a detailed description of the legal structure of Deloitte LLP and its subsidiaries. Certain services may not be available to attest clients under the rules and regulations of public accounting.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or protected veteran status, or any other legally protected basis, in accordance with applicable law.

Qualified applicants with criminal histories, including arrest or conviction records, will be considered for employment in accordance with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, City of Los Angeles's Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, and the California Fair Chance Act. The Innovation and Entrepreneurship master of science degree program is designed for students interested in creating technology-based entrepreneurial projects and companies, as well as those who seek leadership roles in established companies with a goal of creating new visionary opportunities within those organizations. The program supports the goals and aspirations of traditional entrepreneurs, as well as “intrapreneurs” who will promote innovation and change within companies (or even “inventrepreneurs” who create new products for handoff to others). Whether innovating within companies or creating new business ventures powered by unique ideas, entrepreneurs understand that the only true constant is change – and that creativity and innovation are the key to sustainable and successful businesses.

***This position is part time working no more than 20 hours per week, online and must be resident in the state of Florida.***

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Create an environment of learning through effective teaching skills, maintain student-centered focus, and update curriculum to keep current and relevant to industry standards.
  • Utilize a variety of teaching strategies and encourage active learning.

Job.JobTitle: Delivery Consultant, Oracle HCM Technical Integrations
Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

Our Deloitte Human Capital team helps organizations create value through people performance. We work with clients to reimagine work, the workforce, and the workplace across the enterprise and to transform their HR functions with AI and emerging technology. With the rapid pace of change in today's world, you will help clients answer questions like: How do I access, develop, and motivate my workforce? What should my AI strategy be for the HR function? Do I have the right organization and culture to enable performance? Join our team to make work better for humans and humans better at work.

Work You'll Do

As a Delivery Consultant on the team, you will be responsible for:

  • Supporting the design, build, and delivery of technical integrations, data conversions, and/or reporting activities across Oracle Cloud HCM implementations
  • Assisting with the identification of cross-functional impacts across HR, security, reporting, and integrations, and escalating risks or issues as appropriate
  • Supporting integration design and execution across Oracle Cloud HCM and connected systems, including inbound/outbound interfaces, middleware coordination, data mapping, and end-to-end validation
  • Contributing to data conversion activities, including data extraction, cleansing, transformation, load preparation, reconciliation, and cutover support to enable accurate and complete migration from legacy systems
  • Supporting the reporting workstream by gathering reporting requirements, assisting in the development of operational and compliance reports, and helping validate data quality, usability, and stakeholder needs
  • Coordinating with cross-functional technical teams to track risks, dependencies, and issues across integrations, conversions, and reporting, while supporting testing, go-live, and post-production stabilization

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines

The Team

Deloitte's Government & Public Services (GPS) practice – our people, ideas, technology and outcomes – is designed for impact. Serving federal, state, & local government clients as well as public higher education institutions, our team of professionals brings fresh perspective to help clients anticipate disruption, reimagine the possible, and fulfill their mission promise.

Our HR Strategy & Technology offering develops leading global HR strategies and implements HR technologies that drive transformation, maximize the workforce experience, and sustain HR effectiveness and value while navigating a world of disruption.

This opportunity sits within our Deloitte Center model, which is dedicated to driving impactful business services. It leverages Deloitte's scale and talent, as well as a center delivery model to provide high-quality, cost-effective service with standardized processes and procedures to serve businesses across Deloitte.

The Deloitte Center Model has a small-business feel with a big-business impact. With the resources of Deloitte and a community feel, the center model provides high-quality services to our clients. Center professionals work out of one of our specific Deloitte locations, and each location presents dynamic career opportunities for professionals to focus on their work with nominal travel requirements.

Qualifications

Required:

  • 2+ years of experience delivering Oracle Cloud HCM technical solutions
  • 1+ years of experience with supporting or leading the integrations, conversions, and/or reporting for the full-life cycle implementation of Oracle Cloud HCM
  • Ability to obtain and maintain the required Public Trust clearance for this role
  • Bachelor's Degree
  • Center Location & Travel Requirements:
    • Hybrid Work Model: Operate under a hybrid system requiring residence within a commutable distance to one of the Center locations (Gilbert, Lake Mary, or Mechanicsburg)
    • Co-location Expectation: Spend up to 30% of working time co-located at an assigned office for orchestrated opportunities, including projects, practice sessions, training, and Moments That Matter at a Deloitte Center location, Geo-Hub location, approved site, or project location
    • Travel Requirement: Maximum of 10% overnight travel for client or project purposes
    • Relocation Requirement: If relocation is necessary, complete the move within 12 weeks from the start date to reside within a commutable distance
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future

Preferred:

  • Actively Oracle Cloud Implementation Professional certified
  • Experience with supporting or leading small functional teams in a hybrid delivery model
  • Experience with government/public sector projects

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $71,300 to $118,900.

You may also be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.

#GPSHC2026 #GPSOracle2026

Deloitte is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities. If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the recruiting process, please direct your inquiries to the Global Call Center (GCC) at USTalentCICInbox@deloitte.com.

Recruiting tips

From developing a stand out resume to putting your best foot forward in the interview, we want you to feel prepared and confident as you explore opportunities at Deloitte. Check out recruiting tips from Deloitte recruiters.

Benefits

At Deloitte, we know that great people make a great organization. We value our people and offer employees a broad range of benefits. Learn more about what working at Deloitte can mean for you.

Our people and culture

Our inclusive culture empowers our people to be who they are, contribute their unique perspectives, and make a difference individually and collectively. It enables us to leverage different ways of thinking, ideas, and perspectives, and bring more creativity and innovation to help solve our clients' most complex challenges. This makes Deloitte one of the most rewarding places to work.

Our purpose

Deloitte's purpose is to make an impact that matters for our people, clients, and communities. At Deloitte, purpose is synonymous with how we work every day. It defines who we are. Our purpose comes through in our work with clients that enables impact and value in their organizations, as well as through our own investments, commitments, and actions across areas that help drive positive outcomes for our communities. Learn more.

Professional development

From entry-level employees to senior leaders, we believe there's always room to learn. We offer opportunities to build new skills, take on leadership opportunities and connect and grow through mentorship. From on-the-job learning experiences to formal development programs, our professionals have a variety of opportunities to continue to grow throughout their career.

As used in this posting, "Deloitte" means Deloitte Consulting LLP, a subsidiary of Deloitte LLP. Please see https://www.deloitte.com/us/about for a detailed description of the legal structure of Deloitte LLP and its subsidiaries.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or protected veteran status, or any other legally protected basis, in accordance with applicable law.
