Advancement & Partnerships:

Join our dynamic and growing Advancement & Partnerships team as we work together to power partnerships and transform lives through philanthropy.

Together, we can unleash the potential of people and ideas to positively change the world. Your efforts on our team will help us to build the University for the Future.

The Opportunity:

Under the general leadership of the Senior Associate Vice President of Advancement & Partnerships and Co-Campaign Director (Sr. AVP) and in alignment with the strategic priorities of the Senior Vice President for Advancement & Partnerships (SVP), the Associate Vice President for Development (AVP) will provide leadership and operational oversight for a portfolio of Assistant Vice President, Executive Director of Development and Director of Development level fundraisers.

The Associate Vice President serves as a senior fundraising strategist and people leader responsible for advancing philanthropic results, strengthening fundraising operations, and supporting the successful execution of the university's comprehensive campaign.

Responsibilities:

Leadership and Oversight of Development Teams:

  • Provides strategic leadership and direct supervision for a group of Assistant Vice President, Executive Director of Development, and Director of Development level positions and other senior fundraising leaders responsible for major gift fundraising within assigned colleges and units.
  • Guides fundraising strategy, portfolio development, and prospect engagement to ensure teams are positioned to meet or exceed fundraising goals. Establishes expectations for performance, accountability, and collaboration across development teams while supporting consistent fundraising practices and processes across the division.
  • Works closely with development leaders to assess pipeline health, identify opportunities for growth, and remove barriers to fundraising success. Provides mentorship, coaching, and leadership development for senior fundraising staff to strengthen the division's overall fundraising capacity.
  • Supports the recruitment, onboarding, and development of development professionals in partnership with Advancement leadership and Human Resources Operations.

Fundraising Strategy and Principal Gift Engagement:

  • Maintains a select portfolio of select principal and major gift prospects to cultivate, solicit, and steward in partnership with college leadership and development officers.
  • Provides strategic counsel to development leaders on complex fundraising strategies, donor engagement plans, and principal gift opportunities. Works collaboratively with deans, faculty, and university leadership to identify philanthropic priorities and align donor interests with institutional needs.
  • Supports cross-unit fundraising strategies and collaborative gift opportunities that advance university-wide initiatives and campaign priorities.

Campaign and Strategic Initiative Leadership:

  • Supports the success of the campaign by ensuring that the units meet their benchmarks, have what they need to successfully do their jobs, are effectively coached, mentored, deans are engaged, fundraisers are working well with central fundraising services, etc.
  • Assists and supports with prospect strategies and fundraising goal development. They will support the units in achieving their campaign targets, provide guidance to enhance campaign participation and performance.
  • Works collaboratively with Advancement Operations, Prospect Development, and Communications teams to ensure fundraising strategies are informed by data, pipeline insights, and coordinated donor engagement.

Leadership Collaboration and Division Strategy:

  • Contributes to division-wide fundraising planning, goal setting, and strategic initiatives.
  • Collaborates with Advancement leaders to strengthen performance expectations, prospect management practices, and campaign strategies.
  • Provides insight and recommendations to senior leadership on emerging fundraising opportunities, staffing needs, and organizational priorities.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 12+ years of relevant experience with at least 5+ years of leadership experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

Preferred Qualifications:

We're looking for a dynamic fundraising leader who is passionate about the transformative power of higher education. The strongest candidates may also bring:

  • Master's degree in Higher Education, Business Administration, Communications, Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, or related field.
  • 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in higher education advancement, philanthropy, or complex nonprofit fundraising environments.
  • Demonstrated success leading large-scale major gift or principal gift fundraising efforts, including securing seven-figure philanthropic commitments.
  • Experience leading and developing senior fundraising professionals in a complex, matrixed organization.
  • Proven ability to build collaborative partnerships with executive leadership, deans, faculty, volunteers, and high-capacity donors.
  • Experience supporting a comprehensive fundraising campaign within a higher education or similarly complex organization.
  • Strong understanding of prospect strategy, portfolio management, donor pipeline development, and fundraising performance metrics.
  • Experience using fundraising and donor management systems such as Blackbaud CRM, Salesforce, or similar platforms to inform strategy and performance.
  • Demonstrated success managing cross-functional fundraising initiatives and collaborative donor strategies across multiple units or colleges.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and organizational change management skills with the ability to influence and drive results across teams.
  • Experience developing fundraising strategy informed by data analytics, campaign reporting, and pipeline insights.
  • Record of fostering a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing team culture.
  • Record of success in achieving fiscal year and campaign benchmarks.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated starting salary for a well-qualified candidate is $215,000 - $240,000. Advancement and Partnerships values the unique contributions that each team member brings to our division. The final determination of a successful candidate's starting salary will vary based on several factors, including education and relevant experience. The anticipated pay scale indicated for this position generally applies to candidates who meet the minimum requirements and several of the preferred qualifications outlined above. All offers are contingent on successful background and reference screens.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H 1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • Classification Title: Associate Vice President, Central Advancement

This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.

Are you ready to unleash YOUR potential?

As a next-generation public research university and Forbes-ranked top employer in Florida, we are a community of thinkers, doers, creators, innovators, healers, and leaders striving to create broader prosperity and help shape a better future. No matter what your role is, when you join Knight Nation, you'll play an integral role at one of the most impactful universities in the country. You'll be met with opportunities to connect and collaborate with talented faculty, staff, and students across 12 colleges and multiple campuses, engaging in impactful work that makes a positive difference. Job.JobTitle: Sports Director, Winter Park YMCA Family Center
Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

Under the direction of the Sports Operations Director, the Sports Director provides leadership and management of sports programming within the Family Center. The Sports Director manages member participation and retention through the development and execution of sports programs to achieve strategic goals and provide outstanding customer service to all members.

Our Culture

Our mission and core values are brought to life by our culture. In the Y, we strive to live our cause of strengthening communities with purpose and intentionality every day. We are welcoming: we are open to all. We are a place where you can belong and become. We are genuine: we value you and embrace your individuality. We are hopeful: we believe in you and your potential to become a catalyst in the world. We are nurturing: we support you in your journey to develop your full potential. We are determined: above all else, we are on a relentless quest to make our community stronger beginning with you. We are the Y.

Job Responsibilities

  • Implement youth and adult sports programs that promote retention of existing members and engagement of new members. Direct staff to support sports initiatives to achieve retention goals.
  • Analyze data, systems and processes to recognize growth and retention opportunities within the Sports department.
  • Ensure proper implementation of sports schedules and procedures to provide maximum opportunities for member/staff connections. Collaborate and work effectively with all departments to achieve desired results.
  • Identify and employ best practices in systems and technology to support effective management of the Sports department. Utilize available technology, reporting tools and data that enhance sports participation and member retention.
  • Establish systems for regularly scheduled gym and equipment inspections to ensure proper and efficient working order at all times. Coordinate and schedule equipment maintenance and repairs. Purchase equipment, parts and supplies approved by the purchase requisition process.
  • Monitor daily operations to adhere to all state, local and YMCA of Central Florida health and safety standards and policies. Ensure all staff are current with required certifications.
  • Create and implement sports programs with an effort to allow participants to continue along a succession plan from youth sports to adult sports participation.
  • Increase program and gym participation through product knowledge and interactions with existing and potential members. Collaborate with department leads to maximize enrollments in program registration and gym usage.
  • Plan and execute sports events at the Family Center. Promote the Family Center and the YMCA of Central Florida's special events among the members and community.
  • Establish and lead a volunteer Sports committee that assists in development and execution of membership retention efforts.
  • Recruit, select, develop and retain appropriate skill depth level for the department. Supervise department staff. Support training and career succession plan for staff team.
  • Ensure all staff are current with required certifications
  • Provide leadership through established performance goals and standards, regular assessment of staff performance including annual performance evaluations, and staff meetings.
  • Collaborate with the Executive Director to plan and manage the Sports budget. Control payroll and department purchasing costs within the budget and financial guidelines.
  • Identify and recruit active volunteers for the Family Center Annual Scholarship Campaign.
  • Provide leadership and understanding of the mission of the YMCA of Central Florida to staff and members. Promote and represent the mission and core values of the YMCA of Central Florida in the Family Center and its programs.
  • Report all accidents/incidents and follow risk procedures as outlined in YMCA of Central Florida policy.
  • Report all suspicions of child abuse to proper contacts as outlined in YMCA of Central Florida policy.
  • All other duties assigned by Management.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent in related field required; sports management, recreation management, physical education or related field of study preferred. Bachelor's degree preferred.
  • Minimum 1-3 years of previous supervisory and leadership experience in sports and/or customer service related filed preferred.
  • Within 60 days of hire, CPR/AED & First Aid certification

Work Environment & Physical Demands

  • Must be willing to work a flexible schedule, which may include weekends and holidays as needed.
  • Must be willing to work an on-call schedule rotation as required.
  • The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to loud.
  • The physical activities of this position include: stooping, kneeling, crouching, reaching, standing, walking, pushing, pulling, lifting, grasping, feeling, and repetitive motions. Talking is required for expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word. Hearing is required to perceive information at normal spoken word levels, with or without correction.
  • The employee must be able to perform medium work: exerting up to 50 to 100 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.
  • The employee is required to have close visual acuity, along with the visual acuity to determine the accuracy, neatness, and thoroughness of the work assigned or to make general observations of facilities or structures. The employee is required to have visual acuity to operate motor vehicles.
  • The employee is subject to both environmental conditions: activities occur inside and outside. The employee is subject to extreme heat: temperatures above 100 degrees for periods of more than one hour.
  • May be required to sit or stand for extended periods of time while demonstrating manual dexterity in order to accurately work on the phone, computer keyboard, and other equipment.

Disclaimers

  • Must complete a successful employment verification and background screening, which includes a DCF Level 2 Background Check (Additional information on Level 2 Background through Clearinghouse can be found here: https://info.flclearinghouse.com/)
  • All of the above duties and responsibilities are essential job functions subject to reasonable accommodation. The YMCA promotes an equal employment opportunity work place which includes reasonable accommodation of otherwise qualified disabled applicants and employees. Please see your manager should you have any questions about this policy or these job duties.
  • This job description may not be all-inclusive and employees are expected to perform all other duties as assigned and directed by management. Job descriptions and duties may be modified when deemed appropriate by management.

JOB SUMMARY:

Manages Controls engineering efforts associated with safety compliance, improved ride reliability and enhanced show quality for all of the high technology ride and show attractions at Universal Orlando Resort. The manager will also assist the Vice President in maintaining cost controls within Engineerings assigned budget. Work with the attractions to identify, define, and prioritize capital issues to realize optimum cost-of-ownership of Universal Orlandos assets in Rides and Shows.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Manage and lead the Controls Engineering Department. Support the overall goals and priorities of the department to achieve the highest standards of safety and reliability. Inspire customer service attitude and instill a tradition of continuous process improvement throughout the team. Emphasize reduced cost-of-ownership of the Rides and Attractions through superior engineering and cost savings through improvements in preventative maintenance effectiveness and cost avoidance through proactive measures to reduce equipment failures and collateral damage.
  • Ensure that Controls reengineering tasks for the Rides and Attractions are performed to the highest standards of safety, reliability and quality. Ensure compliance with al applicable codes, regulations and standards including: AISC, ASME, ASTM, ANSI, AWS, JIC, NEC and OSHA among others. Ensure that downtime efforts are kept to a minimum through appropriate partnership with tech services, focusing on preventive maintenance.
  • Serve as Safety Control System expert to maintain configuration management of hardware and software documentation in accordance with Engineering guidelines for proper archiving and security. Prepare Ride control system documentation as required including ensuring all configurations files are in Asset Centre, etc. Prepare comprehensive Engineering reports showing technical analysis, design solutions and learned best practices. Conduct technical reliability evaluations of Engineering design concepts and design constructs. Develop risk analysis studies of new designs to improve ride reliability and maintainability.
  • Manage staff, including selection, hiring, induction, training, performance appraisal and IDP to ensure overall increase in knowledge, experience, responsibility and individual accountabilities Lead, motivate and inspire the Engineering Team by providing design reviews, staff meetings, stimulating culture and challenging environment that recognizes achievement, promotes effective communications and develops individuals to achieve their maximum level of performance and ensure a best in class Engineering Department. Manage Rockwell Assurance partners, and Obsolescence initiatives.
  • Coordinate and facilitate inter and intra-department partners and external resources including: Attraction maintenance group(s), Document Control, Environmental Health and Safety, Facilities, Finance, Human Resources, Landscape and Water Quality, Operations, Outside Vendors, Quality Assurance, Security, and Sustaining Engineering. Maintain, and encourage within subordinates, close and friendly working relationships; model by example.
  • Manage spending within assigned budget guidelines and minimize overtime worked. Assist in identifying and developing detailed budget plans for tasks and projects that reduce cost of ownership of the attractions.
  • Understands and actively participates in Environmental, Health & Safety responsibilities by following established UO policy, procedures, training and team member involvement activities.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

EDUCATION:

  • Bachelors Degree from a four-year college or university in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology or related fields is required
  • Masters Degree from an accredited college or university in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology or related fields is preferred

EXPERIENCE:

  • 10+ Years: Experience in an Engineering environment focuses primarily on control and automation systems, preferably in a theme park environment; interacting with other Engineering and Maintenance Department disciplines
  • Experience with:
    • Allen-Bradley PLC based control systems
    • AC and DC motors and motor control systems
    • Motion control systems
    • Show and animation control systems
  • Proficiency with personal computers using Win95, word processing and spreadsheets
  • Proficiency with complex diagnostic test equipment, proficiency in control systems drawings and technical documents.
  • Cognizance in ASTM regulations applying to theme parks, and the NEC are also required.
  • 8+ years project management functions especially in the area of technical compliance, scheduling and budgeting; performing technical support functions in regards to control systems, motor and motion control systems

AND

  • 10+ years demonstrated experience in electrical engineering, control system design and installation utilizing PLCs, ladder logic, variable frequency drives and servo control systems, process and/or machine safety, field experience with Theme Park technical environment and process control fault analysis/isolation experience required
  • Equivalent combination of education and experience

CERTIFICATIONS, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS:

  • PLC controls programming, maintenance, and troubleshooting; required
  • AC/DC Drives (motor controls) Configuration, maintenance, and troubleshooting; required
  • Cisco networking and wireless network certifications; preferred

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

  • Strong analytical skills to perform engineering calculations for design, analysis, test and implementation of electrical and control systems.
  • High Level of knowledge and experience in the design of safety critical systems, ISO 13849-1, ISO 13849-2, ISO12100 standards, IEC60204-1, IEC62061, PL safety levels, and UL 508A, NEC, ASTM, ASTM F24 Standards and UOs Safety Standards.
  • A strong background in servo controls as applied for hydraulic, pneumatic, and electromotive motion control systems is required.
  • High Level of knowledge of Allen Bradley PLC Systems, "C", Visual Basic, and other software platforms. Experience utilizing PLC-5, SLC-500, ControlLogix, CompactLogix, PanelBuilder 1400E, PanelBuilder32, RSView 32, RSLinx, RSLogix (5 thru 5000), RSNetworx, Allen-Bradley PLC, and AC/DC motor control systems.
  • Ability to perform engineering calculations commensurate with Baccalaureate training in electrical, electronic and software engineering.
  • Experience with generation of control system specifications, acceptance test procedures, technical compliance, system risk assessments and failure analysis.
  • Proven application experience utilizing the following products and networks. Anitech, Gilderfluke show system controllers, 1305, 1336, 750 series AB variable frequency drives, Data Highway Plus, Remote I/O, ControlNet, DeviceNet, Ethernet, DMX and SMPTE.

Your talent, skills and experience will be rewarded with a competitive compensation package.

Serves as a liaison with other T&C departments including Talent Acquisition, Talent Development, Organizational Development, Payroll, Benefits, Team Member Services, Compensation and Open Door to manage and resolve issues as well as assist with T&C process coordination. Represents self as face of T&C to Team Members in operational areas.

On-Site Opportunity. Experienced HR professional with employee relations/investigations experienced in a high-volume operational setting highly desired.

  • Consults with managers and supervisors regarding Team Member discipline and performance issues. Investigates workplace situations, including claims of harassment, discrimination, and policy violations. Supports decision making related to terminations and other forms of discipline. Ensures that corrective Team Member coaching and counseling are handled in a fair and consistent manner.
  • Provides support to Team Members by interacting and communicating with guests and Team Members in the parks, visiting break rooms and Lead offices to promote positive relations and seek out potential issues.
  • Supports the process involved in reviewing Performance Reviews, Team Member Counseling, and Performance plans. Ensures that any written communication directed to Team Members is legal, fair, consistent, in line with Universal Orlandos values, and follows the progressive discipline policy. Provides input and drives dialogue regarding Team Member Reasonable Accommodation requests/decisions.

This includes but is not limited to: Wardrobe Home Care program, Open Door Plus Appeals, attending EIL, Town Hall events, TSAT meetings, HR Roundtable presentations, Peer Review preparation, Position Management reviews, work authorization expiration notifications, No Pay Report follow-up, Average Hours report, job descriptions, , talent review, staffing assistance for job fairs, and XTRAS initiatives.

  • Provides advice and consultation for front-line hourly Team Members regarding benefits, payroll questions, policy interpretations, and EAP issues. Provides direction for internal transfer and career path direction including on-boarding plans, Intern programs, seasonal supervisor offers, and related follow-up paperwork.
  • Understand and actively participate in Environmental, Health & Safety responsibilities by following established UDX policy, procedures, training, and team member involvement activities.

  • Strong communication skills, both verbal and written.
  • Solid organizational skills, ability to handle multiple priorities.
  • Ability to flex & adapt in a fast-paced, constantly changing environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver high quality HR services.
  • Ability to objectively coach Supervisors/Managers and Team Members through difficult and emotional issues.
  • Ability to research and analyze various types of data and information.
  • Independent, self-starter, requiring minimal day-to-day task supervision.
  • Professional, confident demeanor.
  • Base knowledge of company policies & practice.
  • Thorough knowledge of MS Excel, Word and PowerPoint, experience with an HRIS (i.e., SAP) preferred.
  • Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
  • Consistent attendance is a job requirement.

EDUCATION:

  • Bachelors degree in Human Resources, Industrial Relations, Business Management, or related field required.

EXPERIENCE:

  • 2+ years Human Resources experience in a large-scale fast paced HR environment preferred; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Working knowledge of employee relations, staffing and payroll required.

Position Summary

Our Deloitte Cyber practice helps organizations address complex cybersecurity challenges across identity, access, and cloud transformation. As part of this team, you will help clients strengthen the security, resilience, and performance of their Microsoft identity environments, including Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID. This role offers the opportunity to lead large-scale identity initiatives, deliver practical risk-based solutions, and support clients as they modernize critical infrastructure.

Recruiting for this role ends on 4/01/2027.

Work you'll do

As an Engineering Manager II on the Deloitte Cyber team, you will be responsible for:

  • Assessing Microsoft Entra ID and Active Directory environments and developing recommendations to improve security, configuration, and operational health
  • Leading the architecture, design, and implementation of Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID deployments, migrations, upgrades, and consolidation efforts
  • Supporting identity modernization activities, including single sign-on, multifactor authentication, conditional access, identity provider migrations, and application integrations
  • Performing health checks, security assessments, recovery planning, and remediation activities across Active Directory services, domain environments, and supporting infrastructure
  • Delivering client-facing identity engagements across assessment, design, implementation, and post-implementation phases, while contributing technical insight to Deloitte eminence efforts

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team

  • Demonstrate advanced understanding of business processes, internal control risk management, IT controls and related standards
  • Responsible to install, integrate, configure, and deploy Saviynt.
  • Understand complex business and information technology management processes. Execute advanced services and supervise staff in delivering basic services.
  • Communicate to clients and partners aspects of both the product and the implementation at the technical and functional level appropriate for the situation.

  • Identity Management familiarity in one or more of the following areas:
    • Identity Governance and Administration (Lifecycle Management and Provisioning)

You will be responsible for individually delivering high quality products within due timelines. Need-basis you will be mentoring and/or directing junior team members/liaising with onsite/offshore teams to understand the functional requirements.

Support the implementation, administration, and ongoing operations of Identity Governance and Administration solutions, with a primary focus on SailPoint Identity Security Cloud (ISC). This role supports application and source onboarding, identity lifecycle and access administration, issue resolution, documentation, and platform operations across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments. The role works with senior team members, engineers, and stakeholders to help strengthen identity governance and operational efficiency.

Work you'll do

As a Security Engineer I on the Cyber Identity team, you will be responsible for:

  • Support implementation, administration, and daily operations of SailPoint ISC solutions
  • Assist with onboarding sources, applications, identities, and platforms into SailPoint ISC
  • Support source and platform administration, identity aggregation and correlation, access request, certification, and provisioning activities across Windows, Unix, and Linux environments
  • Perform issue triage, maintenance support, testing, validation, and documentation activities
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams on integrations, automation, and process standardization

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships

  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Ability to provide clear guidance to others

The team

The Cyber Identity team helps organizations govern identities, manage access lifecycles, and improve access controls across enterprise environments. The team supports SailPoint ISC implementations and operations across infrastructure, cloud, and application platforms. Team members work with internal and client stakeholders to support onboarding, administration, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in cybersecurity, computer science, information systems, engineering, business, or equivalent experience
  • 0–2 years of experience in IGA, SailPoint, cybersecurity, IAM, infrastructure support, systems administration, or a related technology role.
  • Experience with Windows, Linux, or Unix administration
  • Experience with enterprise infrastructure components, such as Active Directory, Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP), servers, databases, or HR and SaaS applications
  • Experience documenting procedures, runbooks, test results, or support activities

  • SailPoint Identity Security Cloud certification, or completion of SailPoint University training
  • Experience supporting account onboarding, access administration, or identity lifecycle management activities
  • Exposure to Windows, Linux, or Unix administration in an academic, lab, or professional setting

Requisition code: 373283

Job ID373283

Position Summary

Our Deloitte Cyber team understands the unique challenges and opportunities businesses face in cybersecurity. Join our team to deliver powerful solutions to help our clients navigate the ever-changing threat landscape. Through powerful solutions and managed services that simplify complexity, we enable our clients to operate with resilience, grow with confidence, and proactively manage to secure success.

Recruiting for this role ends on 4/01/2027.

Work you'll do

As a Engineering Manager II on the Deloitte Cyber team, you will be responsible for:

  • Leading Active Directory and identity infrastructure engagements across assessment, design, migration, implementation, stabilization, and post-implementation phases.
  • Performing and overseeing Active Directory assessments covering domain and forest architecture, domain controllers, Sites and Services, Domain Name System (DNS), Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP), replication, trusts, Group Policy, privileged groups, service accounts, authentication protocols, and administrative processes.
  • Designing and implementing Active Directory security and hardening improvements, including administrative tiering, role-based access controls, service account management, Group Policy controls, and identity threat detection and recovery capabilities.
  • Architecting and supporting enterprise Active Directory environments, including hybrid identity integrations with Microsoft Entra ID, federation, synchronization services, and application dependencies.
  • Leading or supporting domain and forest migrations, separations, and consolidations, including discovery, dependency analysis, cutover planning, validation, rollback, and post-migration stabilization.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
  • Ability to lead projects or workstreams
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Ability to provide clear guidance to others

The team

Deloitte Cyber's Digital Trust & Privacy practice helps organizations build and sustain confidence in their digital products, platforms, services, data practices, and customer experiences. Our work brings together digital trust, online protection, privacy, AI governance, identity, data protection, cybersecurity, and regulatory compliance capabilities.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Security, Engineering, Information Technology, another technical field.
  • 6+ years of experience in technical consulting, enterprise infrastructure, identity security, or Active Directory engineering.
  • 6+ years of hands-on experience designing, securing, assessing, migrating, or operating Microsoft Active Directory environments.
  • Experience with enterprise Active Directory services, including domain and forest architecture, domain controllers and replication, DNS, DHCP, Sites and Services, Group Policy, trusts, service accounts, Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP), and domain or forest recovery.
  • Experience leading or supporting Active Directory domain or forest migrations, separations, or consolidations.
  • Experience with migration tooling such as Quest On Demand Migration (ODM) or Semperis migration capabilities.
  • Experience with identity threat detection, identity resilience, cyber recovery, or recovery validation tooling such as Semperis, Rubrik, or Microsoft Defender for Identity.
  • Ability to travel up to 50%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
  • Limited immigration sponsorship may be available.

Preferred:

  • Advanced degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Engineering, or another technical field.
  • Experience with Active Directory security assessments, attack-path analysis, domain hardening, and privileged access management.
  • Experience with enterprise identity security architectures, including Enhanced Security Administrative Environment (ESAE), tiered administration, administrative forests, or privileged access workstations.
  • Experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, carve-outs, spin-offs, or enterprise reorganizations involving Active Directory environments.
  • Experience with Microsoft Entra ID, federation, synchronization, multifactor authentication (MFA), single sign-on (SSO), or hybrid identity architectures.
  • Certifications such as Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certificate of Cloud Security Knowledge (CCSK), Microsoft SC-300, or Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA).

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $134,500 to $265,100.

Description & Requirements

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

Frostbite is EA's proprietary game engine, powering many of our leading titles across EA SPORTS, Battlefield, and more. We develop shared tools and technologies that connect and empower creators throughout EA. On Frostbite, you'll collaborate with accomplished teams and contribute to the foundation that enables the creation of immersive, high-quality games for players worldwide.

By joining us, you'll be at the forefront of game engine development. You will collaborate with a passionate team to push the boundaries of interactive realism and immersive gameplay, helping us shape the future of gaming technology and leave a lasting mark on the next generation of games.

Our Animation team oversees the core platform that animation technologies across AAA games are built upon. As part of our team, you will handle a variety of rewarding engineering challenges—from improving user workflows for content creators to optimizing real-time runtime performance. As a Senior Software Engineer in the Animation team, you will report to the Development Director in Animation. You'll work on core animation systems that run in-game, as well as the tools and workflows used by content creators to build and author animation data.

This role is Hybrid remote/in-office.

You Will:

  • Build performant systems and features across our runtime animation engine (C++) and content creator tools (C#).
  • Take ownership of animation features from technical design through to production, testing, and multi-platform support.
  • Improve tool and game runtime performance.
  • Partner with animators, technical artists, and game development teams to turn creative concepts into playable features.
  • Participate in design and code reviews, collaborating with the team to share knowledge and keep our codebase reliable and easy to work in.
  • Mentor junior engineers on the team to support their technical growth.

Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of professional software development experience
  • Strong professional programming skills to improve and debug C++ and C# code
  • Experience working with 3D math, including transforms, rotations, and coordinate systems
  • Experience in game engine development
  • Performance and memory profiling
  • Experience with concurrent programming models
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

Bonus Experience:

  • Experience in animation state machines or real-time simulation
  • Experience with WPF / desktop UI development for asset pipelines and editor tools
  • Experience targeting console platforms (PlayStation, Xbox)

Job.JobTitle: Financial Management Lead Specialized Finance Solutions Delivery Senior Consultant
Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

Our Deloitte Finance Transformation team practices to help chief financial officers, controllers, and finance teams define and execute their finance and global business services agendas and strategies. You will work with leading-class teams and solutions, helping clients navigate challenging environments, market uncertainty, technology development, and regulatory considerations to unlock value. Your work may span strategy, operations, process design, and technology as we partner with clients to transform finance.

Work You'll Do

As a Delivery Senior Consultant, Specialized Finance Solutions on the Specialized Finance Solutions team, you will be responsible for:

  • Support U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) accounting operations involving property, plant, and equipment (PP&E) and leases.
  • Support accounts payable, accounts receivable, reimbursable agreements, and Intragovernmental Payment and Collection (IPAC) transactions.
  • Prepare and support the review of monthly financial reporting deliverables.
  • Lead assigned accounting tasks, track deliverables, and communicate progress and issues to client and engagement team stakeholders.
  • Maintain accounting documentation and data needed to support timely monthly reporting.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product

The Team

Deloitte's Government & Public Services (GPS) practice – our people, ideas, technology and outcomes – is designed for impact. Serving federal, state, & local government clients as well as public higher education institutions, our team of professionals brings fresh perspective to help clients anticipate disruption, reimagine the possible, and fulfill their mission promise.

Our Controllership and Treasury Transformation offering modernizes the finance function to support the evolving business objectives of the organization. We work with the CFO, CAO, controller, and treasurer to develop an efficient, high quality, data-driven, tech-enabled controllership and treasury function that empowers our clients to drive more value to their business partners and to their investors.

This opportunity sits within our Deloitte US Delivery Center model, which is dedicated to driving impactful business services. It leverages Deloitte's scale and talent, as well as a center delivery model to provide high-quality, cost-effective service with standardized processes and procedures to service businesses across Deloitte.

The Deloitte US Delivery Center has a small-business feel with a big-business impact. With the resources of Deloitte and a community feel, the delivery center model provides high-quality services to our clients. USDC professionals work out of one of our specific delivery center locations, and each location presents dynamic career opportunities for professionals to focus on their work with nominal travel requirements.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain the required Public Trust clearance for this role
  • 2+ years of experience supporting accounting operations involving one or more of the following: property, plant, and equipment; leases; accounts payable; accounts receivable; reimbursable agreements; or intergovernmental transactions.
  • 2+ years of experience preparing monthly financial reports.
  • You must reside within a commutable distance of your assigned office with the ability to commute daily, if required, without the need for overnight accommodations.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.
  • Delivery Center Location & Travel Requirements:
    • Hybrid Work Model: Operate under a hybrid system requiring residence within a commutable distance to one of the US Delivery Center locations (Gilbert, Lake Mary, or Mechanicsburg) or Geo-Hub locations (Atlanta, Charlotte, Dallas, Houston, and Philadelphia)
    • Co-location Expectation: Spend up to 30% of working time co-located at an assigned office for orchestrated opportunities, including projects, practice sessions, training, and Moments That Matter at a Deloitte Delivery Center location, Geo-Hub location, approved site, or project location
    • Travel Requirement: Maximum of 10% overnight travel for client or project purposes
    • Relocation Requirement: If relocation is necessary, complete the move within 12 weeks from the start date to reside within a commutable distance
Preferred:
    • Experience working in SAP (Systems, Applications, and Products in Data Processing).

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $91,100 to $151,800.

You may also be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.

Job.JobDescription:

The Deloitte Accounting & Reporting Technology team works closely with purpose-built automation technologies in the market to help our clients improve accounting processes, build / configure accounting automation solutions, and develop governance/controls around these tools.   • Lead the coordination and execution of Accounting & Reporting Technology strategic initiatives
  • Lead client pursuits and engagement delivery relating to Accounting & Reporting Technology

  • Ability to meet deadlines

  • 5+ years of related work experience

  • Experience in managing and supervising teams in executing all phases of the technology life cycle, based on proven project management and testing methodologies
  • Prior experience working with and managing data sets as well as integrations between systems
  • You should reside within a commutable distance of your assigned office with the ability to commute daily, if required.

Position Summary

The Team

ConvergeCONSUMER™ is a product-driven business that combines differentiated consumer insights with robust prediction and optimization capabilities to help consumer-focused businesses improve decision-making and deliver personalized experiences to drive growth, consumer loyalty, and profitability.   • Manage multiple workstreams in a fast-paced, dynamic environment while maintaining high standards of quality and attention to detail

The successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Strong analytical mindset, able to interpret data, identify trends, and translate findings into clear, business-oriented narratives that support client decision-making
  • Comfortable partnering across cross-functional teams — product, engineering, and business stakeholders — to shape and deliver client-facing solutions
  • Excellent written and verbal communicator, skilled at developing client-ready presentations and solution documentation
  • Highly organized with strong attention to detail, able to manage multiple workstreams in fast-paced, ambiguous environments
  • Curious and adaptable, connecting technical capabilities to client needs to drive adoption of innovative solutions
  • Comfortable working directly within distributor and field environments, not just from behind a desk

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Analytics, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of experience in analytics, product implementation, solution delivery, or consulting within technology-enabled or data-driven organizations
  • Experience supporting client engagements or product delivery within wholesale distribution, retail, or related supply chain-driven industries
  • Ability to travel 0-25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

As a Senior Product Forward Deployed Engineer (pFDE) on ConvergeCONSUMER, you'll operate at the intersection of sales and delivery — building trust with senior client stakeholders, leading hands-on implementation teams, and feeding what you learn in the field back into our product roadmap.

As the Senior Product Forward Deployed Engineer (pFDE), you will:

  • Own end-to-end delivery of ConvergeCONSUMER product implementations for enterprise clients, from kickoff through go-live
  • Lead discovery and scoping conversations with client stakeholders to define engagement scope, timeline, and success criteria

  • Develop reusable delivery playbooks, demo assets, and implementation patterns that accelerate future engagements
  • Coach and unblock junior FDEs and consultants on the team, sharing delivery and client-management best practices

  • Strong executive presence, with the ability to build credibility quickly with senior client stakeholders
  • Natural people leader, comfortable guiding and unblocking a small team under deadline pressure
  • Skilled at translating between technical delivery realities and business or product priorities
  • Proactive communicator who surfaces risk and feedback early rather than waiting to be asked
  • Resourceful and outcomes-oriented, comfortable navigating ambiguous or evolving client environments
  • Genuine curiosity about the consumer industry and how our products create value for clients

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8+ years of experience in client-facing technology consulting, professional services, or product delivery roles
  • Demonstrated experience leading small delivery teams and managing client engagements from scoping through go-live
  • Ability to travel 20-25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Job.JobTitle: Sr Product Manager – Digital Product Management
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Project Manager, IT / Technology, Sales / Business Development
Job.JobDescription:
Your opportunity


At Schwab, you're empowered to make an impact on your career. Here, innovative thought meets creative problem solving, helping us challenge the status quo and transform the finance industry together.

We believe in the importance of in-office collaboration and fully intend for the selected candidate for this role to work on site in the specified location(s).

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without employer sponsorship.

As a Senior Product Manager, Digital Product Management, you will be part of a team driving digital transformation by delivering experiences and technology capabilities that enable our client-facing representatives to better serve Schwab clients.

You will play a critical role in shaping the strategy and evolution of Salesforce capabilities, reporting, digital channels, and integrations. You will work closely with product, technology, UX/UI, service, marketing, and business partners to translate client and representative needs into meaningful product solutions.

Success in this role requires a strong combination of product management, strategic thinking, relationship building, communication, stakeholder influence, technology fluency, and execution. Experience with Salesforce, financial services, channel management, or telephony integrations can further strengthen your ability to contribute.

What You'll Do

  • Lead product management efforts that enable client-facing representatives to leverage technology solutions to better serve Schwab clients.
  • Partner with product and technology teams throughout the product lifecycle to deliver efficient and effective Salesforce and digital solutions.
  • Develop a strong understanding of end-user needs and use stakeholder insights to help prioritize product initiatives.
  • Partner with UX/UI teams to facilitate feedback sessions, establish OKRs and success measures, and continuously improve the user experience.
  • Partner with business stakeholders to develop product strategy and roadmaps that evolve Salesforce capabilities and support business objectives.
  • Translate business and user needs into product requirements, refinements, and actionable priorities.
  • Work cross-functionally with technology, design, service, marketing, and business partners to evolve digital capabilities.
  • Communicate product vision, strategy, priorities, progress, and outcomes to stakeholders and leadership.
  • Use feedback, product insights, and measurable outcomes to identify opportunities for continued product improvement.

Why You're Set Up for Success

You'll have the opportunity to combine product strategy, technology, client experience, and cross-functional leadership while supporting capabilities used by Schwab's client-facing representatives.

The role provides meaningful ownership across the product lifecycle, from understanding representative and business needs through prioritization, roadmap development, delivery, measurement, and continued enhancement.

You'll collaborate with partners across product, technology, UX/UI, service, marketing, and the broader organization, giving you opportunities to build relationships and influence how Schwab continues to evolve its digital capabilities.

Schwab Training and Development

Schwab supports ongoing learning through role-based development, cross-functional exposure, coaching, and opportunities to deepen your expertise in product management, Salesforce capabilities, digital platforms, client and representative experiences, and financial services.

You'll have opportunities to strengthen capabilities in areas such as product discovery, roadmap development, stakeholder management, technology delivery, data-driven decision making, and digital innovation. Curiosity, adaptability, and continuous learning are important to success as technologies and client needs continue to evolve.

Career Pathing

The role builds transferable capabilities across digital product management, product strategy, Salesforce and CRM platforms, client experience, technology transformation, and cross-functional leadership.

As you expand your expertise and impact, the experience gained in this role can support continued development across product management, digital transformation, client experience, technology enablement, strategy, and broader leadership opportunities based on business needs, demonstrated skills, performance, and career interests.

Competitive Compensation

In addition to the applicable salary range for the posting, this role may be eligible for bonus or incentive opportunities.

Performs responsible and professional technical-level work supporting the digital conversion, research, processing, review, and management of City of Orlando and Orlando Police Department (OPD) records. Responsibilities include scanning, indexing, and quality assurance of records in various formats, including microfilm, electronic, and historical records, some of which may contain sensitive, confidential, or legally protected information. Upon completion of OPD Records Department training, selected candidates will assist Police personnel with researching police records, reviewing and redacting documents in accordance with applicable Florida Statutes, and supporting the processing of Public Records Requests (PRRs). Duties may include researching information across various computer systems, preparing records for release, responding to PRR-related emails and telephone inquiries, and providing administrative and operational support to OPD Records staff. The position requires meticulous attention to detail, discretion in handling sensitive information, proficiency with computers and records management systems, and the ability to follow established procedures and applicable laws governing public records and confidentiality. Work is performed under the direction and supervision of the appropriate OPD Records Department supervisory personnel.


Responsibilities

The Records Specialist's responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

Records Conversion and Management

  • Operates various scanning and micrographic equipment.
  • Scans records into designated records retention systems and indexes documents for future retrieval.
  • Reviews scanned and indexed records to ensure accuracy, completeness, and quality.
  • Identifies and reports potential errors, discrepancies, or missing information to the appropriate supervisor.
  • Maintains an organized, clean, and efficient workstation.
  • Ensures the security, confidentiality, and proper handling of all records.

Police Records Research and Public Records Requests

Upon successful completion of OPD Records Department training, candidates will perform the following duties, including but not limited to:

  • Researches and retrieves police records using various computer systems, databases, and records management applications.
  • Reviews police reports, supporting documents, and other records to identify responsive materials for Public Records Requests.
  • Redacts information from documents in accordance with applicable Florida Statutes, public records laws, and established OPD procedures.
  • Assists OPD Records personnel with the processing, review, organization, and preparation of records responsive to PRRs.
  • Provides administrative and operational support to OPD Records staff in managing PRR-related emails, correspondence, and telephone inquiries.
  • Assists with locating, retrieving, organizing, and preparing responsive records for review and release.
  • Identifies records that may contain confidential, exempt, or sensitive information and refers questions or concerns to the appropriate supervisor for review.
  • Follows established procedures for documenting, tracking, and processing PRRs.
  • Maintains the confidentiality and security of police records and other sensitive information encountered during assigned duties.
  • Communicates professionally and courteously with City and OPD Records personnel and other authorized individuals regarding assigned tasks and inquiries.
  • Performs other records-related duties as assigned to support the daily operations of the OPD Records Department.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Knowledge of basic office procedures and records management practices, or the ability to acquire such knowledge through training.
  • Ability to learn and navigate multiple computer systems, databases, and electronic records management applications.
  • Ability to conduct detailed research to locate, retrieve, and verify information across various records systems.
  • Ability to review documents carefully and accurately identify information requiring redaction in accordance with applicable Florida Statutes and established procedures.
  • Ability to follow written and verbal instructions, established workflows, and departmental policies.
  • Ability to maintain strict confidentiality when handling police records, sensitive information, and legally protected data.
  • Ability to recognize potential errors, discrepancies, or concerns and promptly notify the appropriate supervisor.
  • Skilled in time management, organization, and prioritization of assigned responsibilities.
  • Skilled in the use of computers, scanning equipment, office equipment, and applicable software applications.
  • Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing.
  • Ability to respond professionally to telephone inquiries and assist with PRR-related correspondence.
  • Ability to work independently while maintaining effective communication and cooperation with team members.
  • Ability to maintain accuracy and attention to detail while performing repetitive tasks and working under established deadlines.
  • Ability to sit and work at a computer for extended periods.
  • Ability to lift 20 pounds or more.

Minimum Requirements and Conditions of Employment

  • Valid Florida Driver's License required.
  • Selected candidates must successfully complete a criminal background check, polygraph and submit fingerprints as required.
  • Candidates must successfully complete the required Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) training and certification before being granted applicable system access.
  • Candidates must comply with all OPD policies, security requirements, confidentiality standards, and applicable laws governing access to and handling of police records.
  • Access to department systems and records will be granted only as authorized and necessary to perform assigned duties.
  • Candidates must successfully complete OPD Records Department training before performing assigned police records research, redaction, and PRR support functions.

Note: This is a temporary/seasonal position intended to provide operational support to the OPD Records Department. Duties and assignments may vary based on departmental needs, workload, and supervisory direction.

The University Operations division at UCF is committed to creating a supportive and welcoming environment for our faculty, staff, students, and the broader community. The Opportunity:

Join our dynamic team at University Operations Work Control Center, where you'll play a vital role in delivering exceptional customer service. As a Part-Time Work Control Dispatcher I, you will respond promptly to requests from customers and staff, including emergency situations, while representing the University's Facilities & Business Operations.


Responsibilities:

  • This position processes, initially prioritizes, validates, and distributes all incoming work requests for all main and branch campus buildings including residence halls and apartments. Work requests come into the Work Control Center (WCC) via the Internet, e-mail, telephone, walk-up window or hand-held radio during the shift and are input into the IWMS in accordance with established Facilities and Business Operations (FBO) Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and the Work Order Management Process Guide.
  • Use SOPs to dispatch work to one or more zones, teams or groups across the entire FBO Department. Based on the situation, balance the urgency to protect life and property against the routine but active demands of an engaged organization.
  • Proactively notify the appropriate party to reconcile work requests by understanding intradepartmental responsibilities across the organization. Responsible for understanding the organizational structure for effective communication and collaboration.
  • Handle general requests for information (RFI's) Research relevant histories, logs and Integrated Work Management System (IWMS) data; summarize information obtained in form of a verbal report, e-mail and/or written report/spreadsheet. Place work orders in callback when customer contests work or work was not done.
  • Monitor parameters of Chiller plants and associated equipment, critical laboratories, server rooms and buildings utilizing computer monitoring software. Respond to all alarms in accordance with Standard Operating Procedures, and as necessary, notify the appropriate on-call personnel.
  • Serve as the FBO initial advocate during after-hours emergencies in support of UCF Public Safety Department, Emergency Operation Center, State and Federal authorities, and other University Departments. Execute SOPs during emergencies, maintain situational awareness throughout the event and alert senior facilities staff as the situation warrants.
  • Update IWMS work orders to serve as primary and permanent history of work dispatched, completed, material and time billed.
  • Receive and report after-hour messages to the appropriate FBO staff including external RFI, personnel absentee reports and other intradepartmental requests.

Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma or Equivalent and 2+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Minimum of one year of customer service experience, demonstrating strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills.
  • Prior experience working in a high-volume operations or facilities environment within a large, complex organization, with an understanding of service-oriented best practices.
  • Proven customer service orientation, with the ability to communicate professionally and respond courteously to inquiries from both internal and external stakeholders.
  • Strong command of conversational English to interact effectively with customers and team members, including the ability to manage and resolve conflicts while maintaining a positive customer experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment, applying sound analytical and problem-solving skills to manage multiple priorities.
  • Experience exercising sound judgment and decision-making with limited supervision in a fast-paced, dynamic setting.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel, and Teams.
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritize and handle multiple tasks efficiently.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • This position may qualify for a 5% shift differential depending on the assigned schedule.
  • The anticipated hourly range for this position is $16.43 -$18.00. The final hourly rate will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • Schedule is based on business needs and may include holidays since this area operates 365 days per year.

The Opportunity:

University Operations is seeking to hire a Zone Manager, Floor Care & Projects. This role is responsible for coordinating and overseeing floor‑care operations and custodial project activities across assigned campus buildings. This position ensures that all services, staff, and processes align with university, state, and industry standards. Serving as the primary customer contact for service quality, communication, and project coordination, the Zone Manager plays a key role in maintaining a safe, clean, and welcoming campus environment. The ideal candidate is highly skilled in floor‑care techniques, equipment, and materials; experienced in leading teams and managing projects; and committed to delivering high‑quality, compliant, and customer‑focused service.

Responsibilities:

Operations & Supervision

  • Oversee all floor‑care services and custodial project activities within the assigned zone.
  • Supervise custodial, project, and lead staff, including staffing, scheduling, training, performance management, and corrective actions in accordance with departmental SOPs and guidelines.
  • Maintain internal controls to support efficient operations, asset protection, compliance requirements, and accurate financial tracking.
  • Conduct regular floor inspections and develop comprehensive maintenance plans for all flooring types.

Work Management & Planning

  • Review and manage zone work orders in the Integrated Work Management System (IWMS), ensuring accurate entry of work status, costs, dates, and corrective actions.
  • Develop coordinated schedules involving staff, trades, contractors, vendors, inspectors, and other stakeholders.
  • Align work with team‑cleaning frameworks and ensure the completion of preventive maintenance, including annual inventories of all floor‑care equipment.
  • Evaluate work schedules, forecast manpower needs, and prioritize backlog to ensure efficient work assignment and timely completion.
  • Generate weekly and monthly reports on planned and in‑progress work, including resource allocation and schedule performance.
  • Document schedule variances and adjust project timelines to meet quality, safety, and maintenance standards.

Quality Assurance & Compliance

  • Review work packages—electronic or hard copy—for completeness and accuracy, ensuring specifications, manuals, and drawings meet university standards and regulatory requirements.
  • Inspect zone and contractor work to ensure scope fulfillment, workmanship quality, and process compliance.
  • Complete work order closure in accordance with work‑management processes, validating accuracy of all data, including labor, materials, dates, images, invoices, and corrective actions.
  • Ensure all activities comply with organizational policies, safety standards, codes, and regulations.

Customer Service & Communication

  • Serve as liaison between customers and service providers, facilitating timely resolution of requests and concerns.
  • Conduct customer work‑review meetings using planning documentation and progress reports.
  • Assess zone impacts to balance customer needs while meeting service standards.
  • Schedule periodic customer reviews to assess service quality and performance.
  • Maintain clear, consistent, and transparent communication with campus stakeholders and collaborate with other departments to coordinate services around operational schedules.

Safety, Training & Employee Development

  • Maintain a safe and healthy work environment in compliance with legal codes, regulations, and university standards.
  • Provide coaching and training on job duties, SOPs, and customer service expectations.
  • Ensure accurate documentation of employee performance, coaching, and compliance.
  • Ensure urgent and life‑safety work orders receive expedited response.
  • Perform quality checks to confirm that delivered services meet established standards and the university's process guide.

Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma or Equivalent and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of custodial management or floor-care leadership experience in a university, educational, healthcare, or large-scale commercial environment.
  • Advanced knowledge of floor‑care techniques, equipment, materials, and maintenance practices for a wide range of flooring types (e.g., terrazzo, VCT, carpet, hardwood, rubber, tile).
  • Experience managing custodial or facilities staff including training, performance evaluation, and corrective action within an SOP‑driven environment.
  • Strong project‑planning and scheduling skills, including the ability to forecast manpower requirements, prioritize backlogs, and coordinate multiple stakeholders.
  • Excellent communication and customer‑service skills, with experience serving as liaison between internal customers, contractors, and service providers.
  • Knowledge of OSHA regulations, safety practices, and applicable codes related to custodial operations and floor‑care activities.
  • Certifications in custodial management or floor‑care operations, such as ISSA, IICRC, or similar industry credentials.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Accountant, Accounting / Finance / Banking, Grant Writer
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity:

This position performs post-award sponsored program functions associated with the post-award administration of awards. The Contracts and Grants Accountant II is responsible for the invoicing, collection, and post-award fiscal management of sponsored programs as assigned. This position reports to the Assistant Director, Sponsored Programs.


Responsibilities:

  • Prepare post-award financial reports for federal, state, and private funded research contracts and grants as assigned by the supervisor. This includes but is not limited to invoicing and preparing Cost Reports for awards requiring Draws or Installment Payments. Act as contact person for awarding agency representatives concerning contractual issues of billing and reporting.
  • Interpret and implement post award policies and financial compliance in regard to sponsored research projects as required by federal regulations in 2 CFR 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles and Audit Requirements, sponsor terms and conditions, State of Florida statutes, and University of Central Florida policies.
  • Review award documents (agreement, budget, statement of work, and other contract and grant requirements) to ensure award setup is accurate and complete in the research administration and financial databases.
  • Perform the cash management activities of requesting accurate and timely reimbursements from awarding agencies and following up on accounts receivable, including draw coordination and submission for entire Office of Research Grants Accounting team.
  • Work with principal investigators, institute, center or department administrators and Office of Research award administrators to ensure all cost share commitments of the university are documented.
  • Review project transactions, such as revenue, accounts receivable and expenditures, for accuracy and appropriateness and input or request adjustments as necessary. Analyze project expenditures to ensure costs are allowable, allocable, reasonable and consistently handled as directed by 2 CFR 200 and other Federal agency regulations.
  • Review and approve journal entries submitted by departments to record financial transactions on sponsored awards.
  • Assist principal investigators, institute, center or department administrators and OR award administrators in resolving specific fiscal and accounting problems in relation to sponsored awards.

Work you'll do

As an Accounts Receivable Analyst you will deliver Back End Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) services, including Billing and Claims Submission, A/R Follow-up, Denials Management, Payment Posting, and Credits and Refunds, for health care provider client

  • Review AR aging reports and work queues to identify unpaid and delayed claims.

  • Review payments, contractual adjustments, denials, and patient responsibility balances to validate accurate account resolution.
  • Adhere to defined SOPs and workflows and work within Epic Resolute Hospital Billing, claims clearinghouse, payer websites and portals, and other systems and required by workflows.
  • Meet and exceed minimum productivity and quality standards; submit to performance improvement plans as required according to guidance from engagement management.
  • Support team members in resolving complex claims.
  • Support engagement management in pulling performance reporting.

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
  • Ability to lead projects or workstreams
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Ability to provide clear guidance to others

We enable clients to stay ahead with the latest advancements by transforming engineering teams and modernizing technology & data platforms. Our delivery models are tailored to meet each client's unique requirements.

Our Industry Solutions offering provides verticalized solutions that transform how clients sell products, deliver services, generate growth, and execute mission-critical operations. We deliver integrated business expertise with scalable, repeatable technology solutions specifically engineered for each sector.

  • Build agents against a layered SDK contract (shared types/tools, composable tools, thin agent shell, FastAPI + React surface)
  • Keep business logic in composable skills rather than shells or routers
  • Integrate LLMs through a multi-provider abstraction (Anthropic/Bedrock/OpenAI/Azure, extending to Vertex/OCI) behind a single sanitization + audit boundary so no raw client data leaves the worker
  • Implement durable service boundaries (async persistence, object-storage artifacts, and a tamper-evident hash-chain audit trail per run)
  • Enforce tenant isolation via Postgres RLS scoped sessions and author Alembic migrations (enum/DDL idempotency, RLS policies)
  • Wire agents into an event-driven orchestrator with human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval gates, exposing progress via async tasks (Celery/Redis) and WebSocket
  • Ship behind mechanical architecture linting and CI, contributing new invariant checks
