Job.JobDescription:
Shape the Next Generation of Vacations!
Welcome to Evermore Orlando Resort—the resort that's redefining the Orlando vacation experience. Just steps away from Walt Disney World®, Evermore stretches across 1,100 acres and offers a one-of-a-kind blend of spacious, upscale vacation homes, flats, and villas alongside the luxurious Conrad hotel. Our Team Members are true trailblazers, reimagining the vacation experience for each guest. Here, guests create their own adventure, enjoying the best of both worlds: the space and comforts of vacation home rentals combined with the amenities and services of a world-class resort.

Evermore is Orlando's ultimate game changer. In a city known for its theme parks and endless lines, Evermore is the paradise guests crave on their days between park visits. Imagine endless relaxation around Orlando's first and only beach paradise, Evermore Bay. Our stunning 8-acre crystal-clear lagoon is framed by zero-entry swim zones, beach bars, private cabanas, cozy firepits, and 20-acres of white sand. From beachside bars to a vibrant food hall and rooftop dining with views of the fireworks, we've crafted unforgettable experiences. Guests can challenge themselves on 2 Jack Nicklaus championship golf courses, enjoy water sports including kayaks and paddleboards, a family water slide, rope swing, and activities that fill their days including pickleball, bocce ball, and volleyball.

If you're excited to help guests reimagine the Orlando vacation, join us! Become part of an energetic team bringing Evermore Orlando Resort to life!

Key Responsibilities:

  • Complete knowledge of hot and cold line stations.
  • Prep food items and prepare cold food items utilizing knives, slicers and other kitchen equipment.
  • Skillfully prepare and cook a diverse range of dishes in adherence to menu specifications, maintaining a superior standard of culinary excellence
  • Employ various cooking techniques and utilize kitchen equipment effectively to achieve desired flavors and textures.
  • Ensure consistency in taste, presentation, and portion size for all food items, upholding the resort's high culinary standards.
  • Conduct rigorous quality checks on ingredients to ensure they meet the resort's exacting quality criteria.
  • Maintain a clean and organized workstation, strictly adhering to sanitation and safety guidelines.
  • Provide guidance and mentorship to junior kitchen staff, contributing to a positive and productive work environment.
  • Utilize knives, slicers and other kitchen equipment safely and responsibly.
  • Cook and plate food according to recipes and menus utilizing a variety of equipment, including broilers, outdoor grills, stoves, fryers, ovens, steamers and kettles.
  • Operate kitchen equipment safely and responsibly.
  • Rotate food in walking coolers and freezers to minimize waste and spoilage.
  • Adhere to all food safety and sanitation standards.
  • Set up hot and cold line stations and food trams for transport.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Front Desk Agent / Concierge, Hospitality / Tourism / Events
Job.JobDescription:
JOB SUMMARY

Assists the Front Office Manager in administering front office functions and supervising staff on a daily basis. Front office areas include Bell/Door Staff, Switchboard and Guest Services/Front Desk. Position directs and works with managers and employees to carry out procedures ensuring an efficient check in and check out process. Ensures guest and employee satisfaction and maximizes the financial performance of the department.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education and Experience

• High school diploma or GED; 2 years experience in the guest services, front desk, or related professional area.

OR

• 2-year degree from an accredited university in Hotel and Restaurant Management, Hospitality, Business Administration, or related major; no work experience required.

CORE WORK ACTIVITIES

Maintaining Guest Services and Front Desk Goals

• Manages day-to-day operations, ensuring the quality, standards and meeting the expectations of the customers on a daily basis.

• Develops specific goals and plans to prioritize, organize, and accomplish your work.

• Handles complaints, settling disputes, and resolving grievances and conflicts, or otherwise negotiating with others.

• Supervises staffing levels to ensure that guest service, operational needs and financial objectives are met.

• Ensures that regular on-going communication is happening with employees to create awareness of business objectives and communicate expectations, recognizes performance, and produces desired results.

• Understands the impact of department's operations on the overall property financial goals and objectives and manages to achieve or exceed goals.

Supporting Management of Front Desk Team

• Utilizes interpersonal and communication skills to lead, influence, and encourage others; advocates sound financial/business decision making; demonstrates honesty/integrity; leads by example.

• Encourages and building mutual trust, respect, and cooperation among team members.

• Serving as a role model to demonstrate appropriate behaviors.

• Supervises and manages employees. Manages all day-to-day operations. Understands employee positions well enough to perform duties in employees' absence.

• Establishes and maintains open, collaborative relationships with employees and ensures employees do the same within the team.

• Supervises all areas of the Front Office in the absence of the Front Office or Assistant Front Office Manager.

Ensuring Exceptional Customer Service

• Provides services that are above and beyond for customer satisfaction and retention.

• Improves service by communicating and assisting individuals to understand guest needs, providing guidance, feedback, and individual coaching when needed.

• Responds to and handles guest problems and complaints.

• Sets a positive example for guest relations.

• Empowers employees to provide excellent customer service.

• Observes service behaviors of employees and provides feedback to individuals.

• Interacts with customers to obtain feedback on quality of product, service levels and overall satisfaction.

• Ensures employees understand customer service expectations and parameters.

• Interacts with guests to obtain feedback on product quality and service levels.

• Emphasizes guest satisfaction during all departmental meetings and focuses on continuous improvement.

Managing Projects and Policies

• Implements the customer recognition/service program, communicating and ensuring the process.

• Trains staff and monitors adherence to all credit policies and procedures to reduce bad debts and rebates.

• Supervises same day selling procedures to maximize room revenue and control property occupancy.

• Supervises daily Front Desk shift operations and ensures compliance with all policies, standards and procedures.

• Ensures property policies are administered fairly and consistently, disciplinary procedures and documentation are completed according to Standard and Local Operating Procedures (SOPs and LSOPs) and support the Peer Review Process.

Supporting Human Resource Activities

• Supports the developmental needs of others and coaching, mentoring, or otherwise helping others to improve their knowledge or skills.

• Solicits employee feedback, utilizes an “open door” policy and reviews employee satisfaction results to identify and address employee problems or concerns.

• Brings issues concerning employee satisfaction to the attention of the department manager and Human Resources.

• Assists as needed in the interviewing and hiring of employee team members with the appropriate skills.

• Supports a departmental orientation program for employees to receive the appropriate new hire training to successfully perform their job.

• Participates in employee progressive discipline procedures.

Additional Responsibilities

• Provides information to supervisors, co-workers, and subordinates by telephone, in written form, e-mail, or in person.

• Analyzes information and evaluating results to choose the best solution and solve problems.

• Informs and/or updates the executives, the peers and the subordinates on relevant information in a timely manner.

• Performs all duties at the Front Desk as necessary.

• Runs Front Desk shifts whenever necessary.

• Participates in departmental meetings and continually communicates a clear and consistent message regarding the Front Desk goals to produce desired results.

Shape the Next Generation of Vacations!
Welcome to Evermore Orlando Resort—the resort that's redefining the Orlando vacation experience. Just steps away from Walt Disney World®, Evermore stretches across 1,100 acres and offers a one-of-a-kind blend of spacious, upscale vacation homes, flats, and villas alongside the luxurious Conrad hotel. Our Team Members are true trailblazers, reimagining the vacation experience for each guest. Here, guests create their own adventure, enjoying the best of both worlds: the space and comforts of vacation home rentals combined with the amenities and services of a world-class resort.

Evermore is Orlando's ultimate game changer. In a city known for its theme parks and endless lines, Evermore is the paradise guests crave on their days between park visits. Imagine endless relaxation around Orlando's first and only beach paradise, Evermore Bay. Our stunning 8-acre crystal-clear lagoon is framed by zero-entry swim zones, beach bars, private cabanas, cozy firepits, and 20-acres of white sand. From beachside bars to a vibrant food hall and rooftop dining with views of the fireworks, we've crafted unforgettable experiences. Guests can challenge themselves on 2 Jack Nicklaus championship golf courses, enjoy water sports including kayaks and paddleboards, a family water slide, rope swing, and activities that fill their days including pickleball, bocce ball, and volleyball.

If you're excited to help guests reimagine the Orlando vacation, join us! Become part of an energetic team bringing Evermore Orlando Resort to life!

Evermore Culture

At Evermore, our purpose is Togetherness, and our vision is to make a more together world possible.

Through relational wellness, we cultivate an inclusive, people-first culture where collaboration, trust, and respect empower every Team Member to thrive. Job.JobTitle: Converge for FSI - RAE Lead Product Forward Deployed Engineer_Products & Platforms
Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

The Team

Are you looking for a unique opportunity with both start-up spirit AND enterprise strength? Deloitte's Converge for FSI business offers both! We are looking for a talented individual with an innovative mindset to join the Converge for FSI team in our mission to develop differentiated financial services products that achieve product-market fit. This role is focused on the Retirement Agentic Ecosystem (RAE), an AI-enabled platform that connects retirement systems and coordinates workflows across plan onboarding, ongoing operations and participant servicing—helping providers reduce manual work, improve accuracy and deliver more connected experiences. This is a great opportunity to be on the frontlines of Deloitte's innovation & product strategy while staying close to industry/sector priorities.

Position Summary

We are looking for a highly skilled and client-facing Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to sit at the intersection of engineering excellence and customer partnership. In this role, you will embed directly with our most strategic clients — particularly in the financial services sector — to understand their toughest technical challenges and help them design and implement world-class solutions using our platform. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role with direct influence on product direction.

You are equally comfortable whiteboarding microservices architecture with a client's principal engineer, running a hands-on technical workshop for a team of developers, and standing up a compelling proof-of-concept in days. You thrive in fast-moving, high-stakes environments and know how to earn the trust of deeply technical stakeholders.

Recruiting for this role ends on 11/30/2026.

Work you'll do

  • Serve as a technical point of contact for strategic client accounts, building deep relationships with architects, engineers, and technical leaders
  • Lead discovery sessions to understand client architectures, pain points, and business objectives
  • Translate complex technical concepts into clear, compelling narratives for both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Collaborate with client architects and internal engineering teams to design scalable, production-ready solutions
  • Provide authoritative guidance on microservices architecture, event-driven systems, and cloud-native deployment patterns
  • Review and advise on client system designs, identifying risks and recommending best practices
  • Rapidly prototype and build POCs that demonstrate platform value in the context of a client's real-world use cases
  • Own and deliver polished, technically rigorous demos tailored to the client's specific technology stack and business domain
  • Maintain a library of reusable demo assets and reference implementations
  • Design and facilitate deep-dive technical workshops, hackathons, and onboarding bootcamps for client engineering teams
  • Produce high-quality technical documentation, runbooks, and integration guides
  • Accelerate client time-to-value by enabling their teams to build confidently and independently
  • Act as the voice of the customer — surface product gaps, integration friction, and feature requests to internal product and engineering teams
  • Partner with Sales, Solutions Architecture, and Product to shape the technical go-to-market strategy

The successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Deep expertise in Java and Spring Boot, including building production-grade microservices
  • Strong understanding of event-driven architecture — Kafka, event sourcing, CQRS, async messaging patterns
  • Hands-on experience with microservices design principles: service decomposition, API design, resiliency patterns, observability
  • Proficiency across multi-cloud environments, with AWS as a primary platform; working knowledge of Azure and GCP
  • Familiarity with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes)
  • Exposure to Agentic AI frameworks and tooling — including LangGraph, LangChain, or similar orchestration frameworks
  • Practical understanding of LLM integration patterns, prompt engineering, and AI-powered application design
  • Interest in staying current with the rapidly evolving AI/ML landscape and translating it into client-relevant use cases
  • Exceptional communicator — able to lead technical conversations with senior engineers and C-suite stakeholders alike
  • Strong facilitation skills for running workshops, design reviews, and working sessions
  • Self-directed, highly organized, and comfortable managing multiple client engagements simultaneously
  • Natural curiosity and a bias for building — you'd rather spin up a demo than write a slide about one

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Business, Marketing or equivalent field. MBA a plus.
  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, with significant time spent in client-facing, solutions engineering, or field engineering roles
  • Ability to travel 20-40%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred:

  • Background in financial services, specifically retirement & wealth, strongly preferred
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and DevSecOps practices
  • Contributions to open-source projects or public technical content (talks, blogs, repos)
  • Prior experience in a startup or high-growth SaaS environment
  • Prior experience using AI and LLMs to rapid prototype in a sales, business development or product demonstrations
  • Relevant cloud certifications (AWS Solutions Architect, GCP Professional, etc.)

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $134,500-$265,100

You may also be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.

Benefits

At Deloitte, we know that great people make a great organization. We value our people and offer employees a broad range of benefits. Learn more about what working at Deloitte can mean for you.

Our people and culture

Our inclusive culture empowers our people to be who they are, contribute their unique perspectives, and make a difference individually and collectively. It enables us to leverage different ways of thinking, ideas, and perspectives, and bring more creativity and innovation to help solve our clients' most complex challenges. This makes Deloitte one of the most rewarding places to work.

Our purpose

Deloitte's purpose is to make an impact that matters for our people, clients, and communities. At Deloitte, purpose is synonymous with how we work every day. It defines who we are. Our purpose comes through in our work with clients that enables impact and value in their organizations, as well as through our own investments, commitments, and actions across areas that help drive positive outcomes for our communities. Learn more.

Professional development

From entry-level employees to senior leaders, we believe there's always room to learn. We offer opportunities to build new skills, take on leadership opportunities and connect and grow through mentorship. From on-the-job learning experiences to formal development programs, our professionals have a variety of opportunities to continue to grow throughout their career.

Nature of Work:

An Orlando Venues Security Specialist is a vital member of the Guest Experience Division for KIA Center, Camping World Stadium, and Mennello Museum. The Security Specialist primary roles are to observe & report and deliver legendary guest experiences. They proactively protect facilities, clients, and the public from potential hazards as well as deter theft and criminal acts with their presence. Additional responsibilities include completing written incident reports, ensuring compliance with policies & procedures, assisting pedestrians with traffic crossing, being on alert for safety issues, and handling crowd control with discretion and diplomacy. Security Agents are expected to have good communication skills, exhibit a safety-first mindset, and conduct themselves with a high level of professionalism. Involves standing and walking for extended periods of time, climbing stairs, and working outdoors.

Majority of available shifts are nights and weekends. No set number of hours per week are guaranteed. Will be required to work holidays in accordance with event schedule. Position Summary

The Team

ConvergeCONSUMER™ is a product-driven business that combines differentiated consumer insights with robust prediction and optimization capabilities to help consumer-focused businesses improve decision-making and deliver personalized experiences to drive growth, consumer loyalty, and profitability. We operate with the speed and agility of a startup within the world's largest professional services firm.

We drive value for our clients by optimizing decisions and actions at a level of granularity only made possible with today's data and technology. ConvergeCONSUMER's suite of solutions helps consumer-facing businesses prosper in a world being re-shaped by convergence, where the lines between industries, competitors and collaborators, consumers and suppliers, and even human and artificial intelligence have blurred.

Position Summary

Are you the person people call when a delivery-blocking issue needs to be found fast? As a Backend DevOps & UAT Engineer on ConvergeCONSUMER, you'll be the technical backstop for our product delivery teams — troubleshooting backend issues, owning UAT coordination, and making sure problems get tracked to resolution instead of falling through the cracks.

Recruiting for this role ends on 11/30/2026.

Work you'll do

As the Backend DevOps & UAT Engineer, you will:

  • Troubleshoot backend issues surfacing during product delivery and client implementations, working across environments to isolate root cause
  • Own User Acceptance Testing (UAT) coordination for product releases, catching and resolving issues before go-live
  • Escalate and track defects and delivery blockers across engineering, delivery, and product teams until resolved
  • Build and maintain test scripts and scenarios to validate backend functionality ahead of releases
  • Partner with delivery teams to validate environment configuration, data, and integration issues during implementations
  • Support CI/CD pipeline health and flag recurring failure patterns to engineering
  • Document recurring issues and troubleshooting steps to build the team's shared knowledge base

The successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Methodical troubleshooter who can isolate root cause across multiple layers of a system under time pressure
  • Comfortable working across engineering, delivery, and product teams to track an issue through to resolution
  • Detail-oriented tester who thinks through edge cases and the downstream effects of changes
  • Clear written communicator, able to document issues and steps so others can follow them
  • Stays calm under pressure when a delivery-blocking issue needs fast triage and escalation
  • Continuous-improvement mindset toward reducing recurring issues over time

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of backend development or DevOps experience supporting product delivery or implementation troubleshooting
  • Hands-on experience with UAT coordination, defect tracking, and escalation management across engineering and delivery teams
  • Ability to travel 0-10%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred:

  • Experience with CI/CD tooling and pipeline troubleshooting
  • Experience supporting client-facing product implementations or deployments

Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

The Team

ConvergeCONSUMER™ is a product-driven business that combines differentiated consumer insights with robust prediction and optimization capabilities to help consumer-focused businesses improve decision-making and deliver personalized experiences to drive growth, consumer loyalty, and profitability. We operate with the speed and agility of a startup within the world's largest professional services firm.

We drive value for our clients by optimizing decisions and actions at a level of granularity only made possible with today's data and technology. ConvergeCONSUMER's suite of solutions helps consumer-facing businesses prosper in a world being re-shaped by convergence, where the lines between industries, competitors and collaborators, consumers and suppliers, and even human and artificial intelligence have blurred.

Position Summary

Are you energized by turning inbound demand into a well-run pipeline? As the GTM & Customer Growth Manager on ConvergeCONSUMER, you'll be the connective tissue between account teams, Consumer leadership, and our delivery organization — keeping go-to-market momentum moving even as the team's day-to-day focus shifts toward delivery and product priorities.

Recruiting for this role ends on 11/30/2026.

Work you'll do

As the GTM & Customer Growth Manager on ConvergeCONSUMER, you will:

  • Own and prioritize inbound GTM requests from account teams and Consumer leadership, making sure they're structured and advanced effectively
  • Support customer growth and pipeline development activities across the Consumer portfolio
  • Coordinate Signals and other data-driven analyses needed to support pursuits and growth initiatives
  • Connect internal teams to existing capabilities and resources, reducing duplicated effort across pursuits
  • Provide ongoing support across strategic accounts and growth streams that require sustained attention
  • Partner with delivery and product teams to make sure GTM requests don't stall amid competing priorities
  • Track and report on GTM pipeline health and momentum to Consumer leadership
  • Build lightweight processes and playbooks so GTM support scales as the team and portfolio grow

The successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Comfortable triaging and prioritizing a high volume of inbound requests from multiple stakeholders at once
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, able to work effectively across account teams, delivery teams, and leadership
  • Analytically minded, comfortable interpreting data and analyses to support pursuit conversations
  • Organized self-starter who brings structure to ambiguous, fast-moving requests
  • Clear communicator able to translate between technical delivery teams and business stakeholders
  • Genuine interest in the consumer industry and growth strategy

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7+ years of experience in go-to-market, sales strategy, or business development roles
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating cross-functional stakeholders to support pipeline development and pursuit activities
  • Ability to travel 20-25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred:

  • Experience with data- or analytics-driven pursuit support, such as market sizing or opportunity analysis
  • Experience within the consumer, retail, or related industries

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $134,500 - $265,100.

You may also be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.

Deloitte is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities. If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the recruiting process, please direct your inquiries to the Global Call Center (GCC) at USTalentCICInbox@deloitte.com.

Benefits

At Deloitte, we know that great people make a great organization. We value our people and offer employees a broad range of benefits. Learn more about what working at Deloitte can mean for you.

Our people and culture

Our inclusive culture empowers our people to be who they are, contribute their unique perspectives, and make a difference individually and collectively. It enables us to leverage different ways of thinking, ideas, and perspectives, and bring more creativity and innovation to help solve our clients' most complex challenges. This makes Deloitte one of the most rewarding places to work.

Our purpose

Deloitte's purpose is to make an impact that matters for our people, clients, and communities. At Deloitte, purpose is synonymous with how we work every day. It defines who we are. Our purpose comes through in our work with clients that enables impact and value in their organizations, as well as through our own investments, commitments, and actions across areas that help drive positive outcomes for our communities. Learn more.

Professional development

From entry-level employees to senior leaders, we believe there's always room to learn. We offer opportunities to build new skills, take on leadership opportunities and connect and grow through mentorship. From on-the-job learning experiences to formal development programs, our professionals have a variety of opportunities to continue to grow throughout their career.

Your opportunity

As a Senior Manager, Business Strategy within Retail Field Operations, you will help shape and execute compensation strategies that support Schwab's branch network and client-facing professionals. This role blends strategic thinking, data-driven decision making, program leadership and cross-functional influence to advance compensation strategies aligned to business objectives, employee experience and field performance. It centers on three priorities: Shaping compensation strategy and roadmap, delivering analytics and business cases and leading program execution, governance and change adoption.

You will partner closely with leaders across Field Operations, Human Resources, Compensation, Legal, Compliance, Technology, and Product teams to assess existing compensation programs, identify opportunities for improvement, and design scalable solutions that drive business outcomes. Success in this role requires the ability to influence without authority, communicate effectively with senior leaders, and lead complex initiatives from concept through implementation.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Compensation Planning

  • Contribute to the development and execution of a multi-year compensation strategy and roadmap.
  • Evaluate current compensation practices and identify opportunities to improve effectiveness, scalability, and employee experience.
  • Assess market, business, and organizational trends to inform compensation recommendations.

Compensation Analytics & Insights

  • Analyze compensation-related data to identify trends, opportunities, risks, and business impacts.
  • Develop data-driven recommendations that support strategic decision making.
  • Translate complex analyses into actionable insights for business leaders and stakeholders.

Program Leadership & Execution

  • Develop decision-ready materials and support governance for compensation-related changes, including clear articulation of objectives, rationale, data insights, risks, tradeoffs, stakeholder impacts and implementation considerations.
  • Lead compensation-related initiatives from ideation through implementation.
  • Develop business cases, project plans, success measures, and implementation strategies.
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure alignment and successful execution.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Collaborate with partners across Compensation, HR, Legal, Compliance, Technology, Product, and Retail Field Leadership.
  • Facilitate discussions to resolve complex issues and align stakeholders around solutions.
  • Build trusted relationships across multiple functions and levels of leadership.

Change Management & Adoption

  • Support communication and adoption of compensation program enhancements and strategy changes.
  • Develop approaches that drive stakeholder understanding, engagement, and successful implementation.
  • Navigate evolving business priorities and organizational change effectively.

Executive Communication

  • Prepare and deliver presentations, recommendations, and analyses for senior leaders.
  • Communicate complex concepts in a clear, concise, and compelling manner.
  • Influence decisions through sound judgment, strong business acumen, and effective storytelling.

What you have


Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years of program management or related experience, including setting strategic vision, developing business cases, and executing initiatives end-to-end.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze complex business problems, synthesize data, and develop practical, scalable solutions.
  • Ability to lead complex strategy and execution work in partnership with other enterprises, with either compensation subject matter knowledge or the ability to quickly build compensation acumen.
  • Experience collaborating with cross-functional partners and influencing decisions through clear, effective communication.
  • Ability to navigate ambiguity, prioritize competing demands, and adapt to evolving business needs.
  • Strong relationship-building skills with the ability to partner effectively across multiple stakeholder groups
  • Exposure to tools such as Salesforce, Tableau, Microsoft Teams, Power BI, or similar systems supporting analytics, reporting, and collaboration.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience within financial services, with exposure to compensation strategy, incentive plan design, or related programs.
  • Familiarity with working alongside technology and product teams, including participation in platform, data, or system-related discussions.
  • Experience supporting change management or driving adoption of new programs or initiatives across distributed teams.
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Human Resources, Finance, Economics, Organizational Development, or a related field preferred.
  • Professional certifications such as CCP, SHRM, PMP, or related credentials are a plus.

What Success Looks Like

  • Defines clear strategies and translates them into actionable plans.
  • Uses data and analytics to inform decisions and recommendations.
  • Influences stakeholders and drives alignment across diverse teams.
  • Demonstrates sound judgment when navigating ambiguity and competing priorities.
  • Effectively leads large-scale initiatives from concept through execution.
  • Communicates clearly and confidently with senior leaders and business partners.

What's in it for you

At Schwab, you're empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

We offer a competitive benefits package that takes care of the whole you – both today and in the future:

  • 401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan

Job.JobTitle: Sr. Manager, Business Analysis & Learning Development
Job.JobDescription:
Your opportunity


At Schwab, you're empowered to make an impact on your career. Here, innovative thought meets creative problem solving, helping us challenge the status quo and transform the finance industry together.

The Banking Operations learning and development team helps employees build the knowledge and capabilities needed to deliver strong workplace performance. As Senior Training Manager, you will serve as a trusted peer lead, cross-functional project lead, and decision-making partner to the department leader, without direct supervisory responsibility. You will bring together business acumen, influential communication, adaptive coaching, and applied expertise across the learning and development lifecycle to turn business priorities into focused, measurable learning solutions.

In this role, you will help prioritize the learning portfolio, lead complex initiatives from discovery through evaluation, and create alignment around scope, requirements, risks, trade-offs, decision ownership, and success measures. You will guide quality across needs analysis, instructional design, content development, facilitation, implementation, and evaluation while partnering with business leaders to diagnose performance gaps and determine when learning or non-learning interventions will create the greatest impact. Through clear recommendations, purposeful coaching, and disciplined follow-through, you will strengthen workplace application, reduce avoidable rework, and help Banking Operations deliver consistent performance outcomes.

We believe in the importance of in-office collaboration and fully intend for the selected candidate for this role to work on site in the specified location(s).

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full time basis without employer sponsorship.

What you have


Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years of applied experience in adult learning and instructional design or content development, learning measurement and reporting, and facilitation or presentations. These experience requirements may be met concurrently and are not cumulative.
  • Applied understanding of performance consulting, design, development, delivery, learning technology, and evaluation sufficient to guide quality and effective handoffs across specialties.
  • Ability to connect business goals, observable performance outcomes, learning objectives, and evaluation measures; assess demonstrated capability and workplace application beyond completion and satisfaction; and use findings to improve solutions.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, presentation, and facilitation skills, with the ability to adapt complex information and interactive learning for audiences ranging from new hires to senior executives.
  • Strong analytical and performance-consulting skills, including needs assessment, root-cause analysis, and process improvement, with the ability to distinguish knowledge and skill gaps from process, tool, communication, and expectation gaps.
  • Demonstrated ability to coach adults across career stages, skill levels, and development needs through active listening, purposeful questions, specific feedback, tailored practice, and follow-up that builds capability and independence.
  • Ability to influence consultatively and challenge constructively by questioning requests and assumptions, using evidence to define performance needs, and explaining trade-offs when recommending learning or non-learning solutions.
  • Demonstrated end-to-end learning and development project leadership, organizational discipline, and sound judgment, including prioritizing concurrent initiatives, validating requirements, managing risks and scope changes, and applying quality checks to protect outcomes.
  • Demonstrated peer and cross-functional leadership without supervisory authority, including building alignment, facilitating decisions, following through on commitments, and presenting evidence-based recommendations within clear decision boundaries.
  • Experience applying instructional design models such as ADDIE or SAM across e-learning, instructor-led, and blended learning, and designing coaching or mentoring programs.
  • Familiarity with Agile approaches such as Scrum or Kanban and traditional Waterfall methods, along with a project management certification such as PMP.
  • Advanced Microsoft Office skills and experience with Articulate authoring tools, SharePoint collaboration and content platforms, and learning management systems used for delivery, administration, and reporting.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Extensive experience delivering process training in the brokerage or financial services industry

In addition to the salary range, this role is also eligible for bonus or incentive opportunities


What's in it for you

At Schwab, you're empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

  • Paid parental leave and family building benefits
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance

Job.JobTitle: AI Developer - Financial Crimes AI & Automation
Job.JobDescription:
Your opportunity


At Schwab, you're empowered to make an impact on your career. Here, innovative thought meets creative problem solving, helping us “challenge the status quo” and transform the finance industry together.

Schwab's Financial Crimes Risk Management Shared Services organization builds technology that helps financial crimes professionals reduce repetitive work and focus on risk decisions requiring human judgment. As an AI Developer, you will design, build, test, deploy, and support production-ready AI agents and automated workflows using Microsoft Power Platform, Microsoft Copilot Studio, and related development tools.

This is an opportunity to turn complex business and risk needs into practical AI-enabled solutions that improve operational effectiveness and strengthen financial crimes risk management. You will collaborate with business users, process owners, technical teams, and control partners; make thoughtful architecture and integration decisions; evaluate quality and edge cases; and continuously improve solutions after launch.

You will join a collaborative environment where innovation is grounded in responsible development, strong controls, and service to our clients and colleagues. At Schwab, we lead with integrity and service, succeed together as One Schwab, and empower employees to own their tomorrow through meaningful work, continuous learning, and opportunities to grow as AI capabilities evolve.

What you'll do

  • Design and develop AI agents, automated workflows, and AI-enabled applications using Microsoft Power Platform, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Dataverse, and related development capabilities.
  • Translate business, process, risk, and control requirements into scalable solution architectures and production-ready technical designs.
  • Build custom agents, plugins, actions, orchestration patterns, custom connectors, integrations, and data structures that support reliable end-to-end solutions.
  • Integrate applications and workflows with APIs, approved data sources, connectors, and enterprise systems.
  • Write, review, troubleshoot, and improve code supporting AI, automation, integration, and data-processing solutions.
  • Own solutions throughout design, development, testing, documentation, deployment, monitoring, production support, and continuous improvement.
  • Evaluate solution quality, edge cases, traceability, human-review needs, security considerations, and responsible handling of sensitive data.
  • Monitor production performance, analyze logs, resolve incidents, remediate defects, and maintain operational stability.
  • Communicate technical decisions clearly and collaborate across business, technology, and control teams.
  • Explore emerging AI capabilities and recommend practical approaches that can improve adoption, effectiveness, and scalability.

Location & Work Arrangement: This hybrid role requires four days per week in the office and one remote workday. Candidates must live in, or be willing to relocate on their own to one the listed locations.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without employer sponsorship.

In addition to the salary range, this role is also eligible for bonus or incentive opportunities.

What you have


To ensure that we fulfill our promise of “challenging the status quo,” this role has specific qualifications that successful candidates should have.

Required qualifications

  • 3+ years of professional software development, application development, automation engineering, or related experience, including at least 1 year of hands-on experience developing solutions with Microsoft Power Platform or Microsoft Copilot Studio.
  • Hands-on experience developing AI agents, automated workflows, or AI-enabled applications using Microsoft Power Platform.
  • Experience developing advanced solutions in Microsoft Copilot Studio, including custom agents, plugins, actions, or orchestration patterns.
  • Experience with Power Automate and Dataverse, including data models, tables, security structures, and integrations, as well as custom connectors or related Microsoft development capabilities.
  • Software development or computer science foundation with the ability to write, review, troubleshoot, and improve code.
  • Experience translating business requirements into scalable solution architectures and production-ready designs.
  • Experience integrating applications or workflows with APIs, connectors, approved data sources, or enterprise systems.
  • Experience owning solutions through design, development, testing, documentation, deployment, monitoring, and production support.
  • Experience troubleshooting production solutions through log analysis, issue remediation, and operational support.
  • Ability to collaborate across business, technology, and control teams and communicate technical decisions clearly.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience delivering AI, automation, internal application, or case-management solutions in a production environment.
  • Proficiency with Python, C#, or another modern programming language used for AI, automation, integration, or data engineering.
  • Experience designing solutions that incorporate controls, traceability, testing, human review, and responsible handling of sensitive data.
  • Experience in financial services, financial crimes, fraud, anti-money laundering, risk, compliance, or another regulated environment.

Job.JobTitle: Consultant II, Technology 3rd Party Risk Management - Tax Transformation
Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

The Deloitte Tax LLP's (Deloitte Tax) Tax Transformation Office (TTO) is pivotal to supporting Deloitte Tax client service delivery by optimizing end-to-end business processes and utilizing technology across all Tax offerings. This methodology improves efficiency in service delivery and encourages growth. The Senior Consultant - Technology Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) role offers an opportunity to be part of an innovative team within Deloitte Tax, focused on delivering value consistent with the Deloitte brand.

At Deloitte, we guide clients through the complex and evolving field of tax transformation. Through a broad suite of integrated tax services, we generate greater impact for clients. Our approach merges advanced technology and tax expertise to provide insights and smarter solutions, supporting clients to navigate a rapidly changing global environment.

Recruiting for this role ends on May 31, 2027

Work you'll do

The Consultant II - Technology Third Party Risk Management role in the Tax Transformation Office requires hands-on understanding of professional services, models for third-party relationships, and relevant technologies. In this position, you will collaborate across different tax offerings, engaging with Business Leaders and professionals from multiple Risk Review teams. Key responsibilities include managing a portfolio of technology vendors, software platforms, and strategic alliance partners by supporting the creation of new third-party relationships as Deloitte Tax pursues strategic growth initiatives.

Responsibilities include:

  • Executing TPRM review activities - coordinating intake, gathering and organizing due diligence documentation (such as security questionnaires and SOC reports), and tracking reviews through completion for new and renewing vendors under the guidance of senior team members.
  • Maintaining the vendor risk register and tracking dashboards - keeping records accurate and current, and preparing status updates on in-progress reviews, escalations, and remediation actions for team leads.
  • Serving as a day-to-day contact for routine TPRM process questions - responding to standard inquiries from business sponsors and vendor managers, and escalating more complex or judgment-based questions to senior team members.
  • Coordinating with Independence, Risk, Legal (OGC), Vendor Cyber, Confidentiality & Privacy, and Procurement teams - gathering required inputs, following up on outstanding items, and helping ensure consistent application of established policies and procedures.
  • Supporting process improvement efforts - surfacing friction points observed during reviews and contributing to improvements in tooling, documentation standards, and workflows.
  • Contributing to broader TTO Strategic Technology Services initiatives - assisting with vendor portfolio tracking, alliance program operations, and other activities that support the team's objectives.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Strong communicator who can tailor messages for technical and non-technical audiences and keep stakeholders informed and aligned.
  • Collaborative relationship builder who works effectively across functions and levels to drive consensus and move work forward.
  • Adaptable, self-directed problem solver who can manage shifting priorities, multiple workstreams, and competing deadlines.
  • Confident facilitator who influences without authority, resolves routine issues, and escalates effectively when needed.

The Team

Deloitte Tax LLP's Tax Transformation Office (TTO) is responsible for the design, development, and deployment of innovative, enterprise technology, tools, and standard processes to support the delivery of tax services. The TTO team focuses on enhancing Deloitte Tax LLP's ability to deliver comprehensive, value-added, and efficient tax services to our clients. The TTO Strategic Technology Services team is responsible for the enablement of standard technology to support Tax service delivery and developing technology to facilitate these services. TTO is focused on expanding Deloitte Tax capacity to deliver efficient, value-added Tax services to clients.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Ability to perform job responsibilities within a hybrid work model that requires US Tax professionals to co-locate in person 2 – 3 days per week
  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Information Systems, Computer Science or other relevant discipline
  • 1+ years' experience in transformation, consulting, strategic program delivery, or vendor/third-party management.
  • Hands-on experience managing the TPRM or equivalent vendor risk lifecycle end-to-end – including due diligence, risk assessment, and stakeholder alignment.
  • Demonstrated familiarity with risk and compliance frameworks – TPRM, SOC 2, or similar.
  • Limited immigration sponsorship may be available.
  • Ability to travel up to 10%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve
  • One of the following active accreditations obtained:
    • Licensed CPA in state of practice/primary office if eligible to sit for the CPA
    • If not CPA eligible:
      • Licensed Attorney
      • Enrolled Agent
      • CBAP® - Certified Business Analysis Professional
      • Certified in Risk and Information System Controls (CRISC)
      • Microsoft Azure
      • Project Management Professional (PMP)

Preferred:

  • Experience in a tax, financial services, or professional services environment, with exposure to third-party risk, vendor management, or related compliance processes.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to tailor messages for both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Proven stakeholder management, listening, and facilitation skills, including the ability to build alignment across diverse teams and levels.
  • Broad awareness of technology tools, platforms, and emerging capabilities, with the ability to assess practical fit to business needs.
  • Experience supporting business process improvement, transformation, or technology-enabled change initiatives.
  • Prior consulting or professional services experience, and/or relevant certifications such as PMP, CTPRM, or similar.

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $76,600 to $157,000.

Deloitte is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities. If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the recruiting process, please direct your inquiries to the Global Call Center (GCC) at USTalentCICInbox@deloitte.com.

Recruiting tips

From developing a stand out resume to putting your best foot forward in the interview, we want you to feel prepared and confident as you explore opportunities at Deloitte. Check out recruiting tips from Deloitte recruiters.

Benefits

At Deloitte, we know that great people make a great organization. We value our people and offer employees a broad range of benefits. Learn more about what working at Deloitte can mean for you.

Our people and culture

Our inclusive culture empowers our people to be who they are, contribute their unique perspectives, and make a difference individually and collectively. It enables us to leverage different ways of thinking, ideas, and perspectives, and bring more creativity and innovation to help solve our clients' most complex challenges. This makes Deloitte one of the most rewarding places to work.

Our purpose

Deloitte's purpose is to make an impact that matters for our people, clients, and communities. At Deloitte, purpose is synonymous with how we work every day. It defines who we are. Our purpose comes through in our work with clients that enables impact and value in their organizations, as well as through our own investments, commitments, and actions across areas that help drive positive outcomes for our communities. Learn more.

Professional development

From entry-level employees to senior leaders, we believe there's always room to learn. We offer opportunities to build new skills, take on leadership opportunities and connect and grow through mentorship. From on-the-job learning experiences to formal development programs, our professionals have a variety of opportunities to continue to grow throughout their career.

As used in this posting, "Deloitte" means Deloitte Tax LLP, a subsidiary of Deloitte LLP. Please see https://www.deloitte.com/us/about for a detailed description of the legal structure of Deloitte LLP and its subsidiaries. Certain services may not be available to attest clients under the rules and regulations of public accounting.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or protected veteran status, or any other legally protected basis, in accordance with applicable law.

Qualified applicants with criminal histories, including arrest or conviction records, will be considered for employment in accordance with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, City of Los Angeles's Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, and the California Fair Chance Act. Job ID360370

University Operations:

University Operations at UCF is committed to creating a supportive and welcoming environment for our faculty, staff, students, and the broader community. We take pride in delivering exceptional service, sharing our expertise, and upholding the highest standards to ensure a world-class campus experience.

Visit our website or follow us on Facebook and Instagram to learn more.

The Opportunity:

University Operations is seeking IT Client Support Specialist Is to join their team. In this role, you'll serve as a front-line technical resource for UCF's faculty, staff, and students — resolving hardware and software issues, supporting endpoint technologies, and delivering a high-quality client experience both remotely and in the field across campus.


Beyond day-to-day troubleshooting, you'll contribute to a mature IT service delivery environment — supporting formal incident, request, and problem management processes, building knowledge base documentation, and serving as a lead resource at the student walk-up support location. If you're someone who enjoys getting hands-on, staying mobile, and making a real difference for the people you support, this is your opportunity to do meaningful work at one of the nation's most innovative public research universities.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide technical support for hardware, software, operating systems, and university technology services through multiple support channels, including phone, email, remote, desk-side, and walk-up assistance.
  • Install, configure, maintain, upgrade, diagnose, and repair desktops, laptops, workstations, peripherals, and related equipment across Windows, macOS, and Linux environments.
  • Deploy and support operating systems, software applications, and endpoint configurations.
  • Troubleshoot hardware, software, and network connectivity issues using diagnostic and testing tools, escalating complex problems as needed.
  • Utilize enterprise management tools such as MECM, Intune, Entra, Active Directory, Jamf, DHCP, and vulnerability management platforms to support endpoint management and client computing services.
  • Document, track, and manage incidents, requests, and resolutions in ServiceNow while following established ticketing and communication procedures.
  • Support Change, Request, Incident, and Problem Management processes in accordance with UCF IT and departmental standard operating procedures.
  • Create and maintain knowledge base articles, technical documentation, and support resources to improve service delivery and promote self-service solutions.
  • Educate and assist clients in the effective use of hardware, software, and university systems.
  • Coordinate with vendors and vendor escalation teams to troubleshoot issues, process vendor support tickets, and obtain replacement components when necessary.
  • Communicate effectively with clients, university stakeholders, UCF IT Infrastructure leadership, and external vendors to ensure timely issue resolution.
  • Monitor and achieve established service levels, objectives, key results (OKRs), and performance metrics, contributing to vulnerability remediation and overall service quality.
  • Serve as part of a mission-essential team, remaining available for emergency response and occasional after-hours, weekend, holiday, or campus-closure support.
  • Transport and relocate computer equipment and materials as needed.
  • Provide functional direction and guidance to support staff, liaisons, and consultants to ensure consistent and timely delivery of IT support services.
  • Perform other duties as assigned, including temporarily providing supervisory support during supervisor absences or operational needs.

Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma or Equivalent and 4+ years of relevant experience or a Bachelor's degree and 0+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience providing technical support in a customer service-focused environment, with strong communication, problem-solving, and client service skills.
  • Familiarity with enterprise endpoint management tools such as Microsoft Intune, MECM, Entra ID, Active Directory, or Jamf Pro, as well as vulnerability management platforms (e.g., Tenable, Qualys).
  • Experience supporting mixed operating system environments (Windows, macOS, Linux) in an enterprise or higher-education setting, including direct support to students, faculty, or staff.
  • Familiarity with IT service management practices and tools such as ServiceNow.
  • Experience diagnosing and resolving hardware and software issues using standard technical or network diagnostic tools.
  • Working knowledge of networking fundamentals, including troubleshooting DHCP, DNS, VPN connectivity, and basic routing and switching concepts.
  • Experience developing user-facing documentation, knowledge base articles, or contributing to IT service improvements.
  • Demonstrated ability to meet service expectations in a ticketing environment while managing multiple priorities and maintaining attention to detail.
  • Experience coordinating with vendors, including escalating support cases, communicating with manufacturers, and managing warranty or repair processes.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

Position requires a valid Class E driver's license. The position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.


UCF IT is a critical service to the university, and there may be times when work extends beyond standard business hours, including evenings or weekends (on-call) to support projects or respond to impacts from emergencies on campus.


The anticipated hourly rate range for this position is $20.29 - $20.89. The final rate will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.


UCF is seeking to fill multiple roles for IT Client Support Specialist I. Candidates for this job posting will be considered for additional vacancies in this department.


Are you ready to unleash YOUR potential?

As a next-generation public research university and Forbes-ranked top employer in Florida, we are a community of thinkers, doers, creators, innovators, healers, and leaders striving to create broader prosperity and help shape a better future. No matter what your role is, when you join Knight Nation, you'll play an integral role at one of the most impactful universities in the country. You'll be met with opportunities to connect and collaborate with talented faculty, staff, and students across 12 colleges and multiple campuses, engaging in impactful work that makes a positive difference. Your time at UCF will provide you with many meaningful opportunities to grow, you'll work alongside talented colleagues on complex projects that will challenge you and help you gain new skills, and you'll have countless rewarding experiences that go well beyond a paycheck.

Working at UCF has its perks! UCF offers:

  • Benefit packages, including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Flexible Spending, and Employee Assistance Program
  • Paid time off, including annual and sick time off and paid holidays
  • Retirement savings options
  • Employee discounts, including tickets to many Orlando attractions
  • Education assistance
  • And more…For more benefits information, view the UCF Employee Benefits Guide.

Dive into our Total Rewards Calculator to discover the diverse selection available to you, giving you a glimpse into the benefits that together shape your comprehensive rewards package at UCF.

Unless explicitly stated on the job posting, it is UCF's expectation that an employee of UCF will reside in Florida as of the date the employment begins.

The University Operations division at UCF is committed to creating a supportive and welcoming environment for our faculty, staff, students, and the broader community. We take pride in delivering exceptional service, sharing our expertise, and upholding the highest standards to ensure a world-class campus experience.

Visit our website or follow us on Facebook and Instagram to learn more.


The Opportunity:

At the UCF Police Department, safety is our top priority. Our mission is to help ensure that students, faculty, staff, and visitors can both be safe and feel safe every day. Whether you are starting your career in public safety or bringing valuable experience from another field, you'll join a dedicated team that values professionalism, teamwork, and service to others. If you're looking for a rewarding career where every shift presents an opportunity to make a positive impact, we invite you to become part of the UCF Police Department family.


The Law Enforcement Analyst is a specialized non-sworn law enforcement position collecting, organizing, evaluating and analyzing criminal intelligence information for law enforcement purposes for the University of Central Florida Police Department.


Responsibilities:

  • Collects, organizes, evaluates, analyzes and coordinates criminal and intelligence information for the development and dissemination of criminal intelligence products, to include charts, trend reports and briefing information.
  • Reviews all pertinent intelligence information and public information sources on criminal elements to develop tactical and strategic intelligence.
  • Correlates new information with existing criminal intelligence already stored in manual and computerized systems.
  • Prepares intelligence reports, link charts, association matrices, bulletins, as well as other specialized reports and graphic presentations.
  • Prepares and presents briefings to the University of Central Florida Police Department and other law enforcement agencies on the findings or conclusions from the criminal intelligence analysis.
  • Assists in the management of major case investigations by assembling, collating, coordinating and analyzing reports, data and evidence, as well as projecting trends. Assists in planning, prioritizing and implementing the intelligence collection for pertinent crime trends or groups.
  • Performs frequent quality control checks of the intelligence database. Reviews and purges intelligence files by going through each file, recommending the file either be purged or updated. Provides the necessary documentation to update files.
  • Provides background and criminal history research assistance for internal staff and external agencies.
  • Performs other related work as required and/or directed.

Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma or Equivalent and 2+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) or Application of Network Analysis to Criminal Analysis law enforcement analyst (ANACAPA) certification.
  • Bachelor's degree in criminal justice, criminology, psychology, analysis strategies, or associated area; or four years of experience as a crime analyst.
  • Ability to collaborate in a team environment.
  • Experience in threat management.
  • Knowledge of the law enforcement field.
  • Experience in generating detailed reports, public speaking, and presentations.
  • Experience in data research and analytics.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Suite.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to organize, prioritize, and reach closure on multi-functional tasks.

Additional Application Materials Required:

Along with your application, please submit a resume, a cover letter, and copies of any applicable certifications.


Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated hourly range for this position is $28.73 ($60,000 annual salary) to $31.13 ($65,000 annual salary). The final rate will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • Must pass an extensive law enforcement background investigation, including, but not limited to, a psychological and physical exam, drug testing, and Computer Voice Stress Analysis.
  • Position requires a valid Class E driver's license. This position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.
  • May be required to work outside the normal work schedule for special events and campus emergencies.
  • If you are selected as the final candidate for an employment opportunity, both your position and salary will be significantly based upon the information that you have provided in your application for employment. We urge you to please take the time to complete the application in its entirety.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.

Job.JobDescription:
Access and Community Engagement/TRiO Programs:

The Upward Bound Project EDGE (Exploration and Determination Guarantees Excellence) program is designed to provide opportunities for fundamental support to participants in their preparation for college entrance. The goal is to increase the rate at which participants complete high school education and graduate from institutions of post-secondary (college, technical) education. Our goal is to recruit participants into the Upward Bound program, retain them, graduate them, and get them ready for post-secondary education admittance and graduation.

The Opportunity:

UCF's TRiO Programs Project EDGE is seeking an Academic Support Coordinator II to work with high school students in grades 9-12 at Edgewater High School. The position will be responsible for providing academic advising services to participants in order to encourage and facilitate high school completion, postsecondary enrollment options such as college, vocational and career academy.

The ideal candidate is a self-starter who thrives on building relationships, engaging with students and families, and creating supportive pathways to success. We especially welcome candidates who are energized by helping others, connecting people to resources, and making a lasting difference in students' futures.

Responsibilities:

  • Delivers services to program participants both virtually and in-person at Edgewater High School (EHS), ensuring comprehensive support in alignment with program goals. Collaborates with the Manager to meet internal objectives and improve service delivery.
  • Tracks students' academic progress, including advising, course selection, and graduation requirements, while developing and monitoring Individual Academic Plans (IAPs). Reviews report cards and academic performance to create tailored academic success plans for students.
  • Designs and delivers a college readiness curriculum, including workshops on college access, financial literacy, career exploration, and family engagement. Researches and stays updated on higher education trends to enhance evidence-based decision-making for student success.
  • Maintains accurate student records, updates participation data in the Blumen database, and documents student involvement in project services. Analyzes data and generates monthly reports to inform the Manager of program progress and areas for improvement.
  • Coordinates and participates in academic, social, and cultural events such as college tours, community service, and leadership activities. Develops and supervises the student leadership committee to enhance student engagement and personal development.
  • Assists in planning and executing both the academic year and summer programs to ensure high-quality student experiences. Develops and distributes a monthly program newsletter to keep students and parents informed of upcoming opportunities and achievements.
  • Implements recruitment, orientation, interviews, and intake processes to enroll the required number of students as mandated by the Department of Education. Establishes and maintains relationships with target schools, community stakeholders, and families to support outreach efforts.
  • Other duties as assigned by the Manager and/or Director.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 2+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior experience with TRiO other federally funded student support programs.
  • Experience working with high school-aged students in a classroom setting or additional student support services.
  • Background in teaching, academic advising, guidance counseling, or youth development.
  • Experience designing and facilitating workshops, presentations, or college readiness programming.
  • Familiarity with student information systems such as Blumen or Skyward.
  • Ability to add initiative and creativity to support the goals of the program.

Additional Application Materials Required:

In addition to your application, please include a resume. When applying please have all your documents ready to upload at the same time. Once the submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H 1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This is a Contracts & Grants (C&G) funded position. Employment is subject to availability of funding and may cease at the time funding for this employment is depleted.
  • This position requires a Level 2 Background Check through the Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) Clearinghouse prior to employment. For more information, please visit the FDLE Clearinghouse: https://info.flclearinghouse.com
  • Position requires a valid Class E driver's license. This position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.
  • This position requires the successful candidate to work on-site across two locations: UCF's Main Campus and Edgewater High School. The selected candidate must be available and willing to perform duties at both sites as required by the operational needs of the role.
  • Classification Title: Academic Support Coordinator II

This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.
