Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

Deloitte is seeking a Lead Managed Services Engineer II to design, automate, and operate enterprise-scale cloud capabilities that support clients' critical cyber assets. In this role, you will apply Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Terraform, infrastructure as code, and DevOps practices to build secure, scalable, and reliable solutions. You will collaborate with Cyber Operate, data engineering, and artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) teams to support evolving client needs, operational excellence, and secure cloud delivery.

Recruiting for this role ends on 12/31/2026.

Work you'll do

As a Lead Managed Services Engineer II on the Cyber Operate team, you will be responsible for:

  • Design, build, and maintain Terraform modules and infrastructure-as-code workflows across development, test, staging, and production environments.
  • Provision and operate Google Cloud Platform (GCP) services, including Cloud Run, BigQuery, Cloud Storage, Firestore, Identity and Access Management (IAM), Secret Manager, Google Cloud Load Balancing, Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), virtual private clouds (VPCs), subnets, firewall rules, private connectivity, Domain Name System (DNS), and Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) certificates.
  • Develop continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, infrastructure versioning, automated code-review processes, governance controls, and deployment strategies for infrastructure and applications.
  • Implement monitoring, alerting, logging, observability, high availability, and disaster recovery practices; investigate production incidents and document root-cause findings.
  • Create operational runbooks, architecture documentation, and support procedures for managed cloud environments.
  • Partner with data engineering and AI/ML teams to support infrastructure for data platforms and AI workloads, including Vertex AI Agent Engine, Vertex AI Search, and Model Armor.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
  • Ability to lead projects or workstreams
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Ability to mentor and provide clear guidance to others

The team

Our Cyber Operate offering Operates clients' critical cyber assets as a fully managed service or working in partnership with clients. Provides talent, leading technologies, and processes to operate client cyber capabilities, including the identity lifecycle, security operations, threat intelligence, application security business transformation, and continuous compliance.

Qualifications

Required 6+ years of experience in:

  • Experience with Terraform module development and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) infrastructure provisioning across development, test, staging, and production environments.
  • Experience configuring Cloud Run, BigQuery, Cloud Storage, Firestore, Secret Manager, Google Cloud Load Balancing, Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), Identity and Access Management (IAM), virtual private clouds (VPCs), subnets, firewall rules, private connectivity, Domain Name System (DNS), and Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) certificates.
  • Experience developing continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines with Cloud Build or GitHub Actions for infrastructure and application deployments, including version control, code review, and deployment processes.
  • Experience using Cloud Monitoring for monitoring, alerting, logging, and observability; production incident investigation; operational runbook development; and architecture documentation.
  • Experience building application programming interfaces (APIs) or data connectors using Python, Cloud Functions, or Cloud Run; and supporting data platforms using BigQuery, Dataflow, Pub/Sub, Cloud Storage, or Cloud Composer.
  • Experience supporting infrastructure for Vertex AI Agent Engine, Vertex AI Search, or Model Armor.
  • Experience configuring IAM policies, service accounts, and security controls for cloud infrastructure.
  • You must reside within a commutable distance of your assigned office with the ability to commute daily, if required, without the need for overnight accommodations.
  • You can expect to co-locate on average 1 day/week times a week with variations based on types of work/projects and client locations.
  • Ability to travel 20-25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
  • Limited immigration sponsorship may be available.

Preferred:

  • Master's degree

* Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
* Ability to meet deadlines

The team

AI & Engineering leverages cutting-edge engineering capabilities to build, deploy, and operate integrated/verticalized sector solutions in software, data, AI, network, and hybrid cloud infrastructure. Job.CompanyName: Embassy Suites Orlando - Lake Buena Vista South
Job.JobTitle: Front Desk Agent - Embassy Suites by Hilton Orlando LBV South
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Front Desk Agent / Concierge, Hospitality / Tourism / Events
Job.JobDescription:
We are currently accepting applications for an energetic, experienced Front Desk Agent to join the team here at Embassy Suites Orlando Lake Buena Vista South. Our award-winning property is 300 suites with 40,000 sq. ft. of meeting, pre-function, and event space. We have a highly experienced management team, which runs this very busy hotel and convention center in an exceptional manner with high standards, expectations, and strong results orientation.

Scope of Position

The Front Desk Agent is responsible for a professional, yet personal and efficient check-in and check-out for each guest of the resort. He/she will process all payments according to established resort requirements and provide information to guests, as well as visitor inquiries in person or via telephone. In addition, the Front Desk Agent is expected to complete daily checklists and always demonstrate professional courtesy.

Position Requirements

  • One (1) year experience in a Hotel Front Desk position.
  • Outstanding guest service skills.
  • Able to handle a multitude of tasks in an ever-changing environment.
  • Effective at listening to, understanding, clarifying, and responding to the concerns and issues raised by guests and members.
  • Experience with cash handling, including but not limited to guidelines set forth regarding PCI Compliance.

Primary Responsibilities

  • To be friendly, courteous, and helpful to all individuals, both guest and non-guest.
  • To look after the wellbeing of every guest and take personal responsibility in solving the guest's problems – to ensure a memorable experience.
  • To be able to check-in and checkout guests in a timely, accurate and courteous manner.
  • To command a good working knowledge of the PeP system.
  • To command a working knowledge of the rates, size, layout, bed types and special features of all guest suites.
  • To command a working knowledge of all special rates/packages – requirements, restrictions, special arrangements, services/amenities included.
  • To command a working knowledge of all daily report that needs to be completed.
  • To be aware and familiar with all VIPs, meetings, functions, and conventions in the hotel.
  • To be familiar with the departments in the hotel– their functions.
  • To acquire in-depth knowledge of Hotel services/facilities and major attractions in the vicinity and Orlando area.
  • To learn and practice proper telephone procedures – how to answer phones, place calls, or transfer calls.
  • Be able to work different shifts and/or functions to accommodate business demands.
  • Follow standard operating procedures and adhere to rules and regulation of the Front Desk and the Hotel.
  • To be familiar with the handling of guest mail, messages, and/or packages.
  • To be familiar with the Safe Deposit Box policies and procedures.
  • To assume any additional responsibilities as assigned by the Front Office Manager and Assistant Front Office Manager.
  • To keep a positive attitude and seek pleasure out of assisting others.
  • Maintains and adheres to our company values.
  • Adhere to company cash handling policies.

Education

  • High school diploma or GED or degree in Hospitality related major.

Skills and Abilities

  • Able to communicate in the English language. Second language is a plus.
  • Able to work flexible schedules including holidays and weekends and able to perform multiple tasks.
  • Experience using software programs such as Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, and Outlook).
  • Proficient in PeP (or similar program).

Physical Requirements

  • On a continuous basis, stand at a desk for long periods of time in front of a computer screen. Also requires walking/reaching and bending throughout shift.
  • Must be physically fit to lift, pull, and push items up to 50 pounds.

The statement in this job descriptions are intended to describe the essential nature and level of work being performed. They are not intended to be ALL responsibilities or qualifications of the job.

Job.JobTitle: Cyber Operate Manager - IAM PBAC Architect/Engineer
Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

Deloitte's Cyber Operate offering helps organizations operate and evolve critical cyber capabilities, including identity and access management. As a Lead Managed Services Engineer II, you will lead the design, implementation, and evolution of policy-based access control (PBAC) and broader identity and access management (IAM) solutions for large, highly regulated client environments. You will combine hands-on engineering with technical leadership to strengthen security, support regulatory compliance, and help clients manage access at scale.

Work you'll do

As a Lead Managed Services Engineer II on the Cyber Operate team, you will be responsible for…

  • Lead the design, implementation, and ongoing enhancement of PBAC and IAM solutions for complex, regulated client environments.
  • Translate business and security requirements into IAM architectures, controls, implementation plans, and technology roadmaps.
  • Build and maintain automated provisioning, de-provisioning, and access-control workflows.
  • Assess IAM controls and vulnerabilities, troubleshoot access issues, and lead root-cause remediation that minimizes business disruption.
  • Lead technical workstreams, maintain IAM documentation, deliver enablement on IAM policies and procedures, and mentor team members.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

Position Summary

Join Deloitte as a Lead Managed Services Engineer II and help design, engineer, and deploy identity security capabilities across enterprise environments. You will advance attack path analysis, identity threat protection, authentication modernization, policy-based access control (PBAC), and identity-driven attack containment. Working across cybersecurity, infrastructure, engineering, architecture, product, and vendor teams, you will deliver scalable solutions using Sgnl.ai, PlainID, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), and CrowdStrike Identity Protection. This role combines identity and access management (IAM) architecture, Zero Trust, and product engineering to help clients reduce risk, strengthen resilience, and improve access experiences. This role may require work outside standard business hours based on business needs.

As a Lead Managed Services Engineer II on the Cyber Operate team, you will be responsible for:

  • Lead product engineering and deployment for Sgnl.ai, PlainID, CrowdStrike Identity Protection, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), and authentication and authorization platforms.
  • Expand attack path analysis, identity threat detection, risk scoring, and identity-driven attack containment to address identity-based attack vectors, privilege escalation paths, lateral movement, and access risks.
  • Advance authentication services, including authenticator capabilities and access-experience improvements, alongside adaptive access, PBAC, identity-aware authorization, and risk-based access decisions using identity intelligence and continuous verification.

Required:

  • Experience engineering, integrating, and operationalizing Sgnl.ai, PlainID, CrowdStrike Identity Protection, and Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) across enterprise applications and infrastructure.
  • Experience applying Zero Trust Architecture, identity threat detection and response (ITDR), attack path analysis, authorization frameworks, PBAC, and risk-based authentication; integrating platforms using application programming interfaces (APIs), identity protocols, automation, and cloud-native architectures.
  • You must reside within a commutable distance of your assigned office with the ability to commute daily, if required, without the need for overnight accommodations.

  • Master's degree.

Job Description:


The civil engineer performs technical work in various phases of a computerized traffic control system operations center (TMC). The primary task for this position is for the specific implementation and modification of signal timing plans for the signal systems controlled by the city. Performs modifications and upgrades to traffic signal controller databases using system software (Cubic/Trafficware's ATMS.now) and traffic modeling using Cubic/Trafficware's Synchro and Tru-Traffic software among others. Conducts field investigations of traffic conditions associated with traffic signals for the purpose of adjusting traffic signal timing plans both on a regular schedule and in response to citizen inquiries. Works closely with the Traffic Signal Maintenance section to update traffic signal timing plans when hardware must be changed and works closely with regional traffic signal timing consultants working on annual corridor re-timing projects. Works closely with FDOT's Signal Timing Groupe at the RTMC for timing-plans and database updates. Work assignments are received from a professional supervisor who defines the scope of the work to be performed. Timing Engineer is expected to plan details of work and make technical decisions. Work is reviewed while in progress and upon completion.



Minimum Qualifications:


Civil Engineer I: Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering, plus six (6) months of experience in Transportation Engineering required; or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience. A valid Florida Driver's License is required.

Civil Engineer II: Same as Civil Engineer I, above, except requires two (2) years of experience as identified.

Civil Engineer III: Same as Civil Engineer II, above, except requires four (4) years of experience as identified, including at least two (2) years of experience in transportation development review, traffic studies, or crash data analysis required; or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience. One year of supervisory experience desired.

Civil Engineer IV: Same as Civil Engineer III, above, except requires Registration as P.E. in the State of Florida required.

Job.JobTitle: ConvergeHEALTH Life Sciences - Product Forward Deployed Engineer - Products & Platforms _CMAT
Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

The Team

The Innovation & Delivery Transformation (I&DT) team is building the future of Deloitte's business through new AI-native platforms and products. The team is responsible for identifying, nurturing, scaling, and winning in new markets through new capabilities. Rather than relying on what the firm has historically done, I&DT looks ahead and invests in areas where growth is expected three, five, and ten years into the future.

This role is aligned to the Converge for Life Sciences portfolio, Deloitte's AI-enabled platform portfolio for the modern life sciences enterprise. Converge by Deloitte combines proprietary data assets, advanced analytics, and AI-driven decision intelligence to help pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical product organizations accelerate the pace of discovery, development, and commercialization, while improving compliance and operational visibility across the enterprise.

This role is 100% dedicated to FastForward. Fast Forward is a flagship offering within this portfolio that supports commercial field operations for pharmaceutical organizations.

Position Summary

As a Product Forward Deployed Engineer (pFDE), this role is the technical engine of the FastForward pre-sales cycle. Working across Product Management, Engineering, Account, and Pursuit teams, and in close partnership with the FastForward Sales Executive, the pFDE builds and leads product demonstrations, proves technical fit and feasibility, and translates client workflows into credible solution approaches that move opportunities from qualification through proof of value.

Recruiting for this role ends on 11/30/2026.

Work you'll do

We're seeking a seasoned Senior Consultant Product Forward Deployed Engineer (pFDE) to own the technical side of the FastForward pre-sales cycle. This is an experienced individual-contributor role for someone who operates independently: building and running product demonstrations end to end, shaping solutions directly with clients and internal teams, and raising the technical quality of every FastForward pursuit. Success is measured by technical wins, demonstration quality, and the strength of the pursuits it enables. Day to day, the pFDE will have the following key responsibilities:

Pre-Sales Discovery & Technical Qualification:

  • Lead technical discovery sessions with prospective clients, alongside account, pursuit, and product teams, to understand commercial workflows, data, integration needs, and success criteria for Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud.
  • Independently qualify product fit and feasibility, distinguishing standard capability from client-specific customization, and help determine whether an opportunity stays product-led or is routed elsewhere.
  • Partner closely with the FastForward Sales Executive to shape opportunities, sequence pursuit milestones, and resolve technical objections throughout the sales cycle.

Product Demonstrations & Proofs of Concept

  • Build, own, and lead FastForward product demonstrations end to end, configuring demo environments, tailoring scenarios to the client's needs, and presenting them to both technical and business audiences.
  • Independently stand up and configure demo orgs and proof-of-concept environments.
  • Run fit-gap assessments and proof-of-value exercises that give prospects a credible, hands-on view of the platform before contracting.

Solution Shaping & Cross-Functional Support

  • Develop credible solution approaches and technical narratives in partnership with account, pursuit, product, and engineering teams.
  • Serve as the technical bridge between the field and the product organization, feeding client requirements, objections, and market signals back to Product Management and Engineering to inform the product roadmap.
  • Support account teams with technical inputs to proposals, scoping boundaries, and transition-to-delivery clarity so qualified opportunities hand off cleanly.

Reusable Assets & Enablement

  • Build reusable technical assets, reference configurations, and demo scripts from pursuit work so the team scales without rebuilding from scratch each time.
  • Develop go-to-market and strategic documentation that supports pursuit strategy and product positioning.
  • Share demonstration and technical best practices with newer pFDEs and pursuit-team members, raising the technical bar across FastForward pre-sales.

The successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Clear, audience-aware communication: explains technical concepts credibly to both technical and business stakeholders and tells a compelling product story in a live demo.
  • Strong organization and prioritization: manages multiple concurrent pursuits and demo builds at once, and sequences competing priorities well.
  • Collaborative, team-first mindset: works fluidly across Sales, Product Management, Engineering, Account, and Pursuit teams, and is comfortable being the connective tissue between the field and the product organization.
  • Self-directed ownership: drives demos and technical qualification end to end and moves work forward without needing close direction.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Life Sciences, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience defined as an additional 4+ years of relevant work experience in lieu of a degree.
  • 4+ years of professional experience in solution consulting, sales engineering, technical pre-sales, forward-deployed engineering, or comparable client-facing technical roles, with a demonstrated ability to operate independently.
  • Hands-on technical experience configuring or building on Salesforce (e.g., administrator-level configuration, flows, validation rules, and other declarative/point-and-click tools), sufficient to build and run product demonstrations without engineering support.
  • Experience independently building and delivering 5+ product demonstrations, proofs of concept, or comparable client-facing technical deliverables.
  • Experience supporting the pre-sales cycle, including technical discovery and translating client needs into solution approaches.
  • Demonstrated ability to distinguish standard product capability from custom work and to communicate that distinction clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong collaboration skills across Product Management, Engineering, Account, and Pursuit teams, including experience working directly with sales professionals in a pursuit setting.
  • Ability to travel 20-25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred:

  • Hands-on experience with Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud, Health Cloud, or Veeva CRM.
  • Prior hands-on experience in the client delivery and implementation of field force technology such as Veeva CRM, IQVIA OCE or Salesforce.
  • Experience with Salesforce Agentforce or comparable AI-agent / GenAI capabilities embedded in enterprise applications.
  • Experience in life sciences or healthcare commercial technology environments (e.g., CRM, field engagement, patient services, or market access).
  • Prior experience as a Managed Services Consultant leading full-cycle technology implementation projects, ideally within Life Sciences Commercial or Customer engagement platforms.
  • Prior experience stepping in after go-live to provide ongoing admin support, acting as the product specialist for clients already up
  • Experience building reusable demo assets, reference configurations, or accelerators for a product or pursuit team.
  • Familiarity with data loading, integration patterns, and CRM data models common to life sciences commercial operations, as well as CLI-based deployment or configuration-as-code approaches.

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

The Team

The Innovation & Delivery Transformation (I&DT) team is building the future of Deloitte's business through new AI-native platforms and products. The team is responsible for identifying, nurturing, scaling, and winning in new markets through new capabilities. Rather than relying on what the firm has historically done, I&DT looks ahead and invests in areas where growth is expected three, five, and ten years into the future.

Are you looking for a unique opportunity with both start-up spirit AND enterprise strength? Deloitte's Converge for FSI business offers both! We are looking for a talented Data Scientist to join the Converge for FSI team and help build differentiated, data-driven financial services products that achieve product-market fit. This is a great opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced analytics and financial services industry expertise, developing the models and insights that power Signals for FSI and future products in the Converge for FSI portfolio.

Position Summary

We are looking for a highly skilled and client-facing Engineering Lead to sit at the intersection of engineering excellence and customer partnership, supporting the Signals for FSI product. Signals is a proprietary set of data assets coupled with AI, data science, and statistical models that help our clients drive business growth and power decisions in a dynamic and changing market. You'll own the architecture decisions that turn this from a collection of prototypes into a real platform: a shared data pipeline and warehouse that any app in the suite can draw from, a common geospatial/demographic data layer that scales nationally. In this role, you will partner with our product & data science team to integrate new data sources and harden prototypes into applications based on client feedback. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role with direct influence on product direction. You will be part of the General Manager's leadership team, responsible for proactively bringing ideas that push the business forward, weighing in on key decisions, and helping junior resources across the team overcome hurdles. This is a build-it-for-real role for someone who's done this exact transition before — not scaling one app, but building the reusable foundation that lets a whole suite of client-facing products scale together.

Recruiting for this role ends on 12/1/2026.

Work you'll do

As the Engineering Lead, you will work at the intersection of data science, engineering, and financial services domain expertise to build and refine the data platforms, models, and analytics that power Signals for FSI:

  • Rapidly prototype and build POCs using financial services datasets and data models that demonstrate value in the context of a client's real-world use cases
  • Lead teams of onshore and offshore data engineers and application engineers to harden prototypes into production grade applications that satisfy the highly secure and regulated environments of financial services.
  • Collaborate with internal Product & Data fabric teams to integrate new data sources and design and build scalable, production-ready data pipelines and applications.
  • Partner with the Product team and client architects to translate financial services use cases into requirements, features, and application specifications.
  • Recognize and promote opportunities for reuse when designing prototypes and applications.
  • Evaluate data, model and application performance against business and regulatory considerations relevant to financial services and iterate based on findings.
  • Translate analytical findings into clear, business-relevant insights for Product, Sales, and client-facing teams to shape the technical go-to-market strategy.
  • Maintain a library of reusable demo assets, hardened applications, and reference implementations.
  • Stay current on emerging AI/ML techniques and financial services data trends, and evaluate their application to the Signals for FSI roadmap.
  • Produce high-quality technical documentation, runbooks, and integration guides.

The successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Experience in building data and insights products and pipelines that power insights and signals for business users to drive growth decisions.
  • Demonstrated ability to take a working prototype and re-architect it for production scale, cost, and reliability — not just incremental feature work
  • Exceptional written & verbal communicator — able to lead technical conversations with senior engineers and C-suite stakeholders alike; able to translate infrastructure tradeoffs for non-technical stakeholders
  • Proven experience designing and scaling geospatial/location-based data systems (spatial indexing, PostGIS, H3, or equivalent) — ability to replace client-side point-in-radius rendering with server-side spatial queries at scale
  • Strong background in ETL/data pipeline engineering — designing scheduled ingestion from third-party data vendors into a warehouse or lake (BigQuery, Snowflake, or equivalent)
  • Experience with Python/FastAPI (or comparable) backend development and React/TypeScript frontend development, sufficient to review and refactor both sides of a full-stack codebase
  • Hands-on experience with data security and PII handling — masking, access controls, and retention policy for datasets containing personal identifiers
  • Experience standing up CI/CD pipelines and container/Helm-based deployment from scratch
  • Familiarity with authentication/authorization platforms (OAuth2, enterprise SSO/gateway integration) and migrating services onto a shared platform auth layer
  • Genuine interest in and working knowledge of the financial services industry, with curiosity about how data translates into real client outcomes.
  • Exposure to Agentic AI frameworks, harnesses, and tooling — including LangGraph, LangChain, or similar orchestration frameworks
  • Practical understanding of LLM integration patterns, prompt engineering, and AI-powered application design
  • Strong analytical rigor paired with sound judgment about when a model is ready to ship versus needing further refinement.
  • Comfortable moving between hands-on technical work and clear communication with product, engineering, and business stakeholders.
  • Self-directed and organized, with the ability to manage multiple analytical workstreams at once.
  • Collaborative mindset and a willingness to partner closely with engineering and product teams to bring models into production.
  • Comfortable working through ambiguous, messy problems that require creativity and persistence.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.
  • 7+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years in a technical lead or architecture role
  • Ability to travel 10-25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred:

  • Advanced degree (Master's) in Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, Mathematics, or a related field.
  • 2+ years of experience working with financial services data (e.g., banking, capital markets, or insurance) or delivering analytics solutions to financial services clients.
  • Experience with cloud-based data and analytics platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure) in a financial services or other highly regulated industry context.
  • Familiarity with risk, fraud, credit, or customer analytics use cases within banking, capital markets, or insurance.
  • Experience with feature stores or ML feature engineering pipelines, particularly for on-demand/real-time scoring rather than static precomputed datasets
  • Background in financial services or another regulated industry, with working knowledge of data vendor licensing/compliance constraints (e.g., credit bureau or B2B data providers)
  • Experience with LLM/agent infrastructure (LangChain, LLM gateways) including cost monitoring and latency observability
  • Familiarity with FDIC, Census, or similar public geospatial/demographic datasets
  • Experience building internal developer platforms or paved-road tooling that other engineering teams consume
  • Prior experience taking a product from single-region/regional pilot to national or multi-region scale
  • Experience with observability stacks (e.g., Datadog, Grafana, OpenTelemetry) for both application and ML/LLM monitoring
  • Background in a startup, management consulting, commercial transformation, or enterprise technology product leadership, ideally with a data focus (e.g. Epsilon, TransUnion, Equifax, Experian, Axciom)

Job.JobTitle: Converge for FSI - Data Scientist, Signals for FSI_Products & Platforms
Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

The Team

The Innovation & Delivery Transformation (I&DT) team is building the future of Deloitte's business through new AI-native platforms and products. The team is responsible for identifying, nurturing, scaling, and winning in new markets through new capabilities. Rather than relying on what the firm has historically done, I&DT looks ahead and invests in areas where growth is expected three, five, and ten years into the future.

Are you looking for a unique opportunity with both start-up spirit AND enterprise strength? Deloitte's Converge for FSI business offers both! We are looking for a talented Data Scientist to join the Converge for FSI team and help build differentiated, data-driven financial services products that achieve product-market fit. This is a great opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced analytics and financial services industry expertise, developing the models and insights that power Signals for FSI and future products in the Converge for FSI portfolio.

Position Summary

Financial services data holds enormous, often-underused potential — and turning it into decisions the business can act on takes both rigorous technical craft and real industry fluency. As a Data Scientist on the Signals for FSI team, you'll build the analytical engine behind one of Converge for FSI's flagship products, working hands-on with real financial services data to develop models clients can trust. You'll do it on a team that pairs start-up speed with the scale and credibility of Deloitte, giving you room to experiment while your work reaches some of the most influential institutions in financial services.

Recruiting for this role ends on 12/1/2026.

Work you'll do

As the Data Scientist, you will work at the intersection of data science, product, and financial services domain expertise to build and refine the models and analytics that power Signals for FSI:

  • Develop, test, and refine statistical and machine learning models using financial services datasets (e.g., consumers, businesses, transactions, accounts, risk, or market data) to power Signals for FSI.
  • Partner with the Product team to translate financial services use cases into data requirements, features, data signals, and model specifications.
  • Conduct exploratory data analysis and validate data quality across structured and semi-structured financial services data sources.
  • Evaluate model performance against business and regulatory considerations relevant to financial services and iterate based on findings.
  • Translate analytical findings into clear, business-relevant insights for Product, Sales, and client-facing teams.
  • Stay current on emerging Statistical, AI/ML techniques and financial services data trends, and evaluate their application to the Signals for FSI roadmap.

The successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Genuine interest in and working knowledge of the financial services industry, with curiosity about how data translates into real client outcomes – early use cases are retail banking, investment and wealth management and insurance, but will expand over time.
  • Strong analytical rigor paired with sound judgment about when a signal or model is ready to ship versus needing further refinement.
  • Comfortable moving between hands-on technical work and clear communication with product, engineering, and business stakeholders.
  • Self-directed and organized, with the ability to manage multiple analytical workstreams at once.
  • Collaborative mindset and a willingness to partner closely with engineering and product teams to bring models into production.
  • Comfortable working through ambiguous, messy problems that require creativity and persistence.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.
  • 4+ years of experience in applied data science, machine learning, or statistical modeling, including hands-on model development and validation – proficient at using Python, SQL and other data transformation and analytical tools
  • Ability to travel 10-25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred:

  • Advanced degree (Master's) in Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, Mathematics, or a related field.
  • 2+ years of experience working with financial services data (e.g., banking, capital markets, investment management, or insurance) or delivering analytics solutions to financial services clients.
  • 2+ years of working with customer data to build audiences and segments for sales and marketing use cases.
  • Experience with cloud-based data and analytics platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure) in a financial services or other highly regulated industry context.
  • Experience with MCP servers and use of AI to analyze large data sets.

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $122,000-$240,500.

You may also be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.

Deloitte is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities. If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the recruiting process, please direct your inquiries to the Global Call Center (GCC) at USTalentCICInbox@deloitte.com.

Recruiting tips

From developing a stand out resume to putting your best foot forward in the interview, we want you to feel prepared and confident as you explore opportunities at Deloitte. Check out recruiting tips from Deloitte recruiters.

Benefits

At Deloitte, we know that great people make a great organization. We value our people and offer employees a broad range of benefits. Learn more about what working at Deloitte can mean for you.

Our people and culture

Our inclusive culture empowers our people to be who they are, contribute their unique perspectives, and make a difference individually and collectively. It enables us to leverage different ways of thinking, ideas, and perspectives, and bring more creativity and innovation to help solve our clients' most complex challenges. This makes Deloitte one of the most rewarding places to work.

Our purpose

Deloitte's purpose is to make an impact that matters for our people, clients, and communities. At Deloitte, purpose is synonymous with how we work every day. It defines who we are. Our purpose comes through in our work with clients that enables impact and value in their organizations, as well as through our own investments, commitments, and actions across areas that help drive positive outcomes for our communities. Learn more.

Professional development

From entry-level employees to senior leaders, we believe there's always room to learn. We offer opportunities to build new skills, take on leadership opportunities and connect and grow through mentorship. From on-the-job learning experiences to formal development programs, our professionals have a variety of opportunities to continue to grow throughout their career.

Job.JobTitle: Adjunct Faculty - Artificial Intelligence in Computer Science
Job.JobDescription:
If you're looking for the chance to learn, grow, and make a contribution to the community, look at employment opportunities with Full Sail University. You'll find your choice of career opportunities, great benefits, an environment that welcomes and values creativity, and a work experience that is both challenging and rewarding!

We are seeking Adjunct faculty to help deliver courses in the Computer Science Bachelor's — Artificial Intelligence Concentration. The program curriculum focuses on the skills to design, develop, and implement AI solutions. Faculty should possess knowledge and experience in topics such as machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and Human-AI interaction. Faculty in this program will develop and teach curriculum to educate students on the design, development, and implementation of software-based artificial intelligence solutions for the business, entertainment, and consumer markets. This position is part-time working no more than 20 hours per week, on-campus OR online, and must be a resident in the state of Florida.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Create an environment of learning through effective teaching skills, maintain student-centered focus, and stay current with relevant industry standards.
  • Utilize a variety of teaching strategies and encourage active learning.
  • Perform lectures for campus courses, and hold scheduled virtual course meetings for online courses. Teaching will be conducted through on-campus and online delivery.
  • Interact positively with diverse student populations; provide all students with equal opportunities for learning.
  • Demonstrate a commitment to the industry, maintain knowledge and skill relevancy through continuing education as defined in the faculty development plan.

Other Responsibilities:

  • Adheres to the policies and procedures of Full Sail University
  • Maintains strict confidentiality of student and company information
  • Demonstrates a strong commitment to the mission and values of the organization
  • Adheres to company attendance standards
  • Performs other duties as assigned

Supervisory Responsibilities: None

Competencies:

  • Strong organizational, analytical, and interpersonal skills
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including proofreading and editing for grammar and punctuation
  • Detail oriented
  • Ability to multi-task while working independently and collaboratively with other teachers and university staff
  • Ability to interact professionally and constructively with students and staff at all levels in an immersive, fast-paced environment

Education and/or Experience:

The ideal candidate must have a minimum of four (4) years related and verifiable work experience and are required to hold a Master's (preferred) or Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software or Computer Engineering, or related discipline from an accredited college or university.

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations:

  • N/A

Skills:

  • Strong working knowledge of software-based development, problem solving, principles, and applications.
  • Experience as a software developer, software engineer, programmer, etc.
  • Experience implementing AI in software preferred
  • Strong working knowledge of object-oriented design, and data structures and algorithms preferred
  • Experience in Agile software development preferred
  • Experience developing for multiple platforms preferred
  • Teaching or mentoring experience preferred
  • Proficiency using software programs such as MS Word, Excel, Keynote/PowerPoint and Outlook
  • Proficiency with programming languages such as C++, C#, Java, or Python preferred
  • Familiarity with integrated development environments like Visual Studio or the Anaconda suite preferred


Environmental Factors/Physical Demands:


Work is performed in an office and classroom environment. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to have the ability to maintain active student and employee communication; access, input and retrieve information from the computer system. May be subject to; bending, reaching, kneeling, stooping and lifting up to thirty (30) pounds.

Full Sail is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

The Opportunity:

The postdoctoral scholar with support a DARPA project focused on developing predictive pressure load models for external hypersonics aerodynamics. The postdoc will develop these data-informed models in collaboration with researchers at another university and an industry partner, and our own group at UCF. The postdoc will be responsible for rigorous model development, testing, and deployment to solve the demonstration problems. Postdoc will also write scientific journal articles, present novel research at technical conferences, attend collaborator meetings, and contribute to the quarterly project reports. To a lesser extent, the postdoc will help with mentoring of junior researchers in the group.

Minimum Qualifications:

Must have a Ph.D. in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering with experience with machine learning tools, Python, and end-to-end training paradigms. Past experience in high-speed aerodynamics.

Preferred Qualifications:

Multiphysics modeling experience focused on fluid-thermal-structural interactions. Prior work on developing generalizable and explainable ML models. Design of physics based loss functions in data-informed modeling frameworks. Direct experience with high-speed surface pressure models and panel methods.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr Rohit Deshmukh at Rohit.deshmukh@ucf.edu

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

University Audit:

UCF University Audit serves as the university's internal auditor, providing internal audits and reviews, management consulting and advisory services, investigations of fraud, waste, or abuse, follow-up on recommendations, evaluation of the processes of risk management and governance, and coordination with external auditors.

UCF University Audit reports administratively to the Office of the President and functionally to the Audit and Compliance Committee of the Board of Trustees. This reporting structure promotes independence and full consideration of audit recommendations and management action plans.

The Opportunity:

UCF University Audit is seeking an Audit Investigator III to conduct complex and sensitive investigations involving financial fraud, waste, abuse, employee misconduct, and violations of laws, regulations, rules, and university policies. This position independently manages investigations from initial complaint assessment and planning through evidence analysis, documentation, findings, and final reporting while helping promote accountability and safeguard university resources.

The ideal candidate will bring experience in financial fraud investigations, accounting, auditing, forensic accounting, compliance, law enforcement, or a related investigative field. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong analytical and investigative writing skills, discretion in handling sensitive information, and the ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with university stakeholders.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead complex and sensitive investigations involving alleged fraud, waste, abuse, employee misconduct, and violations of applicable laws, regulations, rules, and university policies.
  • Independently manage investigations from initial planning through interviews, evidence collection and analysis, documentation, findings, and final reporting.
  • Manage the intake and triage of complaints by assessing jurisdiction, investigative needs, risk, urgency, and the appropriate course of action.
  • Evaluate the potential applicability of the Florida Whistle-blower Act and coordinate with university stakeholders to support appropriate and consistent complaint resolution.
  • Prepare comprehensive investigative reports, workpapers, findings, and related correspondence in accordance with university procedures and professional standards.
  • Assist with reviewing investigative workpapers, managing assignments, and providing backup support to the investigations manager or associate director, as needed.
  • Maintain regular communication with team members and leadership regarding investigative progress, significant developments, and case resolution.
  • Support fraud awareness and prevention initiatives such as the UCF Fraud Risk Assessment Committee, guide University Audit interns, and participate in audits or consulting projects, as needed.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree and 4+ years of experience or an equivalent combination of related education and experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).
  • Must obtain Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) designation within one year of hire.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience conducting complex financial fraud, compliance, employee misconduct, or fraud, waste, and abuse investigations.
  • Experience applying accounting, auditing, forensic accounting, or financial analysis principles in an investigative environment.
  • Experience independently managing investigations from complaint assessment through findings and final reporting, including preparing investigative reports and professional correspondence.
  • Experience in preparing for, conducting, and documenting sensitive interviews and communicating with stakeholders at multiple organizational levels.
  • Experience using data analytics, case-management systems, audit software, or emerging technologies to support investigative work.
  • Experience working in higher education, government, the public sector, internal audit, corporate compliance, or another regulated environment.
  • Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, business administration, criminal justice, or a closely related field.

Job.JobTitle: Administrative Coordinator II, Strategic Operations and Engagement
Job.JobDescription:
Kenneth G. Dixon Career Development Center:

The Kenneth G. Dixon Career Development Center (DCDC) empowers UCF students to prepare now for what's next through transformative experiences, personalized guidance, and campus-to-career connections that turn career aspirations into reality.

DCDC serves as a comprehensive hub for career readiness at UCF, bringing together programs, services, technology, and partnerships that support students throughout their academic and career journeys. The center helps students explore career pathways, gain meaningful experiences, prepare for internships and employment, pursue graduate and professional education, and successfully transition beyond UCF.

Through collaboration with employers, faculty, staff, alumni, and campus and community partners, DCDC works to integrate career development throughout the student experience and build connections between education, experience, and lifelong career success.

The Opportunity:

UCF's Kenneth G. Dixon Career Development Center (DCDC) is seeking an Administrative Coordinator II to support the Strategic Operations and Engagement unit. At the DCDC, every operational decision matters — because behind every smooth process is a student whose career journey depends on it. This opportunity is a great fit for a motivated, service-minded professional eager to join a team dedicated to connecting students with the tools, resources, and experiences they need to thrive professionally. This is a role for someone who finds purpose in building environments where students and staff alike can do their best work. You'll be part of a collaborative, student-centered team where operational excellence and meaningful impact go hand in hand.

Responsibilities:

  • Supervise student employees supporting front desk and call center operations, including recruitment, hiring, onboarding, training, scheduling, coaching, performance evaluation, and daily work assignments. Develop staffing schedules to ensure appropriate service coverage and create meaningful opportunities for student employees to build professional and workplace skills.
  • Oversee daily front desk and call center service operations, establishing expectations for professional, responsive, and student-centered service. Maintain current scripts, FAQs, referral resources, escalation procedures, and information about DCDC programs, services, events, and university resources. Address routine service concerns and coordinate follow-up or escalation as needed.
  • Coordinate DCDC space reservations and scheduling for conference rooms, interview rooms, multipurpose spaces, and other shared facilities. Serve as a primary contact for reservation requests, maintain calendars and utilization records, coordinate room readiness and technology needs, resolve scheduling conflicts, and communicate reservation procedures to internal and external users.
  • Coordinate day-to-day facility and building support needs, including submitting and monitoring work orders, maintenance and repair requests, furniture and equipment needs, office moves, and other operational issues. Work with university partners such as Facilities, IT, Security, and Surplus Property to support effective building operations.
  • Support asset, inventory, and space management activities, including furniture moves, surplus property, equipment and asset tracking, room inventories, and routine review of shared and stakeholder-facing spaces. Coordinate with the designated Building Liaison on building-wide needs, accessibility accommodations, outages, emergency communications, and related activities.
  • Develop and maintain operational procedures and resources, including standard operating procedures, training materials, service guides, schedules, workflow documentation, reservation procedures, and other documentation that supports consistent operations and continuity of service.
  • Track and evaluate operational activity, including service inquiries, call and front desk volume, space utilization, staffing patterns, stakeholder feedback, and recurring operational issues. Identify trends and recommend process, technology, or workflow improvements that strengthen service delivery and operational efficiency.
  • Provide administrative and operational support for the center, including purchasing, travel, scheduling, meeting logistics, budget coordination, employment documentation, and other administrative functions.
  • Support cross-functional projects and strategic initiatives led by the Strategic Operations & Engagement team.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement and organizational effectiveness by implementing approved process improvements, supporting assessment and reporting activities, exploring new technologies and tools, and identifying opportunities to strengthen administrative processes and workflows.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 2+ years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Background in supervising, scheduling, training, or coordinating student employees, part-time staff, or other front-line team members, including supporting their coaching and professional development.
  • Familiarity with higher education or a similarly complex, service-oriented organization, with a background in customer service delivery.
  • Experience developing or maintaining operational documentation such as standard operating procedures (SOPs), training materials, service guides, or scheduling systems.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while exercising sound judgment and maintaining follow-through with minimal supervision.
  • Proficiency in computer applications and digital tools relevant to administrative operations, with effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience with crisis response, de-escalation, or time-sensitive decision-making in a fast-paced, operational environment.
  • Interest in exploring and applying new technologies — including AI-enabled tools — to improve workflows, streamline processes, and enhance operational efficiency.

Job.JobTitle: Professor and Director, School of Communication Sciences and Disorders
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The School of Communication Sciences and Disorders (CSD) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for a 12-month, tenured professor to serve as school director. The position is located at the UCF main campus with an anticipated start date in August 2027.


The successful candidate will assume leadership of a school with a growing team of internationally recognized faculty engaged in rigorous graduate and undergraduate education, expansive clinical service-delivery, cutting-edge research, and innovative partnerships. Opportunities for innovation and expansion abound in the interprofessional context of the College of Health Professions and Sciences within UCF's Academic Health Sciences Center. The selected candidate will provide academic and administrative leadership (i.e., management of human resources, implementation of a new budget model, academic and clinical programming, student success and research excellence); facilitate intra- and inter- school collaborations to enhance the impact of scholarship, teaching, and service; support and mentor faculty to secure external funding; and advance impactful programming to fulfill the healthcare needs of the community.


The School of Communication Sciences and Disorders was founded in 1969 and was first accredited in 1987. It has a strong history of excellence in teaching, research, and community service. The school includes 34 full-time faculty members serving an average of 175 graduate and 500 undergraduate students. It offers bachelor's, master's, and Ph.D. degrees in communication sciences and disorders and ranks among the top 15% of speech-language pathology programs in the nation. The Master of Arts program boasts numerous internal and external affiliations, and the UCF Communication Disorders Clinic serves as the centerpiece for clinical education and applied research. This 15,000+ square foot state-of-the-art facility houses several research labs and specialty services, including audiology, the Aphasia House, the AAC Lab / Florida Alliance for Assistive Services and Technology (FAAST) Center, the Communication Technologies Research Collaborative, the Communication, Aphasia Recovery, and Emotion (CARE) Lab, Early Language & Literacy Intervention & Education Lab, Examining Patient-Provider Language and Interactions in Healthcare (EXPLAIN) Lab. For more information about the school, visit our website at: UCF School of Communication Sciences and Disorders - College of Health Professions and Sciences


Along with the School of Communication Sciences and Disorders, the College of Health Professions and Sciences at UCF is home to the School of Health Sciences, the School of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Sciences, the School of Global Health Management and Informatics, and the School of Social Work. The college also houses several labs and research collaboratives, including the CHPS Rehabilitation Innovation Center – a state-of-the art interdisciplinary facility designed to become a destination center for solving complex healthcare problems through allied healthcare research, education, technology development/applications, and collaboration. UCF and its 12 colleges provide opportunities to more than 69,000 students offering 240+ bachelor's, master's, doctoral, and specialist degree programs.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • A research doctoral degree in communication sciences and disorders or a related discipline from an accredited institution;
  • To be eligible for appointment as a tenured professor upon hire, the selected candidate must have a record of teaching, research/scholarly achievements, and service commensurate with a tenured faculty appointment at the rank of professor in the School of Communication Sciences and Disorders at UCF;
  • A record of administrative leadership and mentoring in a university setting.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Effective communication skills;
  • Experience overseeing complex budgets;
  • Experience with program accreditation;
  • Experience with student recruitment for undergraduate and graduate programs;
  • A record of federally funded research & mentoring faculty in securing external funding;
  • Experience with interprofessional education;
  • A record of facilitating successful collaborations within and outside the university setting;
  • Experience with alumni engagement; and
  • Experience with curriculum revisions and launching new educational programs.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.
  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.


Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr. Shawn Lawrence at Shawn.Lawrence@ucf.edu.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

Note to applicants: Please keep in mind that a job posted without an end date may close at any time without notice. As such, we encourage you to submit your application and all required documentation as quickly as possible to ensure consideration for the posted position.

Are you ready to unleash YOUR potential?

As a next-generation public research university and Forbes-ranked top employer in Florida, we are a community of thinkers, doers, creators, innovators, healers, and leaders striving to create broader prosperity and help shape a better future. No matter what your role is, when you join Knight Nation, you'll play an integral role at one of the most impactful universities in the country. You'll be met with opportunities to connect and collaborate with talented faculty, staff, and students across 13 colleges and multiple campuses, engaging in impactful work that makes a positive difference. Your time at UCF will provide you with many meaningful opportunities to grow, you'll work alongside talented colleagues on complex projects that will challenge you and help you gain new skills and you'll have countless rewarding experiences that go well beyond a paycheck.

Working at UCF has its perks! UCF offers:

  • Benefit packages, including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Flexible Spending, and Employee Assistance Program.
  • Paid time off, including annual (12-month faculty) and sick time off and paid holidays.
  • Retirement savings options.
  • Employee discounts, including tickets to many Orlando attractions.
  • Education assistance.
  • Flexible work environment.
  • And more…For more benefits information, view the UCF Employee Benefits Guide click here.

Unless explicitly stated on the job posting, it is UCF's expectation that an employee of UCF will reside in Florida as of the date the employment begins.

Additional Requirements related to Research Positions:

Pursuant to Florida State Statute 1010.35, prior to offering employment to certain individuals in research-related positions, UCF is required to conduct additional screening. Applicants subject to additional screening include any citizen of a foreign country who is not a permanent resident of the U.S., or who is a citizen or permanent resident but is affiliated with or has had at least 1 year of education, employment, or training in China, Cuba, Iran, Russia, North Korea, Syria, or Venezuela.


The additional screening requirements only apply to research-related positions, including, but not limited to faculty, graduate positions, individuals compensated by research grants or contract funds, post-doctoral positions, undergraduate positions, visiting assistant professors, and visiting research associates.

Position Summary

Our Deloitte Cyber team understands the unique challenges and opportunities businesses face in cybersecurity. Join our team to deliver powerful solutions to help our clients navigate the ever-changing threat landscape. Through powerful solutions and managed services that simplify complexity, we enable our clients to operate with resilience, grow with confidence, and proactively manage to secure success.

Recruiting for this role ends on 12/31/2026.

  • Supporting the design and implementation of Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) solutions aligned to client digital transformation and security objectives.
  • Participating in end-to-end CIAM engagements, including requirements gathering, current-state assessment, solution design, testing, deployment, and production support.
  • Configuring and supporting CIAM capabilities across platforms such as Transmit Security, Ping Federate, Okta, and ForgeRock, including authentication, federation, registration, multi-factor authentication, adaptive access, and customer identity lifecycle processes.

Enables trust and safety of online communications and digital products, protecting users, consumers, and patients from harm. Enables clients to provide consumer confidence in knowing with whom they are dealing and ensuring the integrity of access to data.

Required:

  • BA/BS Degree in Computer Science, Cyber Security, Information Security, Engineering, Information Technology, Finance, Business, or relevant fields
  • 2+ years of industry experience
  • 1+ years hands-on experience working on IAM core concepts such as OAuth 2.0, Authentication & Authorization, API Security, API Gateways, System Integrations, Security Requirements
  • Ability to travel 25-50%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve

Preferred:

  • Certifications such as: Ping Identity/Transmit Security certifications, CISSP, CISM, or CISA certification a plus
  • Design, develop, and implement secure and scalable solutions to support our Customer identity and access management (CIAM) infrastructure.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Physician / Medical Director, Healthcare, Adjunct / Professor
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The University of Central Florida College of Medicine (UCF COM) is seeking an experienced psychiatrist at the rank of assistant, associate, or professor of medicine to have a significant teaching role in undergraduate medical education (UME), graduate medical education (GME), and provide direct, outpatient psychiatric care at UCF Health Faculty Practice. This position is a non-tenure track appointment.


College of Medicine Educational Programs (60-70%)

The successful applicant will teach psychopathology, psychopharmacology, and fundamentals of medical interviewing in an integrated format to first- and second-year medical students and participate in case directed learning sessions. This position will serve as the discipline lead for the Integrated Sciences 4 module, which focuses on pre-clinical psychiatry and neurology. Additionally, teaching psychiatry didactics in the 3rd year clerkship, assisting with mid-clerkship evaluations, and teaching and mentorship in the psychiatry residency program will be required. Collaborations with both basic science and clinical faculty to integrate and reinforce psychiatry concepts throughout the M.D. program curriculum is an essential element of this role. All faculty are expected to pursue scholarly activities to fulfill the criteria for academic advancement. General and specialty-trained psychiatrists with an interest in medical education are encouraged to apply.

The College of Medicine aspires to become an extraordinary research-based institution training physicians of the future who will become exemplary clinicians, leaders in medicine, scholars in science, innovators in medical technology and compassionate providers of health care.


Clinical Responsibilities (30-40%)

Psychiatric medical care will be provided at UCF Health Faculty Practice, an expanding adult outpatient multi-specialty clinic. The successful candidate will provide care in a team that embraces other health care disciplines and involves collaborating with physicians and advanced practice practitioners from a variety of specialties including Primary Care, Rheumatology, Endocrinology, Dermatology, Cardiology, and Ophthalmology.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Candidates must hold an M.D./D.O. from an accredited institution. Candidates must be eligible for licensure or licensed to practice in the state of Florida. Must be board certified or board eligible by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology upon completion of training. Board certification would be expected within two (2) years of completion of training.
  • The candidate's scholarly background and experience must be commensurate with the faculty rank for which the application is submitted.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience teaching medical students and/or residents in an LCME/ACGME accredited program.
  • Commitment to student-centered, active learning in a multidisciplinary environment that integrates basic sciences with clinical application.
  • Proficiency with instructional technology and digital platforms.
  • Track record of scholarly activity.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.
  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Job.JobTitle: Postdoctoral Research Associate in Large Nonlinear Computational Dynamical Systems
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

CREOL (Center for Research and Education in Optics and Lasers) is one of the world's foremost institutions for research and education in optical and photonic science and engineering. The College offers MS and PhD degrees in optics and photonics, and a BS degree in photonic science and engineering. The faculty engages in fundamental and applied research and education in lasers, optical fibers, semiconductor and integrated photonic devices, nonlinear and quantum optics, imaging, sensing, and displays. The college is home to the CREOL, Florida Photonics Center of Excellence (FPCE), and Townes Laser Institute (TLI), and the Institute for the Frontier of Attosecond Science and Technology (iFAST). In addition, the College of Medicine, which includes the Burnett School of Biomedical Sciences, provides rich opportunities for collaboration. For more information see www.creol.ucf.edu.

Applications are invited for a postdoctoral research position in computational nonlinear dynamics and large-scale numerical modeling of semiconductor laser arrays at the College of Optics and Photonics (CREOL), University of Central Florida. Our research program investigates collective dynamics, synchronization, and self-organization in large arrays of coupled semiconductor diode lasers. The work combines experiments with computational and theoretical modeling of nonlinear dynamical systems with time-delayed interactions.


A major objective of this position is to develop and implement efficient numerical methods for increasingly large and complex systems of coupled nonlinear delay-differential equations (DDEs). Models range from arrays of single-mode semiconductor lasers described by Lang–Kobayashi-type equations to substantially larger multimode systems incorporating multiple optical modes, carrier dynamics, nonlinear interactions, heterogeneity, and delayed nonlocal coupling. As the number of lasers and optical modes increases, direct numerical simulation becomes computationally demanding. The successful candidate will therefore focus not only on physical modeling but also on developing, optimizing, and accelerating computational approaches capable of treating large laser networks efficiently.


The postdoctoral associate researcher will contribute to several areas, including:

  • Numerical integration of large systems of nonlinear delay-differential equations
  • Modeling of single-mode and multimode semiconductor laser arrays
  • Optimization and acceleration of existing simulation codes
  • Parallel computing and high-performance computing (HPC)
  • GPU acceleration, where appropriate
  • Development of scalable numerical algorithms for systems containing large numbers of lasers and optical modes

An important component of the project will be determining how numerical algorithms and existing stimulation codes can be redesigned or optimized to achieve substantial improvements in computational speed while preserving numerical accuracy and stability. The position provides an opportunity to work at the intersection of computational mathematics, nonlinear dynamics, high-performance computing, and experimental photonics. The research is closely connected with ongoing experiments involving large semiconductor diode laser arrays. This interaction provides an unusual opportunity for computational researchers to test theoretical and numerical predictions against experimentally observed collective dynamics. This position allows for opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration involving researchers in optics, photonics, nonlinear dynamics, applied mathematics, and computational science.


Semiconductor-laser experience is not required. The successful candidate will work closely with experimental researchers, and the necessary background in semiconductor laser physics and external-cavity laser systems can be developed as part of the project.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. from an accredited institution in Applied Mathematics, Computational Mathematics, Computational Science, Physics, Optical Science, Electrical Engineering or a closely related discipline.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong experience in one or more of the following:
    • Numerical methods for ordinary and delay-differential equations.
    • Scientific computing and numerical analysis
    • Large-scale dynamical systems
    • High-performance computing
    • Parallel numerical algorithms
    • GPU computing
  • Strong programming skills are very important.
  • Experience with C/C++, Python, Julia, MATLAB, CUDA, or a comparable scientific-computing environment is desirable.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.
  • Brief statement of research interests and relevant experimental experience.
  • A list of publications
  • List of three professional references with contact information

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr. Yehuda Braiman at yehuda.braiman@ucf.edu.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

This is a Contract & Grants (C&G) funded position. Employment is subject to availability of funding and may cease at the time funding for this employment is depleted.

The position is anticipated for at least two years, with continued appointment and possible extension subject to satisfactory performance and availability of funding (up to a total of four years).
